Read our Privacy notice

A 24-year-old man has been sentenced after approaching several young girls to touch and sniff their feet.

Alexander Scott-Bowen, of Kingswood, South Gloucestershire, was sentenced at Bristol Crown Court on Friday after pleading guilty to seven counts of sexual assault against seven victims.

He was sentenced to 38 weeks in prison, but has been released after serving his custody period on remand this year. A 10-year Sexual Harm Prevention Order was also granted, and he has been added to the Sex Offenders' Register for the next decade.

Scott-Bowen would engage all of his victims in an innocuous conversation about their feet or shoes, often paying them compliments, before swiftly grabbing their foot and sniffing it, Avon and Somerset Police said.

Detective Mike Coleman said: “These attacks caused considerable distress to the victims and the wider community and we are pleased Scott-Bowen has been sentenced for these crimes.

“Throughout this investigation, we were clear in our mindset to view these incidents for what they really were - a series of sexual attacks against predominantly young girls.”

open image in gallery Scott-Bowen was sentenced at Bristol Crown Court on Friday (Ben Birchall/PA) ( PA Archive )

Mr Coleman added: “Scott-Bowen carried out his offending over a long period of time and was not even deterred by being arrested and released with bail conditions, as he went on to commit further offences.

“In pleading guilty in the face of the substantial evidence presented, he has accepted that his motives for all these attacks was his own sexual gratification.”

The force launched an investigation in 2022 after receiving reports of three young girls being separately approached by a man in Yate who touched and sniffed their feet.

Police received two more reports of young girls being stopped in Kingswood in similar circumstances in March 2025, and another investigation led officers to identify Scott-Bowen as a suspect.

He was arrested, interviewed, and bailed while the force continued to carry out its enquiries and gather evidence.

His DNA was also obtained and had been found and matched to DNA on the shoelace of one of the victims in 2022.

Police then received further reports regarding two girls being approached in Cribbs Causeway on New Year's Eve last year in a similar manner and a woman being approached in Stoke Gifford in January while Scott-Bowen was on bail.

He was re-arrested three days after these incidents and remanded into custody. During a forensic examination, material indicative of a foot fetish was located on his phone, police said.

Mr Coleman added: “We want to thank and recognise the brave victims who came forward, especially those from the 2022 incident who all positively re-engage when we contact them to inform them their cases were being re-opened.”

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

News.title: Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon
News.content:
The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

News.title: Wall Street hit by tech sell-off after AI bosses push for slowdown
News.content:
Donald Trump has attacked what he calls a “sick conspiracy” against AI after the head of Anthropic called for a slowdown in the technology’s development.

The US president warned that China would benefit after the bosses of Silicon Valley’s top AI companies backed calls to restrict AI development for safety reasons, calling the concerns a “hoax”.

He also launched a tirade against Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, whom he accused of trying to be a “perfect little angel”.

Mr Trump wrote on Truth Social: “The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so!

“We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies!

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China.”

Mr Amodei released a letter at the weekend calling for an industry-wide slowdown, endorsed by the US government, to prevent safety issues going “seriously wrong”.

In response, Mr Trump wrote: “Concerning AI, when, in the history of business, did anyone see the leaders of an industry call for regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy.

“AI taking over the world, destroying humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX.”

JD Vance, the US vice-president, echoed Mr Trump’s comments, calling tech leaders’ requests a “Trojan horse”.

He added: “I have to say, just personally, I feel a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them.

“It feels a little bit to me like a bit of a Trojan horse.”

OpenAI has since called on the UK Government to introduce mandatory safety rules for major AI developers.

Under proposals supported by the company, the UK’s AI Security Institute would play a central role in third-party testing and creating adaptive technical standards.

Tom Duff-Gordon, the company’s head of policy in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, told Politico: “OpenAI is in a position to support legislation in the UK to establish durable, mandatory, capability-based requirements for frontier AI that would build on the set of voluntary commitments that we currently have.”

Under the plans, Britain would move from the current system of voluntary agreements with AI companies to enforceable standards, bringing the UK in line with emerging frameworks in the EU and US.

The Government has not yet put forward plans for AI safety legislation, despite pressure from backbench MPs.

US tech stocks fell sharply on Wall Street after AI bosses called for a slowdown, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping by as much as 1.3pc.

Nvidia, the world’s largest listed company and a manufacturer of semiconductors used in the AI race, plunged by 4.2pc while fellow chipmaker AMD dropped 6.2pc.

The main European indexes in France, Germany and Spain were all down sharply on Monday after falls in South Korea and Japan overnight.

News.title: The best boutique hotels in Madrid
News.content:
In Madrid, choosing a boutique hotel gives you the chance to stay in some of the Spanish capital’s most elegant buildings, with smart design and often palatial levels of grandeur. This is a particularly noisy and frantic city, but as soon as you step inside these calm havens, you can relax and get yourself ready for more urban adventures. The people on reception and behind the bar have more time to chat and are usually more than willing to spill their secrets on favourite bars, restaurants and shops.

Although these places are smaller than the chain hotels, they often have spectacular roof terraces as well as attractive spas and great restaurants. This is also an opportunity to stay in some of the smartest neighbourhoods, such as Salesas and Salamanca, where you might find yourself fantasising about living in Madrid as you drift around the boutiques and bakeries near your hotel. Here's our pick of the best boutique hotels in Madrid.

News.title: 50 of the most family-friendly hotels in France
News.content:
La belle France promises endless family escapades – by the sea or sand dunes, overlooking horse-ploughed vines or atop a mountain or a clifftop. Natural green space for children of all ages to let off steam is in abundance pretty much all over the hexagon, and as French hoteliers refine their services and facilities to make stays more eco-conscious, there’s never been a greener and more exhilarating choice of places to stay en famille. Château, chalet, hôtel particular (historic mansion), upcycled oil mill or belle epoque seaside villa: all budgets are embraced with signature French panache.

Sophisticated city hotels and resorts entertain with action-packed kids’ clubs, themed treasure hunts, outdoor activities and hands-on workshops like patisserie classes, grape-picking and cheese-making. Mid-range hotels pamper young explorers with traditional games, kitchen-garden visits and old-fashioned fun en plein air. Away from towns and cities, hotels increasingly offer flexible self-catering packages too – a cottage positioned on a rambling estate perhaps – allowing families to mix-and-match hotel dining with their own, memorable market-sourced feasts.

Located in Paris, Provence or pinprick hamlets you’ve probably never heard of: here are 50 of the best family-friendly hotels in France.

News.title: Asia on high alert as El Niño threatens new Dengue epidemic
News.content:
Countries from Brazil to Taiwan are bracing for a surge in dengue driven by the “supersized” El Niño, as the UN warns this year’s weather phenomenon could be the strongest on record.

Both the virus and the Aedes mosquitoes that transmit it are especially sensitive to heat – and the El Niño is expected to push global temperatures to new highs.

“El Niño is being supersized before our eyes,” Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary General, said last week. “The ​science leaves no room for doubt: the planet is in uncharted waters, and those waters are heating up.”

The weather phenomenon – a periodic warming of sea surface temperature in the eastern Pacific, caused by weakening trade winds – alters rainfall and temperature patterns across the globe. That, in turn, causes extreme weather like droughts, heatwaves, floods and typhoons – which then trigger events including wildfires, crop failures and a collapse in affected fisheries.

But it can also have a major impact on the transmission of disease, including dengue – and countries across the world, especially in Asia and Latin America, are bracing for outbreaks.

In July, Brazil’s Ministry of Health sent an alert warning states that arboviruses like dengue, chikungunya and Zika could surge later this year, and urged officials to ramp up disease surveillance and mosquito control programmes.

The increase will likely peak in 2027: the biomedical research institute Fiocruz has estimated that Brazil will see 1.7 million dengue cases next year, driven by El Niño.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick issues Carlos Baleba injury update as wait goes on for £70million star to make his Man Utd debut
Sports.content:
CARLOS BALEBA is set to make his Manchester United debut after the international break.

Baleba, who has been sidelined since sustaining an ankle injury in a friendly for Brighton on July 18, began outdoor training this week.



The £70million summer signing has not had a single team training session with his team-mates, which all but rules him out of this week’s games against his former club and at Fulham.

United head coach Michael Carrick said in late August that Baleba would be available in “a couple or three weeks” but the club are preparing for him to be ready for the visit of Tottenham on October 10.



When asked if Baleba will be available after the three-week international break, Carrick replied: “Yeah, he definitely will be.

“He’ll be back in and around the group at some point over the next week or so, so that means after internationals he should be in good shape.



“Carlos came being injured and then he’s desperate to get out there and be part of the group and training fully with the boys.

“I’ve said before, obviously, he’s a quality player, that’s why we bought him. And he balances off the dynamics of the midfield particularly well.”

There is no timeframe on the returns of Amad, who sustained an injury on the eve of the season opener against Hull City, or Matthijs de Ligt, sidelined since November 30 with a back problem.

Luke Shaw could be available for the League Cup third round tie against Brighton, having missed last week’s games against Sabah and Manchester City. If Shaw is not risked, Carrick expects him to be back at Craven Cottage on Sunday.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Shaw’s substitution with United 2-1 up at Everton and absence against City were costly, with his full back replacements Noussair Mazraoui and Patrick Dorgu culpable for the decisive goals United conceded.

Carrick billed Dorgu as “like a new signing” after he missed three months last term with a hamstring injury, but the Denmark international did not convince at left back last week.

“Pat played fantastically well the other night and I thought he did a lot of good things [against City], to be honest,” Carrick added.

“That’s why we’ve got the squad, to fill in different things. Injuries aren’t ideal, but we’ve got to deal with them.”

United have won two trophies in nine years and went out of both domestic cup competitions at the first hurdle last season.



Carrick played in two League Cup final triumphs with United under Sir Alex Ferguson in 2010 and Jose Mourinho in 2017.

“For me, trophies are the beauty and the feeling of winning,” Carrick said. “It’s what we’re in football for, what we’re in sport for, and certainly what I’m at this club for is to try and win.

“It’s not straightforward and you decide you want to win and you go and win. But it’s important.

“And I think trophies and achieving things and giving supporters that feeling of the emotion of that is important, definitely.”



Carrick also backed the United players to respond positively to the derby defeat. The Pro Ref organisation admitted a “judgement of error” for Erling Haaland’s controversial winner but Carrick was widely criticised for his game management after Phil Foden’s 23rd-minute red card.

On the three occasions United have lost under Carrick, they have won their following fixture.

“We’ve got to move on,” Carrick stressed. “We’ve still got to look at it for ourselves, and we’ve got to win games. We’ve won a lot of games, and we need to continue to do that.

“I understand it’s a new season, it’s a fresh season, and the points tally right now is not what we want it to be. I’m not hiding from that.

“But it’s more of winning games, getting that feeling, getting the habit. It’s easier said than done, of course it is, but we’re capable of it.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The players have got an edge. I think they’ve shown that to me since I’ve been here. We’ve had setbacks, and they’ve bounced back particularly well and had some really good performances and good results.

“So they’ve got an edge. It does give you something when something like that happens [against City] to use moving forward.”

Sports.title: England vs Spain – Nations League tickets: Where can I buy them and how much do they cost?
Sports.content:
ENGLAND face Spain in a mouthwatering Nations League match – and fans are desperate to get tickets for the showpiece game.

The Three Lions suffered heartbreak at yet another major tournament this summer.

Thomas Tuchel’s men got dumped out at the semi-final stage of the World Cup 2026 by Argentina despite taking the lead through Anthony Gordon.



But now all attention turns to the Nations League, and England will be hoping they can get their group campaign off to the best possible start.



However, the Three Lions couldn’t have been given a tougher test as they face World Cup winners Spain.

And you can be there in person watching it all unfold but you have to be quick as tickets are flying off the shelf.

Where to buy tickets for the England vs Spain

Ticombo still have tickets available for the huge match at Wembley in September.

England, Spain and neutral fans can still grab their spot inside the iconic Wembley stadium.

Season ticket holders usually get priority and supporters who have been several matches before, so your best chance to get a ticket may be through a third party.

The prices are often more than face value, but for fans who do not qualify, it is often the best option.

Where to watch England vs Spain without a ticket

England’s Nations League match against Spain will take place on Saturday, September 26.

Kick-off is set for 7:45pm BST.

Fans can watch the Nations League encounter live on ITV 1.

It was also be streamed live on ITV X.

Alternatively, you can follow live updates of the match through SunSport‘s live blog.

Sports.title: Shooting at amateur football match leaves one dead and six injured as gunmen ride up touchline and open fire
Sports.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FOOTBALL HORROR Shooting at amateur football match leaves one dead and six injured as gunmen ride up touchline and open fire

A MAN has been killed and six others wounded after gunmen opened fire during an amateur football match.

The attackers drove up to the touchline on a motorbike and fired shots into a crowd of people.



Players and spectators scattered as a witness captured the gunfire on their phone.

The shooting happened in the city of San Francisco del Rincón in Guanajuato State, Mexico, at about 2.40pm on Sunday.



Seven people were hit and six remain in hospital, NeedToKnow reports.

One victim later died in hospital after relatives drove the wounded away themselves.

The deceased was identified as 25-year-old food vendor Julio César.

Two of the wounded were named as Israel, 25, and Christian Antonio.

A municipal officer at the scene said the gunmen appeared to target “two people” and that “others ran so there were collateral victims”.

The Guanajuato state prosecutor’s office has opened a murder file and is hunting the gunmen.



The city council said they would help the injured and their families and work with investigators.

Gunmen have struck amateur matches in the state before, including a massacre in Salamanca in January that left 11 dead.

The investigation continues.

Sports.title: Inside Oasis star Noel Gallagher’s love affair with football, from Man City party to Wonderwall becoming England anthem
Sports.content:
NOEL GALLAGHER has long been one of Manchester City’s most famous supporters, and few things sum up his love for the club better than joining the players in a dressing-room rendition of Wonderwall.

The Oasis legend was invited into the City dressing room after their stunning 2018/19 title triumph.



Pep Guardiola‘s side had beaten Liverpool to the Premier League crown by just a single point, finishing on 98 points to the Reds’ 97.

After beating Brighton 4-1 at the Amex Stadium on the final day, the players celebrated their back-to-back league titles in style with Gallagher right in the middle of it.



The City-mad rocker joined the squad as they belted out Oasis classic Wonderwall, before joining in himself as the dressing-room party continued.

It was a fitting soundtrack given the song’s status as one of the biggest anthems in British football.



Gallagher has never been shy about celebrating City’s success.

The 59-year-old was back in the stands for Sunday’s Manchester derby as City beat Manchester United 1-0 thanks to Erling Haaland‘s controversial winner.

The cameras repeatedly picked Gallagher out during the dramatic goal controversy, including when Haaland‘s strike initially appeared to have been ruled out.

Gary Neville couldn’t resist the perfect Oasis reference, telling viewers: “Don’t Look Back In Anger.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Gallagher reflected on the experience of going to Old Trafford with his two sons.

He told talkSPORT: “Ordinarily I wouldn’t [go]. I don’t like going to Old Trafford because it can get a bit spicy getting in and out, but they were there.

“They were so keen to go because they’d never been, so I went for them really and they got stuck into it big time and it was a great, great day.”



“There comes a point in your time as a father where you look at your children and you think, ‘My god, I brought you up well’ – when they feel it as much as you do and when they get it.

“Let’s not forget, when you’re in that away end and the United fans are in front of you, they’re giving it to you as much as you’re giving it to them.

“But he made the newspapers today and my heart is full of pride for my sons who got stuck into it yesterday and got stuck into the United fans as well.”

Gallagher’s relationship with City has long gone far beyond simply turning up for matches.

He has celebrated title wins with the players, goes to games regularly, and was even part of TNT Sports‘ commentary team for Manchester City‘s 4-1 defeat against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League in November 2024 alongside Darren Fletcher and Ally McCoist.



As for Oasis, the iconic Manchester band are set to be in the limelight again in 2027 following their world tour last year – when the Gallagher brothers re-united to play concerts again for the first time in 16 years.

Next summer, the Etihad is among the venues where they will play.

Oasis will perform an incredible 11 dates at City’s home, alongside shows at some of Europe’s biggest football stadiums.



Those include Celtic Park, Bayern Munich‘s Allianz Arena, Barcelona‘s Olympic Stadium, the Stade de France (which hosted the 2022 Champions League final), Rome’s Stadio Olimpico, and Ajax’s Johan Cruyff Arena.

It is another reminder of how closely Oasis have become intertwined with football culture.

And this summer, their influence stretched beyond club football.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Wonderwall was adopted as England‘s World Cup anthem, giving the iconic Oasis track another lease of life as supporters followed the Three Lions.

At the end of every game England won, they would sing the famous anthem in front of their fans.

Sports.title: Ligue 1 side Lens brutally sack manager Dino Toppmoller after just four games having replaced new Premier League boss
Sports.content:
LENS have reportedly sacked manager Dino Toppmoller just four league games into the season.

The German tactician, 45, joined the Ligue 1 outfit in June, replacing Pierre Sage after he joined Crystal Palace.



But now it appears he will have to find a new club on short notice after L’Equipe reported he was set to be let go.

Lens were desperate to build on Sage’s success in the role after he led the side to a Coupe de France trophy and a second-place finish in the French top tier, earning them Champions League football for this campaign.



And Toppmoller’s quest to repeat the feat got off to a dream start as Lens stunned Paris Saint-Germain in the Trophee des Champions in his very first official match in charge.

He followed it up with an even more emphatic win as his side thumped Auxerre 5-2 in their first game of the Ligue 1 season.



But those games proved to be the highlight of his time with the club, as results quickly took a turn for the worse.

Their next match was a 2-1 loss to Strasbourg, before Lorient shocked them 1-0 at home.

Patience would have been at a low when Slavia Prague tucked home what they thought was an 88th-minute winner in their Champions League clash last week.

But Toppmoller’s men fired back with goals in the first and third minutes of injury time to somehow turn the fixture around at the death.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The feel-good factor lasted just a couple of days, however, drawing that weekend to newly promoted Le Mans.

With the side well off the pace of their Champions League aspirations in 10th, it seems the hierarchy has decided to pull the trigger on a managerial shake-up.

Sports.title: Former Prem stars still playing abroad that you forgot about including Man Utd hero, infamous striker and 45-year-old
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE stars can quickly go from being household names to yesterday’s news in the blink of an eye.

Football is a fast-moving sport and the stars we once adored are often quickly forgotten about.



Philippe Coutinho, 34, is a prime example after news he had joined Brazilian side Santos to play alongside Neymar.

Most fans likely didn’t realise he was still playing football after recent spells with Al-Duhail and Vasco da Gama.



He had spent seven months unemployed beforehand after Vasco ripped up his contract in February.

There are a number of other veteran stars playing abroad who haven’t featured in the Prem for years.



SunSport breaks down a list of footballers who you might have forgotten about who are still playing overseas.

Roque Santa Cruz, 45, Nacional (Paraguay)

Starting with perhaps the most surprising entry, the former Man City and Blackburn star is STILL playing in the Paraguayan top flight.

The forward turned 45 last month but is still going strong with Nacional in his native Paraguay.

Santa Cruz – who also played for Real Betis and Malaga – has netted four goals from 19 appearances this season to continue his incredible longevity.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Mario Balotelli, 36, Al-Ittifaq (Dubai)

A long way from the days of “Why always me?”, the former Italy international is now living a much more quiet life in the Middle East.

Balotelli has spent the last two seasons with UAE outfit Al-Ittifaq and netted six goals last term.

He has become something of a journeyman striker in recent years after spells with Brescia, Monza, Sion, Genoa and Turkish outfit Adana Demirspor.



Shinji Kagawa, 37, Cerezo Osaka (Japan)

Manchester United fans will remember the Japanese playmaker Kagawa after he signed in a £12m deal from Borussia Dortmund in 2012.

But he struggled to dazzle under Sir Alex Ferguson and later David Moyes, before returning to the Bundesliga club in 2014.

The Japan international ended up playing for PAOK in Greece and Sint-Triuden in Belgium before joining current side Cerezo Osaka in his home country.



Nani, 39, Aktobe (Kazakhstan)

Yes, Nani is still playing football and I’m just as surprised as you are.

The ex-United star who won four Prem titles and the Champions League is now plying his trade in Kazakhstan of all places.

He initially retired in 2024 after a spell with Portuguese side Estrela Amadora before making a U-turn and signing for Aktobe in January.

Nani has since made 14 appearances for the club, scoring twice.



Christian Benteke, 35, Al-Wahda (Dubai)

Another former Prem striker playing his football in the UAE.

At his peak, Benteke banged in 19 goals for Aston Villa in the 2012-13 season and netted a total of 49 goals in 101 appearances.

That form earned him a £32.5m move to Liverpool, but the move didn’t work out and he went on to star for Crystal Palace for six years.

Benteke then had four years with MLS side DC United where he was a goal machine before joining Al-Wahda last year.



Gary Medel, 39, Universidad Catolica (Chile)

Remember the tough-tackling former Cardiff City star who spent one season with the Welsh club?

The Chile legend played 35 times for the Bluebirds in 2013-14 under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer but couldn’t prevent their relegation.

He then played for Inter Milan for three years and also had spells with Besiktas, Bologna and Vasco da Gama.

Medel – who has 161 caps for Chile – joined Catolica in his hometown last year.



Teemu Pukki, 36, HJK (Finland)

The former Norwich City hitman has returned to Finnish side HJK, the team he last played for in 2011.

Pukki made a name for himself during his two-decades-long career and became known for his deadly ability in front of goal.

English football fans will recall that killer instinct during his time at Carrow Road, where he scored 88 times in 210 appearances.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Those goals earned Norwich two promotions and he departed as a beloved figure at the club.



He spent two years with MLS side Minnesota United before joining HSK in 2025.

Sports.title: Daniel Farke and Leeds leading charge of clubs who can upset Premier League old guard
Sports.content:
Daniel Farke and Leeds leading charge of clubs who can upset Premier League old guard

There are signs that the traditional order in the English top flight could be dismantled as Leeds United sit in third in the table and have Hull City and Brighton directly below

View 3 Images Daniel Farke has enjoyed Leeds' start to the Premier League season (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

For those keeping a close eye on Daniel Farke in the immediate aftermath of a wonderful win over Newcastle United, it will come as no surprise to find the German is one of Pep Guardiola’s closer managerial friends.

‌



And Farke is also one of Guardiola’s multitude of disciples, which might explain why he was frowning over and talking about a late error rather than instantly celebrating what felt like a landmark victory.

‌



It was quintessential Pep. Leeds United’s performance in the rout of Newcastle was one that Guardiola would have admired, that is for sure.

‌



And he will be pleased that Farke can enjoy some time in the limelight. Leeds sit third in the table ahead of a home game against Crystal Palace on Sunday.

There is every chance they will stay in that position when the Premier League breaks for an international window. The table is, of course, in its very formative stages.

If you need reminding of the folly of reading too much into an early-season table, Spurs were third at this stage of last season. But you cannot deny that the presence of Leeds, Hull and Brighton in third, fourth and fifth places respectively is eye-catching. As are their performances.

‌



Between them, they scored eleven goals in the last round of fixtures. Hull contributed only two, but those two were at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds and Hull are undefeated while Brighton’s only loss came at Chelsea, where they were beaten 4-3 despite enjoying over 74 percent possession and looking the better team for long periods of the contest. Brighton’s manager, Fabian Hurzeler, now has more than two years of Premier League experience.

View 3 Images Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic has made a great start to life in the Premier League

‌



Farke is in his fifth season as a Premier League manager, although one of them was curtailed when he was sacked by Norwich in November, 2021. They are both well aware of the demands.

At Hull, Sergej Jakirovic is in his first Premier League season but already has a Manager of the Month award in his locker. It will remain a major challenge for Jakirovic to even keep his side in the top half of the Premier League table but there is no doubt a summer outlay of £150million helped his cause.

Leeds did not spend as much as Hull but James Trafford might well have been the signing of the summer and centre-half Tarik Muharemovic - despite the late mistake against Newcastle that sent Farke into Pep mode - looks a great acquisition. As usual, Brighton made a profit in the transfer window but still reinvested £150million.

‌



These clubs are embracing the challenge. Brighton’s challenge is to continue making their mark, Leeds’ challenge is to improve significantly on last season and Hull’s is to show they are not in the competition to make up the numbers.

View 3 Images Fabian Hurzeler is in his third season in the Premier League (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

And what gives them genuine hope of maintaining their promising starts to the season? Here's what - the fact that below Arsenal and Manchester City, no group looks as though it might separate itself from the rest.

Article continues below

You might think teams such as Liverpool, Manchester United, Aston Villa and even Chelsea could form a second tier but there are absolutely no signs of that happening right now. There are certainly serious reservations about any of those sides being able to mount a sustained title run.

No, it could well develop into a free-for-all below the top two. Again, these are very, very early days. But on the evidence of the opening four rounds of fixtures, Leeds, Hull and Brighton are going to provide plenty of entertainment and intrigue this season.

Sports.title: Man City star's dad left Oasis legend Noel Gallagher with two black eyes after headbutt
Sports.content:
Man City star's dad left Oasis legend Noel Gallagher with two black eyes after headbutt

Oasis star Noel Gallagher was left bloodied after an unfortunate incident at a Manchester City match

View 3 Images Oasis superstar Noel Gallagher is a well-known Manchester City supporter (Image: Getty)

Oasis will tour again in 2027 and the brothers' love for Manchester City is no secret. But the duo – and specifically lead guitarist Noel Gallagher – sometimes really do have to roll with it when watching City in action.

‌



Running from May through September, the Manchester band will once more embark on a stadium tour next summer. It includes UK stops in Glasgow, Manchester and Knebworth, alongside shows across mainland Europe, Ireland and North America.

‌



The 2027 stadium run comes two years after the band officially ended their 15-year hiatus in 2025. Noel had infamously quit in August 2009 following a backstage fallout with Liam, but the brothers put their differences aside for their massive reunion.

‌



Amid all the public bickering, one constant remained: their shared passion for boyhood club City. Their father first took Noel to Maine Road in 1971, Liam soon followed suit and both have remained fanatical supporters ever since.

Man Utd handed new Bruno Fernandes punishment verdict after Man City controversy READ MORE :

But in 2022, as City celebrated winning the Premier League for the fourth time in five years, Noel admitted that things were perhaps taken too far as the father of defender Ruben Dias accidentally headbutted him and he required stitches.

‌



View 3 Images The two brothers were in attendance for last season's FA Cup final (Image: Getty)

In May 2022, City hosted Aston Villa on the final day of the top-flight season, needing a win to beat Liverpool to the title. The visitors took the lead just before half-time and doubled it through Philippe Coutinho in the 70th minute.

Just as it looked like the title could slip away in the unlikeliest of circumstances, the tide turned in double quick fashion. Ilkay Gundogan halved the deficit before Rodri equalised. Gundogan then netted an 81st-minute winner and City retained their crown.

‌



On the Monday following the title win, Noel appeared on talkSPORT and recalled his experiences at the whirlwind of a game. An unfortunate clash with Dias' father led to him being treated by medical staff.

"So as the third goal goes in, right, there is absolute bedlam," he said. "As you can imagine, in the stadium where we sit. Ruben Dias' family are in the box, a couple of boxes up.

"So I'm jumping around like an idiot, passing my 11-year-old son around like the Premier League trophy, everyone is lifting him up and I turn around and Ruben Dias' dad runs straight into me, headbutting me. I'm on the floor, covered in blood. I don't see the last two minutes.

‌



View 3 Images Gundogan scored the winner against Villa as City lifted the title (Image: Getty)

"I've got to get taken down by the St John's Ambulance and had to get stitched up. I've got stitches in my top lip and I've got two black eyes.

"As I'm going down the corridor, Pep's running up crying and we kind of hug each other and he says, 'What's up with your face?' And I was like, 'Go and be with your players, nothing to do with me.'

Article continues below

"I look like I've just arrived home from the eighties at Elland Road. I look like I've had my head smashed in. It's unbelievable. He [Dias' father] is a big bear of a man - he almost knocked my teeth out. But as days go at The Etihad, that's got to be up there with the best."

Noel and brother Liam will be rooting for their beloved City again this season. As part of their 2027 tour, they will play 11 shows at the Etihad Stadium between June 4 and June 26.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel is still bruised and bitter over England World Cup criticism - does he have a point?
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel still feels very hard done by. In fact, it would be fair to say the England manager has been bruised by the whole World Cup 2026 experience. England finished third in the World Cup, their best-ever performance on foreign soil.

So, why are so many England fans still so frustrated, still hurt and why, when looking back upon the summer, do they do it with regret rather than happy memories?

And they do. I struggle to find an England fan who does not feel a sense of “what might have been” after a World Cup which promised so much.

In a poll on the Mirror website and app immediately after England's exit, we asked our readers who was "most to blame" for the defeat.

‌



The majority, 56%, of 2,500 people said Tuchel was to blame; 7% said the players; and more than a third, 37%, answered "both must take the blame".

'Tuchel's sense of annoyance is palpable'

View 4 Images Tuchel's substitutions in the Argentina semi-final defeat were highly criticised after England's World Cup exit (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Tuchel names his next England squad on Friday for the forthcoming Nations League fixtures.

And, by the way, so many football fans have not clocked it. It’s gone unnoticed that there are no Premier League games for the best part of THREE WEEKS.

‌



None from next Sunday until the weekend of October 10 and 11. In between, England play Spain at Wembley, then they have a trip to Czech Republic, Croatia and then back to Wembley to face Czech Republic again. Four games.

On Friday, Tuchel will unveil his squad but also expect some more questions about the World Cup, what happened, what was good and what went wrong.

Now, Tuchel has been a regular face in Premier League boardrooms, in directors’ boxes and on TV screens as he watches games. On Sunday, Tuchel was at Old Trafford for the Manchester derby.

And anyone who has spoken to him at those games - from former managers to ex-players - has got a sense that he feels hard done by. That England did well and he did not deserve so much criticism in the wake of the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

‌



Tuchel is friendly, approachable and enjoys the chat and banter when he goes to clubs to watch players. But people have noticed a sense of annoyance over the way some people still view and remember England’s World Cup campaign.

Tuchel was visibly annoyed when he faced tough questions on the eve of England’s third place play-off with France in Miami in July.

The never-ending 'England DNA' question

View 4 Images Declan Rice with England manager Thomas Tuchel (Image: Javier Garcia/Shutterstock)

‌



The questions were probing and fair about who he thought was to blame. This was not the blame game. But if he gave the team instructions - were the players not following orders.

Tuchel is searingly honest and, immediately after that defeat to Argentina, he talked about England’s DNA and the need to keep the ball better. It was interesting. And a debate and a genuine subject.

There is no way in the world that, after finishing third, Tuchel was going to lose his job. The Football Association feel he did and is doing a fine job. I’m inclined to agree. But he did get it wrong in the semi-final. And those are the games he was brought in for.

His harshest critics - the ones on phone-ins, the shock jocks and social media - disagreed and felt he was entirely to blame for the tactical own goal against Argentina. Many argued he should have lost his job. Thanks very much. Onto the next one.

‌



The more realistic fans just saw it as an opportunity wasted. This was not a classic Argentina team, they were there for the taking, they kept on going on about the Falklands… and England blew their chance.

That is where the frustration comes. Along with Tuchel’s promise to try and put another star on the shirt. Well, he tried. And England came up short.

There’s no doubt about it. England’s last-16 win in Mexico at altitude took it out of the players, with a hangover effect continuing into the quarter and semi-final.

England were then taken to extra time by Norway in the quarters. They did lots more travelling than Argentina. That constant back and forth to Kansas City felt excessive.

‌



By the time they played Argentina, even superhuman Jude Bellingham looked tired. It is so long since England have had a world-class superstar like Bellingham playing at his highest and best level. When will that happen again? He was phenomenal.

Thomas Tuchel's intensive World Cup inquest as FA prepare major report into England failings READ MORE :

'Tuchel must remain open, honest and interesting'

View 4 Images Tuchel addresses the media after England's third place play-off win over France (Image: Carmen Mandato - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Straight afterwards, it felt bizarre that the FA even needed to offer some support for Tuchel - who is under contract until 2028 - and his future. Sadly, by doing so you make it a topic of conversation.

There was clearly some frustration among some players about England’s tactics after Argentina. They did go defensive by going five at the back. Why not stay on the front foot?

‌



But that is why it became a fair question over who was to blame? Tuchel suggested he went five at the back to actually change shape and allow the wing backs to push on while strengthening the centre halves.

So did the players just not follow orders? Maybe Tuchel’s directness raises question marks. We never, ever want a manager to stop being open, honest and interesting. But on occasion, it will raise difficult questions.

That’s the frustration. But it does raise a genuine question: did Tuchel deserve more respect for what England did at the World Cup? And are England genuine contenders for the next Euros?

My view is that Tuchel did do well at the World Cup. Very well. But he probably raised our expectations - and blew a big chance against Argentina. That’s the frustration.

‌



But should it overwhelm the achievement? It’s hard not to argue not because it was such a big opportunity against such a big rival.

His squad will be interesting on Friday. But, actually, what he says and how he moves the agenda forward might be just as compelling.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes insists 'jury is still out' on Senne Lammens in Premier League title claim
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes insists 'jury is still out' on Senne Lammens in Premier League title claim

Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has been discussing what the club need to challenge for titles again - including the prospects of goalkeeper Senne Lammens

View 2 Images Paul Scholes says the jury is still out on Senne Lammens (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside)

Paul Scholes believes only time will tell whether or Senne Lammens is the 'top-class' goalkeeper Manchester United need to become Premier League champions once again.

‌



The Red Devils have not won the domestic crown since the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson stepped down as manager back in 2013, with Michael Carrick now at the helm after guiding the club back into the Champions League following a chastening period.

‌



Carrick's remit after landing the job full-time in the summer is to build on the third-placed finish United achieved last season, though Arsenal and Manchester City more likely to fight it out for the title this time around.

‌



United reshaped their midfield in the summer transfer window in a bid to kick on, though more work needs to be done. Scholes, a treble winner with United back in 1999, is of the opinion that United will attempt to 'sort out' their defence next year as part of the next phase of their rebuild.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Lammens has proved himself to be an upgrade on Andre Onana in goal since joining last summer, but Scholes reckons the jury is still out on whether the Belgian is up to the task of starring for a team with genuine title aspirations.

“I think they’re doing it in sections, that’s what it looks like,” Scholes told The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite.

“They sorted the forwards out last year and the forwards look alight. They still probably need a top class centre-forward, I’m not sure how much confidence they have in Sesko, although I think he has got better.

‌



“It looks like they did the midfield this year and it feels like the defence will probably come next year. At this moment in time, defensively, they’re always going to concede goals in that team.

View 2 Images Scholes says only time will tell if Lammens is good enough to star for a team with serious title aspirations (Image: YouTube/The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast)

“What team have you seen win the Premier League without a top class goalkeeper? Lammens might be that, I don’t know, I think the jury’s probably still out on that. Then you build from the back four.

‌



“The way Arsenal started three or four years ago Defensively they have been absolutely brilliant. You need a top class goalkeeper. You think of Liverpool’s team with Alisson, City’s teams, Raya at Arsenal. Man United with Peter Schmeichel and Edwin van der Sar.

“They’ve all got brilliant, brilliant goalkeepers. You start from the back, of course you do.”

Sports.title: Man Utd handed new Bruno Fernandes punishment verdict after Man City controversy
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed new Bruno Fernandes punishment verdict after Man City controversy

There has been plenty of discussion on the incident between Phil Foden and Bruno Fernandes in the Manchester Derby last weekend

Michael Carrick concerned by Manchester derby goal decision

Bruno Fernandes should have also been sent off after his exchange with Phil Foden, according to Alan Shearer. The Manchester derby began with United midfielder Fernandes being kicked by Foden in the first half.

After Fernandes went down clutching his mid-section, Foden was handed a straight red card. However, the City ace appeared to have been provoked by a petty little kick from Fernandes, who left his foot in while the England international was on the floor.

The United captain did not receive any penalty and City were reduced to ten-men. The Cityzens still went on to win the game through Erling Haaland's controversial late strike.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Nevertheless, Shearer believes Fernandes should have also been dismissed for provoking the incident. Speaking on the Rest is Football podcast, Shearer said: "I thought the way Bruno Fernandes went down was pathetic. He helped get Foden off and, yes, he's kicked out at him a little bit but Bruno Fernandes has also kicked Phil Foden.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes' clash with Phil Foden is still dominating conversation (Image: Zohaib Alam, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"If Phil Foden reacts in the same way as Bruno Fernandes did then both get red cards. So, for me, either both are red or neither of them are.

"He's kicked out, so he's stupid, OK? But Bruno Fernandes has done the same thing so for me, without doubt, they both should've been a red card if Michael Oliver thinks Phil Foden's is a red card."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



City manager Enzo Maresca reached the same conclusion as Shearer. Speaking after the final whistle, he said: "Phil's card is a red card, but I also think the same action is a red card by Bruno.

"I think reviewing the action, and I reviewed it immediately, it is a clear red card for Phil because it is a reaction. But you can also see Bruno [foul Foden]. But anyway, it is what it is. Red card, but we won.

"Last year I was here with Chelsea and we had red card after three minutes, so next time I was hoping for a different story. We had a plan for 11 vs. 11, but after the red card, the game completely changed, but also for them.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Foden will be banned for three matches (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

"They [United] love transition and space in behind, but the game became more difficult with us and them We just drop, no space in behind and no more transition which is why the game was also more difficult for them."

Foden now faces a three-match suspension following his straight red card, unless City opt to challenge the ruling. He is expected to sit out the League Cup clash against Norwich City, the home fixture against Sunderland on September 20 and the away trip to Liverpool on October 11.

Sports.title: Five stars could miss Ipswich vs Arsenal Carabao Cup clash through injury amid nervous wait
Sports.content:
Five stars could miss Ipswich vs Arsenal Carabao Cup clash through injury amid nervous wait

Arsenal and Ipswich Town face each other in an intriguing League Cup clash at Portman Road, but some are expected to miss the match

View 3 Images Ipswich Town host Arsenal in a League Cup third-round clash (Image: Naomi Baker, Getty Images)

Arsenal and Ipswich Town could be without five injured players between them for Tuesday night's clash. Both sides go into their Carabao Cup contest off the back of a victory.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side maintained their 100 per cent start to the new campaign by beating Sunderland 2-0 at the Stadium of Light. Meanwhile, Ipswich secured their second Premier League win of the campaign with a dramatic 3-2 away victory over Crystal Palace.

‌



The East Anglians and the north Londoners come together on Tuesday evening in the third-round of the League Cup, in which Arsenal got all the way to the final in last year before losing to Manchester City at Wembley.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal are sweating on the fitness of Ben White , who appeared to pick up a knock during the victory over Sunderland at the weekend, reports Football London.

White started the match at the Stadium of Light but was hauled off at the break after visibly wincing in discomfort at several points throughout the opening 45 minutes. White did not feature in any training pictures uploaded by the Gunners' media team on Monday.

‌



Arteta offered no update on White's condition following the win on Wearside, leaving his availability for the Ipswich clash very much up in the air. William Saliba remains a long-term casualty for Arsenal with a back problem sustained while on international duty with France during the World Cup.

View 3 Images Ben White came off at half time after looking visibly in pain (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

There is further doubt surrounding when Cristhian Mosquera will return to first-team contention, with the defender continuing his recovery from a muscle injury.

‌



Arteta revealed last week that he anticipates Mosquera returning to action relatively soon, saying: "(Cristhian's) doing really well, let's see if he can get [back] for this game [Sunderland] or the next one," Arteta said.

Ipswich are also grappling with several injury worries ahead of their encounter with Arsenal, with midfielder Jack Taylor remaining sidelined with a knee problem.

View 3 Images Jack Taylor is yet to feature this season (Image: Izzy Poles - AMA, Getty Images)

‌



There is also uncertainty surrounding whether Azor Matusiwa will be fit for Ipswich, with the midfielder having only just recovered from a thigh complaint.

Town manager Gary O'Neil confirmed last week that Matusiwa is ready for minutes, but cannot yet feature from the start.

The ex-Wolverhampton Wanderers manager said: "Azor will obviously be a little bit longer before he's available to start football matches, but he's ready for minutes now. We can start to get him back in and around matchday squads."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Action taken after Mikel Arteta's 'not acceptable' claim as Gunners eye Serie A raid
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Action taken after Mikel Arteta's 'not acceptable' claim as Gunners eye Serie A raid

Arsenal are top of the Premier League with four wins from as many matches but there was some controversy around their most recent match

View 2 Images Arsenal were unhappy with a penalty award in their win at Sunderland (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

The games are coming thick and fast for Arsenal in the lead-up to the international break. Mikel Arteta is expected to ring the changes for a Carabao Cup meeting with Ipswich Town, just days after the Gunners saw off the challenge of Sunderland in the Premier League.

‌



That trip to Wearside didn't pass without incident. Arsenal survived a contentious penalty call after David Raya pushed Enzo Le Fee's effort onto the post, with Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka going on to punish Sunderland late on.

‌



We have seen the fallout from that decision continue into the new week but there is plenty more to talk about. While Arteta's team showed their strength in depth on Saturday, speculation over their future plans continues.

‌



We've got an update on one eye-catching transfer link, as well as the latest on the Gunners' conversations with Pro Ref. Here are our lines from around the Emirates Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Gunners embark on Pro Ref talks

Arsenal's frustration with the refereeing on Saturday has prompted the club to open talks with Howard Webb, head of officiating body Pro Ref, according to football.london. The frustration surrounds a decision to award a penalty against Ezri Konsa after a tussle with Dan Ballard, a call which was upheld despite the presence of VAR.

"I'm so upset, it is unacceptable at this level, unacceptable. It can change the course of the season," Arteta told TNT Sports after the match. "I've seen it 10 times to make sure and I said 'it is not possible it is penalty'. It is a judo roll. That's what it is.

"This cannot happen. In my view. I have been involved in football for 27/28 years. It's not a penalty in any game, in any game, in any context in any league."

‌



Paz deal and Real Madrid option

View 2 Images Nico Paz has attracted attention with his displays for Como (Image: Marco Canoniero/Shutterstock)

Arsenal are considering a January swoop for Como star Nico Paz, according to The Sun. However, the Argentina star's former club Real Madrid could yet stand in their way.

The 22-year-old delivered 12 goals and seven assists last season to help Como reach the Champions League for the first time. He set up two of his team's four goals as they beat RB Leipzig in Europe last week and scored his first goal of the new season in a Serie A win at Genoa.

Article continues below

Paz joined Como for a little over £51m in 2024 but Real Madrid have an option to bring him back to the Bernabeu for the best part of £70m in summer 2027. This leaves Arsenal with a potential battle for one of European club football's rising stars, who scored once in eight appearances for Los Blancos before moving to Italy.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher sticks the boot in on Bruno Fernandes over 'disappointing' antics in Man City loss

Jamie Carragher says he was "really disappointed" with the actions of Bruno Fernandes during the incident which led to Phil Foden's red card in the loss against Manchester City

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher was not impressed with Bruno Fernandes (Image: Sky Sports)

Jamie Carragher has condemned the behaviour of Bruno Fernandes following the incident that led to Phil Foden being sent off in the Manchester derby.

‌



The Manchester City midfielder was shown a straight red card after aiming a kick at the midriff of Fernandes, who had left Foden on the ground following a coming together by the touchline. The Manchester United captain then sent his foot into the small of Foden's back, sparking the violent reaction which curtailed his involvement in the game.

‌



Erling Haaland went on to win the game for City following a highly dubious VAR intervention which, along with Foden's red card, became one of the major talking points from the derby.

‌



Fernandes escaped punishment for his part in the clash with Foden and Carragher has now questioned the Portugal international for the manner of his reaction after the 'kick'.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“What I would say is two yellows [cards] would have been fine. But I was really disappointed with Bruno Fernandes,” Carragher said on Monday Night Football.

“There’s a lot of things in football that we like or we don’t like. My big one that I really don’t like is people going down, pretending they’re hurt. But doing that…I can’t have it.

“I know there will be Manchester United fans watching this saying: “Oh it’s because he’s a Manchester United player, it’s because he’s a foreign player”. On this show about five or six years ago Harry Kane did the same in a game between Tottenham and Everton and I said the same, I can’t accept it. I’m not having the reaction from Bruno there, it was a brush from his foot.”

‌



View 2 Images Fernandes was kicked by Foden during the derby (Image: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images)

Roy Keane echoed similar sentiments when he dissected the incident at half-time of Sunday's game on Sky Sports.

“Foden gets up and reacts obviously so he's now sent off. The strange thing is, if you look at it, so Bruno catches him, gives the foul away and gives him a little kick. Foden is sent off and I'm guessing it's classed as violent conduct.

Article continues below

“To me, Bruno is the one who's violent here. I have to call it out. I called Kyle Walker out a few years ago when he went down with a headbutt. Listen, we see violence, I suppose, in a different way. But I don't think that's a red card for Foden.”

Sports.title: England confirm Williams as captain for Rugby League World Cup
Sports.content:
England head coach Brian McDermott has confirmed George Williams will be his captain at next month's Rugby League World Cup.

Williams suffered a neck injury and required surgery in April but returned to action in August and has hit the ground running for Warrington Wolves since, hoping to lead them to the Super League Grand Final.

Warrington face Hull KR in the eliminators this Saturday, live on Sky Sports, with the winner facing Wigan Warriors in the semi-finals before the Grand Final on October 3.

McDermott has been impressed with Williams' return from injury and said his "leadership has been really good".

"I didn't really know George at all. In fact, I didn't know many of the squad at all, to be fair. I've only ever shook their hands after games," he said.

"I normally shook George's hand after his team beat my team when I was at Leeds. We had a horrible record against Wigan in the regular season!

Image: Williams is also Warrington Wolves captain

"It's been really enjoyable to get to know him. He's keen as anything and while he was injured, you could tell if anyone was coming back from injury early then it would be him.

"I'm pleased to see the form he's in now, the intent he's playing. He's not feathering about on his feet and waiting for the game to come to him, he's going and getting the game. He goes and chases the game and that's George Williams all over.

"When he first broke into first grade, we all said, 'who the hell's this guy?' Because he went and got the game, he chased the game, whether he's trying to beat the bloke opposite him or quite often coming back to the inside and finding a lazy defender. Add a few years to that and he's got a bit stronger and wiser."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League match between Hull FC and Warrington Wolves

Who will be England's other half-backs?

Williams being captain means he will almost certainly take one of the half-back spots, which raises question marks over who will partner him.

Mikey Lewis, Jake Connor, Harry Smith and Hugo Savala are all in the mix but McDermott suggested only three will be on the plane to the World Cup, which takes place in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea from October 15 to November 15.

"Whether we take a six and a seven to back up the six and a seven that I have in mind to start, I'm still not sure," said McDermott.

"We're certainly going to take another half. We need to take another half. But if we take two halves as cover, it has an impact on how many covers we have for our outside backs, what cover we have with the back rowers, what cover we have for the other spine members as well. Some of that will be to do with form, some of that will be to do with versatility as well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikey Lewis scored on his return from a four-month ban last month

"If a guy can play in the halves, but he can also play at nine, I might favour that as well. Unsure yet. Certainly, the spine members there, it's a difficult one with the spine members.

"I've got to see them play in finals. Everyone would understand who the spine members are going to be or what other players I'm choosing from. But there's another couple out there that the finals will reveal.

"Can they handle the big occasion? Can they handle the game when there's so much on the balance? I'll certainly be taking one half as back-up. Whether I take two or not, it's dependent on the ship."

Sports.title: London misses out as Nairobi secures 2029 World Athletics Championships
Sports.content:
The World Athletics Championships are heading to Africa for the first time after Kenya's capital Nairobi was confirmed as host of the 2029 edition, with London missing out.

Kenya has long been a superpower in distance running but has yet to host an event of this scale. The championships will return to Germany in 2031 with Munich hosting.

"We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council," said World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as he announced the decision following the Ultimate Championship in Hungary.

"The quality, ambition and commitment demonstrated by all four candidates underlines the strength and global appeal of the World Athletics Championships."

Jack Buckner, CEO of UK Athletics and co-founder of Athletic Ventures, said: "We are deeply disappointed that the 2029 World Athletics Championships will not be held in London. We believed we had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels.

"We would like to thank the Government, the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, the Mayor of London and UK Sport for their fantastic support for our bid. Our thanks also to the London Stadium, West Ham United and our many stakeholders for their commitment and hard work to put the bid together.

"The UK is an incredible host for major sports events and the British public loves athletics. Athletic Ventures has the ambition to bring those events here and, although today's announcement hasn't gone our way, we will review and regroup. We know the world's athletes love competing here and we'll continue to explore further opportunities to make that happen.

"Our congratulations go to Nairobi and we wish the organising committee all the best for a great event in 2029."

Image: Seb Coe, president of World Athletics, confirmed the decision to take the 2029 championships to Nairobi

Nairobi's selection represents a landmark moment for athletics, bringing its biggest global event to Africa for the first time.

"Taking our championships to Africa for the first time will be historic," Coe said. "Athletics is woven into the fabric of Kenya."

After the new Ultimate Championship brought big cash prizes instead of medals for an invitation-only field of track's biggest names, it is back to the traditional worlds format next year in Beijing.

The World Championships run for 10 days, against three for the new Ultimate Championship, with a full slate of events. That means including competitions like the men's triple jump, shot put, walks and marathon which were not on the schedule in Budapest last week.

"Kenya is one of the great athletics nations. The sport is woven into the fabric of the country, and athletes such as world gold medallists Faith Kipyegon, Vivian Cheruiyot, Eliud Kipchoge, Hellen Obiri and David Rudisha, as well as two-time Olympic champion Kip Keino, multiple world cross-country champion Paul Tergat and multiple world half-marathon champion Tegla Loroupe, have shaped the history of our sport," Coe added.

"It was important that the World Athletics Championships should come to Africa when we had the right host, the right bid and the right circumstances. Nairobi has demonstrated emphatically that this is their moment."

Sports.title: Five newcomers included in Pocognoli's first Scotland squad
Sports.content:
Sevilla striker Robbie Ure and Brondby's Luis Binks are among five players handed their maiden full Scotland call-ups in new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli's first squad.

Celtic defender Colby Donovan, Hearts winger Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh of Swansea City are also included for the upcoming Nations League games.

There is also a long-awaited recall for Hull City striker Oli McBurnie who won his last international cap in 2021.

Scotland squad in numbers Five - Robbie Ure, Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh are first-time call-ups.

Seven - The total number of uncapped players, with Luke Graham and Jon McCracken returning to the squad after previous call-ups.

Seven - Also the number of those back in after missing out on the World Cup: Oli McBurnie, Scott Bain, Billy Gilmour, Josh Doig, Kieron Bowie, Lennon Miller and James Wilson.

Three - Scott McTominay, Lawrence Shankland and Che Adams were all at the World Cup but are now sidelined and miss out this time.

Twelve - One dozen from the USA miss out, with John Souttar, Anthony Ralston, Grant Hanley, Dom Hyam, Tyler Fletcher, Lyndon Dykes, George Hirst and Ross Stewart adding to the three above.

Goalkeepers Scott Bain and Jon McCracken are back in following Craig Gordon's decision to retire after the World Cup.

Napoli's Billy Gilmour returns after a knee injury forced him to withdraw from former boss Steve Clarke's final squad.

Luke Graham is included after being part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May, following a breakthrough season with Dundee.

The Stoke City defender, who has been capped three times at under-21 level, has played every minute as The Potters picked up three wins and a draw in their last four Championship games.

Josh Doig and Kieron Bowie of Serie A club Sassuolo, Lennon Miller of Udinese and Hearts forward James Wilson have also been recalled.

Image: James Wilson (L) has impressed since returning to Hearts

Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay is missing as he recovers from minor heart surgery. Rangers striker Lawrence Shankland is sidelined with a hamstring issue, with Torino's Che Adams also injured.

A total of 12 players who went to the World Cup are missing from the Belgian's first squad.

Rangers' John Souttar, Anthony Ralston of Celtic, Hibernian defender Grant Hanley, Wrexham's Dominic Hyam, Tyler Fletcher of Manchester United, Millwall's Lyndon Dkyes, Stoke forward George Hirst and Swansea's Ross Stewart are also not included.

Who are the new players?

Image: Defender Luis Binks captains Brondby

Defender Binks is the captain of Danish SuperLiga side Brondby.

The 25-year-old has previously represented Scotland at U18 level before playing for England youth.

Former Rangers academy product Ure secured a mega-move to LaLiga club Sevilla after an impressive spell at Swedish side Sirius where he netted 20 goals in 20 matches.

The 22-year-old is also eligible to play for Ukraine through the grandparent rule.

Image: Josh McPake has scored twice for Hearts this season

McPake has been rewarded for his impressive form since his summer switch to Hearts from St Johnstone, while Swansea's Welsh comes in after his successful loan spell at Motherwell from Celtic last season.

Right-back Donovan has featured in all of Celtic's games so far this season and replaces his Hoops team-mate Ralston.

Scotland squad in full:

Goalkeepers: Scott Bain (Falkirk), Angus Gunn (San Jose Earthquakes), Liam Kelly (Rangers), Jon McCracken (Bradford City)

Defenders: Luis Binks (Brondby), Josh Doig (Sassuolo), Colby Donovan (Celtic), Luke Graham (Stoke City), Jack Hendry (Al-Ettifaq), Aaron Hickey (Brentford), Scott McKenna (Dinamo Zagreb), Nathan Patterson (Torino), Andy Robertson (Tottenham), Kieran Tierney (Celtic), Stephen Welsh (Swansea City)

Midfielders: Ryan Christie (Bournemouth), Lewis Ferguson (Bologna), Billy Gilmour (Napoli), John McGinn (Aston Villa), Kenny McLean (Norwich City), Josh McPake (Hearts), Lennon Miller (Udinese)

Forwards: Kieron Bowie (Sassuolo), Findlay Curtis (Rangers), Ben Gannon-Doak (Bournemouth), Oli McBurnie (Hull City), Robbie Ure (Sevilla), James Wilson (Hearts)

'Style' key for Pocognoli

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli explains his first squad with five new call-ups for the Nations League games

Sebastein Pocognoli, speaking after his squad announcement:

"For me, the most important is regarding the style of play I want to produce on the pitch.

"My focus is to select the players regarding this.

"I could extend this list because I had to make some choices. There are a lot of players who could also be in this list, players who are not there could be because of the style of play.

"It can be from injury or playing time. That's the main reason, the style of play that I want to produce.

"I think we have a good mix between experienced players, new faces, first-cap players, young lads, players who are back.

"The most important thing is to welcome these new faces, to have these experienced players, to pass the DNA, the heritage and also the culture.

"I have to start a new journey, start a new book. What happened is part of the past. "Now I have to build something.

"It's a new opportunity for some players, a really new beginning for the other one. After that, it's to show on the pitch and to have the right attitude outside and on the pitch."

McFadden: Ure has been brave

Image: Robbie Ure has played for Scotland at youth level

Former Scotland striker James McFadden on Sky Sports News:

"Robbie Ure is one that has been on the radar for his form in Sweden in particular, towards the run-up to the World Cup, but missed out on the squad.

"Getting that move to Sevilla shows that he has the capabilities to go and play at the highest level.

"It's an area that we've struggled with for a number of years and for Scotland to bring competition.

"Robbie Ure's taken an unconventional route. He definitely deserves a respect because he's been brave to move away and forge a career elsewhere and probably be allowed to develop and focus on himself to get to this point."

On McBurnie's recall, McFadden added: "Oli deserves his opportunity and there's been a bit of a backlash towards Oli over the last few years.

Image: Hull City's Oli McBurnie (L) won his last Scotland cap in 2021

"I know how passionate he is about playing for Scotland. He's had to be patient but again another one that's gone away and worked on himself and focused on himself.

"Got back to the Premier League and Oli is definitely worth coming in and having a look at to see if he can go and make that number nine spot his own."

Sports.title: Littler needs 'crucial days off' as he chases history
Sports.content:
World No 1 Luke Littler says he has earned the right to pick and choose which darts tournaments he plays in.

Littler has only played two Players Championship floor events, entered just three European Tour tournaments and skipped the recent World Series competitions in New Zealand and Australia.

The 19-year-old has taken a step back this year, limiting the number of lower-key events he has entered as he manages his schedule.

PDC president Barry Hearn recently fired a warning to the sport's top stars about regularly missing tournaments, but Littler says he can be his own master given his position at the top of the rankings.

"I think obviously it's just what's best for me and my family, just having those crucial days off. I think we're going to see more days off just to rest," he told the Press Association.

"That's all I'm doing. I'm obviously world number one, and there's a massive gap between myself and world number two. I can sort of take that step back and not go chasing every single tournament. It allows me to have, obviously, days off and weeks off, and yeah, just about balancing the schedule."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler reacted to the huge mural that has gone up of him in Warrington

Littler is only taking part in the Players Championships this year in a bid to win a clean sweep of major titles.

However, having won the first six major titles of the year, he is aiming for all 10 and that requires him to qualify for the Players Championship Finals in November.

He is playing catch-up after skipping the first 26 floor events of the year, before beginning his bid in Leicester a fortnight ago.

Whether he continues his pursuit will depend on how he fares in the World Series of Darts Finals this week.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Laura Turner and Chris Murphy debate whether or not Littler is currently the best sportsperson in the world

If he does not win the tournament in Amsterdam and can no longer secure every major title this year, he is unlikely to try and qualify for the Players Championship in Minehead.

"That's all you can do. I can't be looking forward any more than what's next, which is the World Series in Amsterdam," he added, speaking through his role with KP Nuts, which launched 'Hit the Bullseye', giving fans the chance to win £20,000.

"If I hopefully do win the World Series, then Tuesday and Wednesday I'll be in Den Bosch for the Pro Tours, try and qualify for Minehead. We've just got to see what happens in Amsterdam this weekend."
