World.title: Container truck crashes into vehicles on Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
World.content:
A 40-foot container-laden truck on Tuesday crashed into demarcation blocks and other vehicles at the exit of Kara Bridge on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, causing traffic to build up to New Garage.

The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) stated that the truck reportedly suffered brake failure before the crash.

“A 40ft container laden truck reportedly had a brake failure and rammed into the demarcation blocks and other vehicles at the exit of Kara Bridge,” the agency said in a post on X.

LASTMA noted that its officials and police officers were deployed to the scene to control traffic, while the affected vehicles were being evacuated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The crash happened amid ongoing repair work on Kara Bridge, where the federal government is replacing damaged expansion joints.

The two-week repair began on 8 September and is scheduled to end on 22 September.

The Acting Controller, Federal Ministry of Works, Ogun State, Richard Adeleye, told journalists during an inspection of the affected portion of the expressway.

Mr Adeleye explained that the repair had become necessary because the expansion joints had exceeded their service life and were posing risks to motorists using the busy highway.

He noted that the work would be carried out in phases to minimise its impact on traffic. One half of the affected section was initially closed while motorists use the other half under strict traffic control.

“There will be traffic control here from the 8th of this month, which will last for two weeks, precisely because of the curing that is expected before it is opened to traffic,” he said.

“We will first work on half of the expansion joint to allow traffic to go slowly on the other half of the carriageway. After one week, we will switch to the other end.”

The work has led to traffic restrictions around the bridge and the adjoining sections of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

Kara Bridge has been the scene of several crashes involving heavy-duty vehicles.

In January, two people were killed in a multiple-vehicle crash around the Kara axis.

LASTMA also reported another crash on Tuesday involving a loaded trailer and a Sport Utility Vehicle on the bridge inward to Mowe.

The agency advised motorists using the route to drive with caution and follow the directions of traffic officials at the scene.

World.title: Full List: ‘Widow’s Bay’ leads 2026 Emmy winners with record 14 awards
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

‘Widow’s Bay’ dominated the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, setting a new record with 14 awards, including Outstanding Comedy Series, as the 2026 ceremony produced a night of historic wins and broke the previous comedy single-season record of 13 set by ‘The Studio’.

The series emerged as the biggest winner of the night, setting a new single-season record for wins by a comedy series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards with 14 total victories while ‘The Pitt’ claimed Outstanding Drama Series and ‘DTF St. Louis’ won Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series.

Matthew Rhys was one of the night’s biggest stars, making history after winning two lead acting awards — Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series for ‘Widow’s Bay’ and Outstanding Lead Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie for ‘The Beast in Me’.

Jean Smart won Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series for ‘Hacks’, extending her record to five consecutive wins in the category.

Rhea Seehorn won Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for ‘Pluribus’, while Noah Wyle took Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for ‘The Pitt’. Sally Field won Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie for ‘Remarkably Bright Creatures’.

World.title: Barca’s Flick says supporting ‘self-confident’ Yamal Ballon d’Or bid
World.content:
Yamal

Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said Tuesday he will support teenage winger Lamine Yamal’s bid to win the Ballon d’Or, noting the player’s “self-confidence” on and off the pitch.

The 19-year-old forward, who won the World Cup with Spain and La Liga with Barca last season, said Sunday he believes he deserves the individual accolade.

Yamal claimed in an interview with Movistar that he and Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe were the two best players in the world and that his teams’ success should put him first, when the award is decided on October 26.

“I think he’s honest, has the self-confidence and shows in the beginning of the season how good he is,” Flick told reporters.

Yamal has scored seven goals in Barca’s last four games, helping the Catalan giants maintain a 100 percent start to the season.

Flick said although he would have preferred the teenager not to have spoken about it, he accepts it as part of the winger’s self-belief.

“He’s exceptional and it’s a part of this… I would not prefer this, but he’s doing this. He has self-confidence, he wants to win the Ballon d’Or.

“As a player it’s an important thing. He’s honest, it’s his feeling and we have to accept it. I will support him of course.”

– Everyone goes ‘wow’ –

Flick said Yamal’s confidence was also what makes him such a spectacular player to watch.

The youngster made his debut for the club at 15 years old and finished as runner-up in last year’s Ballon d’Or award behind Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele.

“He also shows his self-confidence on the pitch and for us this is important,” continued Flick.

“We all want him to play how he plays, and this is a style of confidence. One against one, or two, or three… everyone in the stadium goes ‘wow’. This is Lamine and I will support him.

“It’s amazing to have a player like him. When he’s of the opinion he deserves it, I think also he deserves it. He won two titles with us, the World Cup with Spanish national team, why not?

“There’s a lot of world class players on the list, so it’s not easy. They will decide and I’ll be very happy when it’s finished.”

Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane is also among the favourites to win the Ballon d’Or.

La Liga leaders Barca welcome promoted side Racing Santander to Camp Nou on Wednesday as they bid to maintain their perfect start to the season.

Barcelona’s rebuilt stadium will host the Champions League final in 2029, European football governing body UEFA announced earlier Tuesday.

Flick, whose contract with the club ends in 2028, said he did not know if he would still be managing Barca by then.

“I’m 100 percent there… as a coach or as a supporter of Barca,” said the coach.

“We never know what happens. Football is very fast. I enjoy staying in Barcelona, coaching Barca, this is a fantastic team, but in the end you don’t know what happens.”

World.title: Wike to Uzodimma: Rainbow Coalition not responsible for your abysmal support for Tinubu
World.content:
Wike

By Omeiza Ajayi

Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, has queried why the Imo State Governor and Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF), Hope Uzodimma, was unable to garner massive support for President Bola Tinubu in the 2023 election, saying modern politics is no longer about coming from fourth position to emerge governor.

He insisted that his own task ahead of 2027 is to mobilise support for President Tinubu’s re-election, not to intervene in local politics in the states.

In a statement on Tuesday by the Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the FCT Minister, Lere Olayinka, Wike said the Rainbow Coalition does not have anything to do with the All Progressives Congress APC, describing the coalition as a platform for other political parties that are pleased with the good works of the President and are supporting his re-election.

The minister, who said he won’t be the one to help people win elections in their states, noted that “politics is local and those having problems in their States should resolve them instead of using the reelection of the President to whip up sentiments.”

Wike pointed out that he never met with the APC before himself and other members of the G5 supported the President in 2023, and that for 2027, his support is for the president only.

The minister said politics is no longer about coming from fourth position to be governor; it is about genuinely mobilising support and winning elections from the polling units.

Taking a direct swipe at Uzodinma’s home turf, he asked: “In Imo State under Governor Hope Uzodimma, how did APC win two Senate seats in 2023, in an election held the same day with that of the President and APC had less than 15 percent in the presidential election? Was it Rainbow Coalition? Were the voters confused?

“Was it Rainbow Coalition that also made APC to win National Assembly elections in Ebonyi, Abia and Enugu states where the President did not have ten percent of the votes?

“If in 2023, the voters in Imo, Abia, Enugu and Ebonyi voted APC in the Senatorial election and voted another party in the presidential election, they won’t be confused in 2027 provided we all support the president genuinely this time?”

The minister urged all stakeholders to put the presidential election first, saying: “After the President must have been reelected, we can all go and face elections in our states.”

“What I said and stand for is that I will mobilise support for the re-election of the President. I never promised anyone that PDP will not field candidates to contest governorship, National Assembly and States House of Assembly elections.

“Most importantly, Rainbow Coalition has nothing to do with the APC. Rather, it is own way of mobilising support across political parties for Mr President, who has done well to deserve a second term,” he added.

State governors elected under the platform of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) had warned against the creation of parallel political structures capable of undermining President Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, in a position widely seen as a direct response to the Rainbow Coalition championed by Wike.

Uzodimma, who Wike had recently accused of sponsoring political attacks against him, made the declaration on behalf of the governors on Monday night during a closed-door meeting at the Imo State Governor’s Lodge in Abuja.

World.title: Owie carpets Tinubu over concession of Kings College
World.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY – FORMER Chief Whip of the Senate, Sir Rowland Owie on Tuesday carpeted President Bola Tinubu over the concession of Kings College Lagos to the old boys association of the school, a decision that has resulted into a national strike by staff of unity schools across the country.

They are contending that such fate would befall all other unity schools in the country if that of Kings College succeeded as they argue that it was a surreptitious way of privatising the school.

Reacting to the development in Benin City, Sen Owie said the Unity schools were the remaining symbols of unity in the country and that the concession must be allowed to stand.

According to him, “This is trying to destroy unity school, you want to privatise them? It is shocking that the president of a nation that comes from old western region, which was controlled by the old UPN where free education started, free health, can now be talking about privatising education.

“This is the highest level of insanity insanity in body, insanity in health, insanity in administration. It is unfortunate that Tinubu will be the one doing this. It shows certainly that there is madness in this government.

“This policy should be reversed immediately so that the unity of our country will be sustained.”

World.title: Tribunal slams SDP over lack of diligent prosecution of case against Oyebanji
World.content:
Governor Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State

By Rotimi Ojomoyela

Ekiti State Governorship Election Petition Tribunal has slammed the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and 1st petitioner over unnecessary delay in presentation of witnesses for speedy trial of the petition.

The Chairman of the three-man tribunal, Justice Abubakar Kutigi, expressed disappointment and anger over the way the petitioner’s counsel, Ebenezer Akingbule, who stood in for the lead counsel, Adebayo Adewole, was foot-dragging and adopting delay tactic in the presentation of witnesses.

After the tribunal’s adjournment, the court premises became charged, as SDP members, who considered themselves the real owners of the party made spirited efforts to attack those they described as ‘impostors’ parading themselves as witnesses.

Policemen on guard had to quickly intervene and urged the party members to go outside the court’s premises to resolve their internal wranglings, which was a replica of the internal crisis that played out on Monday when the party’s candidate withdrew his case.

The SDP and 1st petitioner in the case, is challenging the victory of Governor Biodun Oyebanji, the candidate of the ruling All Progressives Congress in the June 20 election, claiming that the conduct of the poll didn’t substantially comply with the provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026.

During the tribunal’s proceeding held on Monday, the party’s candidate and second petitioner in the matter, Amb Isaac Adedayo Alade, had withdrawn his petition, leaving behind only the SDP to prosecute the case.

The candidate of the People’s Democratic Party and runner up in the poll, Dr Wole Oluyede, had during the tribunal’s inaugural sitting of last Monday, withdrawn his petition and was struck out accordingly.

At the trial on Monday, Justice Kutigi could not hold back his disappointment at the counsel to the petitioner over inability to present witnesses in court and for craving for adjournment to do same, after telling the panelists that the witnesses were ready.

Speaking pointedly, Justice Kutigi, emphasized the imperative of the counsel closing his case, if he realises that his witnesses are no longer available, rather than to tactically waste the precious time of the tribunal.

Justice Kutigi, who frowned at the action, said the SDP lawyer must make up his mind and ensure the matter is not stalled unnecessarily, saying procrastination could constitute serious snags and impediments to the electoral trial.

“We can’t continue to indulge you or allow you to tender apology over flimsy excuses. You can’t continue to waste the time of the court here. Why are you behaving as if you are not ready for this case? Any serious practitioner must have put his house in order. You don’t know the volume and even the serial number of exhibits and witnesses. We are not going to indulge you again.

“Do you think we are here to play. You are deliberately wasting our time because you knew that your witnesses are not around. You knew that the petitioner has internal crisis. You can’t say at one breath that they are ready and the next time you are saying they are not available.

“Why can’t you just say the truth and ask for adjournment to be able to put everything in order. You said they were here, have they now disappeared? Later you said they are here, but not within range. What are you trying to say?

“Our own is for you to do the right thing and you can go and take care of your internal crisis later. If you know you can’t get witnesses, then close your case within reasonable time, so that you won’t waste our time”.

However, Justice Kutigi granted adjournment sought by the counsel to the petitioner and ordered him to present the witnesses on Wednesday, September 16 unfailingly.

World.title: Some people sponsor terrorism to blackmail Tinubu as they did to Jonathan — Bishop Kawas
World.content:
President-General of the conference, Archbishop Leonard Bature Kawas

The President-General of the Charismatic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria, Archbishop Leonard Bature Kawas, has alleged that some individuals are sponsoring banditry, kidnapping and terrorism in the country in an attempt to discredit President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

Kawas made the allegation while defending the recent endorsement of Tinubu for a second term during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Tuesday.

The cleric said the endorsement was not financially motivated, insisting that no money was given to the bishops in exchange for their support for the President.

“Today, this endorsement has not given us any one naira. No one naira has been given to us. We did it because, based on current happenings in our nation, the sabotage of people sponsoring banditry and sponsoring kidnapping and all these things just to give Tinubu a bad name,” he said.

Kawas compared the situation to what he said happened during the administration of former President Goodluck Jonathan, arguing that similar efforts were allegedly made to portray Jonathan negatively.

He said the bishops were convinced that the insecurity confronting the country was being exploited by some people to frustrate and discredit Tinubu’s government.

“That is why we decided that since it is a proven fact and there are international intelligence on this that some people are sponsoring all this banditry and terrorism just to give Tinubu a bad name to frustrate his government and to blackmail him and blacklist him,” Kawas said.

The cleric said the bishops’ decision to endorse Tinubu was therefore based on their conviction that he remained the candidate they should support.

“That is why we say no. If that is the case, then it is Tinubu that we are going to support. So we are. We believe that we are being led to do so,” he added.

Addressing the question of whether political endorsements should be influenced by financial considerations, Kawas said the absence of financial benefits would not prevent the bishops from backing a candidate they believed was suitable.

“If we participate in politics, and any blessing comes from it, fine and good. But where the blessing does not come financially, it also doesn’t matter so long as we are convinced that that is the right candidate,” he said.

He also referred to the 2023 presidential election, noting that Peter Obi’s reported refusal to give money to Nigerians did not prevent the bishops from supporting him at the time.

“So, that is what happened as at the time when Peter Obi did not give any money to any Nigerian, he said he would give shishi, and that did not stop us,” Kawas said.

World.title: As Ballon d’Or vote nears, stars campaign for the award
World.content:
MIAMI, FLORIDA – SEPTEMBER 12: Lionel Messi of Inter Miami CF is challenged by Elias Saad of Nashville SC during the MSL match between Inter Miami CF and Nashville SC at Miami Freedom Park on September 12, 2026 in Miami, Florida. Photo by Sam Navarro / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

With less than two weeks to go before Ballon d’Or voting closes, many leading candidates are campaigning hard to be awarded football’s top individual honour.

This self-promotion is a relatively recent development in a team sport where, until a few years ago, the top individual prize went largely unnoticed until it was time to present it.

But now, the Ballon d’Or dominates the football conversation during the months when the new European season is still finding its feet.

The trophy will be presented on October 26, while the final sprint began on September 8 when France Football, the award organiser, released the list of 30 candidates to succeed Ousmane Dembele.

The ceremony will be in London, even though only five of the 30 nominees play in the English Premier League.

The award carries no cash prize, but it has become worth increased income and status to players and their teams.

Many stars have related bonuses in their boot contracts while the award also increases their overall marketing value, and that of their club.

The two all-time leading Ballon d’Or winners, Lionel Messi, who has picked up the trophy eight times, and Cristiano Ronaldo, who won five times, both have annual sponsorship income estimated by Forbes at more than 65 million dollars.

Clubs can expect to sell more merchandise if one of their players wins.

Some 100 invited journalists –- one representative from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings -– will cast votes.

With no clear favourite, the stars and their PR agencies are stepping up their campaigns. Achievements are shamelessly paraded to scrape together votes.

‘I deserve it’

“For me, Mbappe and I, we’re the two best players in the world,” Lamine Yamal, who has won the World Cup and La Liga in 2026, said in an interview on Movistar Plus.

“I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I deserve it because of what I’ve won,” the 19-year-old aded.

He was responding to the Frenchman, who days earlier had emphasised the award’s individual nature — after a year in which he won no trophies with either Real Madrid or France, who lost a World Cup semi-final to Spain, but scored 10 World Cup goals to take his tally to an all-time leading 22.

“Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out, a global event. Who am I voting for? Myself,” said the striker, who was also the top scorer in last season’s Liga and Champions League.

His manager, Jose Mourinho, did not hesitate to back up the argument: “We know who has made history this summer, and he’s not from PSG or the Spanish national team.”

In 2024, Real Madrid boycotted the ceremony after learning just before they were due to travel that none of their seven nominees had won.

This year, Paris Saint-Germain have a record 10 nominees, after retaining the Champions League.

That number, and also the side’s reputation for collective team spirit, may count against them.

Their leading candidates are Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Fabian Ruiz, the only player on the list to have won both the Champions League and the World Cup this year.

‘Why not dream?’

“Why not dream?”, the unassuming Spanish midfielder told French television.

PSG are refusing to pick one individual while arguing that the winner has to be one of their players.

“Kvara and Doue are incredible players. For me Kvara could win the Ballon d’Or, as could Dembele and others,” said coach Luis Enrique.

Dembele told France Football that he would not try to influence the poll.

“May the best player win; in any case, it’s not us who are voting,” he said. “I never sell myself. It’s up to them to decide.”

Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane, who scored 73 goals while leading Bayern Munich to a German domestic double and his country to third in the World Cup, remains quiet.

Bayern are speaking up for their leader, putting together a video in which team-mates said that Kane should win.

“He deserves to win it, 100 per cent, without a doubt,” said Colombian Luis Diaz, who is also on the shortlist.

Vanguard News

World.title: ‘Why?’ — Richarlison reacts with crying emoji after Spurs snub
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Tottenham forward Richarlison has reacted angrily to being left out of the squad for Tuesday’s Carabao Cup clash with Liverpool, posting a “Why?” message alongside a crying emoji on social media.

According to the BBC, the Brazil international shared a screenshot of a post about his omission before adding the brief message, amid growing uncertainty over his future at the north London club.

Richarlison’s latest reaction comes days after a proposed return to Brazilian side Vasco da Gama collapsed, with Tottenham reportedly agreeing a fee for the 29-year-old but failing to reach an agreement on personal terms before Brazil’s transfer window closed.

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi had earlier said he tried to convince Richarlison to remain at the club and offered him a contract extension.

“At the start of this season, I spoke to him many times to convince him to stay and he didn’t want to,” De Zerbi said.

“I can’t go every day to pray for him to stay.”

The Italian added that the situation between the player and the club was private, saying: “The relationship, the problem is between the player and the club.”

Richarlison had also been left out of Tottenham’s Premier League squad after his proposed £35 million deadline-day move to former club Everton collapsed over personal terms.

The forward is understood to be exploring his options and wants to be released from the remaining nine months of his contract, although Spurs have an option to extend the deal by another year.

His latest omission comes at a difficult time for Tottenham, who are yet to win a Premier League match under De Zerbi and have failed to score in their opening four league games.

Richarlison was Tottenham’s leading scorer last season with 12 goals in all competitions, while he has also scored four times in seven appearances against Liverpool since joining Spurs from Everton in 2022.

The 29-year-old has 54 caps for Brazil and previously played for Watford and Everton.

World.title: FJGLOBAL Properties Seeks Global Expansion Through British Business Forum
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohworiole in Abuja

FJGlobal Properties Limited is seeking global al expansion through the British Business Forum (BBF), with the aim of attractiing foreign investors to Abuja.

The firm is seeking to strengthening its international business links to attract more global attention to investment opportunities in Abuja.

This was contained in press statement issued by the firm and signed by Chief Executive Officer of FJGlobal Properties, Dr. Femi Joshua and made available to the press on Tuesday.

“The move followed a strategic meeting between the company’s founder and CEO, Dr. Femi Joshua, and Prince Afolabi Andu, President of the Nigerian British Business Forum.

“Their discussions focused on international investment, real estate, business partnerships and cross-border capital movement.

“They also explored emerging opportunities in Abuja’s real estate market, with a focus on how company can take the lead in positioning Abuja as a compelling investment destination for Nigerians in the diaspora and international investors, while becoming a trusted voice and gateway to Abuja real estate, showcasing credible projects, investment opportunities and the city’s growing real estate economy.”

Describing the caliber of Prince Andy and the what he’s capable of bringing to the real estate sector in Abuja he said, “Prince Andu, is a UK-based entrepreneur and business strategist, has spent years developing platforms that connect Nigerian and African businesses with international markets.

“His activities include involvement in initiatives such as the Nigerian British Business Forum, Best of Nigeria Expo and Nigerian Achievers Awards Institute.

“Through these platforms, Andu has promoted Nigerian businesses and encouraged stronger commercial relationships between local enterprises and international investors.”

The meeting offered FJGlobal Properties an opportunity to explore wider channels for promoting Abuja as an investment destination.

Joshua explained that the project represents more than a conventional real estate development. He said it forms part of a broader effort to showcase Abuja’s economic potential to investors beyond Nigeria.

It also wants to connect the city with Nigerian, African, diaspora and international investors seeking new business opportunities.

FJGlobal Properties’ membership of the Nigerian British Business Forum fits into that broader strategy.

The company sees the platform as a channel for building relationships with investors, entrepreneurs, professionals and institutions across international markets.

Joshua said the company wants to position Abuja within global investment conversations while using its real estate projects to demonstrate the city’s potential.

“We want to take Abuja to the world. Jabi Prime Hub is not just about property; it is an opportunity to tell the story of Abuja’s economic potential and connect that story with investors and businesses across the world,” he said.

He added that the company would continue building partnerships that connect Abuja with the wider global investment community.

The engagement with Andu also highlighted the importance of visibility and collaboration in attracting international capital to Nigerian opportunities.

For FJGlobal Properties, the strategy goes beyond promoting individual projects. The company aims to develop a globally connected real estate and investment platform.

The initiative also seeks to strengthen Abuja’s profile as a city capable of attracting international investors and businesses.

World.title: Inuwa Returns to APC After Four Years of Criticism
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The former Secretary to the Katsina State Government (SSG), Dr. Mustapha Mohammed Inuwa, has returned to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after four years of criticism and political estrangement of the administration of Governor Dikko Umaru Radda.

Inuwa’s return was formally announced on Sunday at a grand reception organised by the Zawiyyah Foundation in his honour at Capital Hall, Katsina.

The erstwhile government scribe renounced his APC membership in 2022 after losing the party’s governorship ticket to Radda and had, since then, been a vocal critic of the governor and his administration.

But while welcoming the former SSG back into the party, Governor Radda described his return as a significant boost to the APC’s unity and strength ahead of the 2027 general election.

Radda, who said his political relationship with Inuwa spanned more than three decades, urged politicians to prioritise public service and the welfare of the people rather than personal interests.

The governor said his administration remained committed to strengthening the APC as a united political family, adding that internal cohesion was essential to sustaining the government’s development agenda and delivering on its promises to the people.

Noting that his government’s doors remained open to working with political elders and stakeholders committed to Katsina’s development, Radda assured people of the state that his administration would continue to prioritise projects and programmes aimed at improving their livelihoods.

He called on party members to work collectively and assiduously towards the victory of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

He said: “Politics should ultimately be about service to the people and not personal enrichment. The people have become politically conscious and they can assess the intentions, records and contributions of those seeking their support.

“We are ready to do everything possible to strengthen our political family. We will not allow the people of Katsina State to be disappointed because we are committed to implementing projects and programmes that will improve their lives.”

Responding, Inuwa described the APC as his political home and pledged his support for the Radda administration.

The former SSG said his return followed decades of political experience, struggles and relationships, stressing that the party’s collective interest should take precedence over personal differences.

“We do not have time for anything that will undermine our collective interest. Our concern should be how to win elections and ensure the success of the APC,” Inuwa said.

He urged APC members to work together to strengthen the party from the grassroots to the national level and sustain the development gains recorded in Katsina State.

Inuwa also acknowledged the support received by the Radda administration from the people, saying the recognition reflected the impact of its programmes and interventions.

The Director-General of the Zawiyyah Foundation, Hon. Hamisu Idris Kofar Bai, said the reception was organised to formally welcome Inuwa back into the APC and recognise his contributions to the state’s political development.

He highlighted the Radda administration’s interventions in security, agriculture and grassroots development, including the establishment of the Katsina State Community Watch Corps, the Community Development Programme and the distribution of fertiliser and other agricultural inputs.

On his part, the state APC Chairman, Dr. Bishir Gambo Saulawa, described the reunion of political leaders within the party as a positive development, stressing that unity and reconciliation were essential to consolidating the achievements of the Radda administration.

Earlier, the member representing Mashi/Dutsi Federal Constituency, Hon. Salisu Yusuf Majigiri, traced the political evolution of Katsina State and acknowledged the contributions of successive administrations and political movements to its development.

World.title: Police Rescue Two Kidnapped Victims, Neutralise Three Gunmen
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

The Niger State Police Command has rescued two kidnapped victims after a fierce battle with the kidnappers in the Wawa forest of Borgu Local Government Area of the state.

According to the command, three of the kidnapers were neutralized, while others escaped with gunshot injuries.

Police Public Relations Officer, SP Wasiu Abiodun, on Monday said the rescued victims were abducted from Wako village with the kidnapers demanding ransom.

Based on this report, Abiodun said in a statement, said the surveillance team attached to New-Bussa Area Command commenced investigation and mobilized with some vigilante men to Wawa forest for the rescue operation.

He added that In the course of this, the suspected kidnappers were intercepted and there was a gun battle between the team and the hoodlums, adding that consequently, the two abducted victims were rescued unhurt, while three suspects amongst the hoodlums were neutralized.

He said other kidnappers escaped with bullet injuries, adding that the victims have been “debriefed and further investigation is ongoing”.

Abiodun also disclosed that one Mohammed Jamiu was arrested at a students hostel in Bida in connection with the discovery of 27 pieces of suspected fake N1,000 notes,

some charms, a calabash and a red cloth.

He said the suspect claimed he sold his motorcycle and that part of the proceeds from the business were the fake N1,000 notes.

World.title: Violence: Tinubu Risks Losing Enugu Votes in 2027, Says PDP Chieftain
World.content:
Gideon Arinze in Enugu

A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Chief Basil Ani, has warned that growing political tension and alleged violence in Enugu State could hurt President Bola Tinubu’s chances in the state in the 2027 general election.

Ani, in a statement to newsmen yesterday, said growing anger over alleged attacks on PDP members and supporters was increasingly being directed at the federal government, and by extension, the president.

He warned that the situation could trigger a protest vote against Tinubu if the federal government was perceived to have failed to intervene in the alleged political violence.

According to him, what began largely as opposition to the administration of Governor Peter Mbah was gradually assuming a wider dimension, with opposition politicians, traditional rulers, and other citizens questioning the federal government’s response to developments in the state.

Ani cited alleged attacks on PDP activities in different parts of the state, including a ward meeting at Akpugo Ward 3 on August 16 and another meeting at Obe Ward, Nkanu West Local Government Area, on August 29.

He also referred to alleged attacks on two PDP ward meetings on September 12, during which more than eight people were reportedly shot and injured, while property was destroyed.

“The allegations are grave, and raised a much larger question: Can citizens freely participate in political activities in Enugu State without fear of violence or intimidation?” he asked.

Ani said the incidents had raised concerns among political stakeholders, particularly against the backdrop of what he described as the absence of publicly known arrests or decisive action over the alleged attacks.

He urged security and law-enforcement agencies to investigate the incidents and prosecute anyone found culpable irrespective of political affiliation.

“If PDP members are attacked, investigate it. If APC members are attacked, investigate it. If supporters of any other political party are attacked, investigate it,” he said.

World.title: Joint Security Outfit Rescues 16-year-old Boy in Onitsha
World.content:
David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

Joint security forces in Anambra State have thwarted the abduction of a 16 year old boy by unknown persons. The boy was rescued in Onitsha at a checkpoint.

A press release by the Anambra State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, stated that with the rescue, the command has intensified surveillance for suspected the abductors.

The command also stated that it is seeking the assistance of members of the public to reunite victim with his family in Enugu State where he was abducted.

The statement read: “Anambra State Police Command has intensified efforts to apprehend a suspected criminal gang following the rescue of a 16-year-old boy, Favour Ayogu.

“The boy was allegedly abducted in Igboeze South Local Government Area of Enugu State and later abandoned near a security checkpoint in Onitsha.

“The rescue followed improved strategic joint security operations conducted on the evening of 13 September 2026.

“A joint patrol team operating at Ekene Junction along Oguta Road, Onitsha, intercepted the victim after he was reportedly dropped from a black Toyota Highlander SUV by unidentified persons close to the security checkpoint.

“The swift response of the joint patrol team led to the boy’s rescue and prevented further harm. The Command has since stepped up surveillance and other intelligence-led measures to identify, trace, and arrest those responsible for the alleged abduction.”

The Command appealed to members of the public, particularly residents of Igboeze South and Ibagwa-Aka in Enugu State, who may have information that could assist in locating the victim’s family, to contact the nearest Police Station or the Anambra State Police Command.

World.title: Shettima Back In Abuja After Attending BRICS Summit In India
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

Vice-President Kashim Shettima Tuesday morning returned to Abuja, Nigeria’s capital, after representing President Bola Tinubu at the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit in New Delhi, India.

During the visit, Shettima participated in the summit’s high-level sessions and held bilateral engagements aimed at advancing Nigeria’s economic and diplomatic interests.

Among the key engagements was a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, where both sides discussed renewed crude oil trade, investment, pharmaceuticals, defence, digital technology, fintech, renewable energy and other strategic sectors.

The vice-president also met with the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, reaffirming Nigeria’s support for multilateralism and a more inclusive global economic order.

At the summit, Shettima delivered President Tinubu’s message calling for reforms of global governance and financial institutions, while positioning Nigeria as a gateway to Africa’s expanding market under the African Continental Free Trade Area.

Nigeria also used the summit to deepen its engagement with BRICS member and partner countries in agriculture, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, manufacturing, healthcare, energy and human-capital development.

World.title: Olaniwun Ajayi Advises on Dangote Refinery IPO, Says Deal Sets Important Precedent
World.content:
Olaniwun Ajayi LP has said that the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE (DPRP) Initial Public Offering (IPO), involving up to 4.1 billion ordinary shares, is an important precedent in the Nigerian capital market.

The firm, in a statement on Monday, also expressed its pleasure at having advised on the IPO while acting as Joint Solicitor to the transaction.

According to a Forbes report on Monday, Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, saw his fortune rise to $51.3 billion following the launch of the refinery’s highly anticipated IPO on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX), amid strong investor demand on the opening day.

The transaction was brought to the market by a consortium of professional advisers, including Olaniwun Ajayi LP, which acted as the Joint Solicitors to the issue.

In that capacity, the firm advised Dangote Refinery on the legal aspects of the offer, from transaction structuring and regulatory engagement through to launch

According to the law firm, the transaction is expected to be the largest IPO in both Nigeria and Africa, marking the first public offer of shares by a Nigerian Free Zone Enterprise in Nigeria.

The law firm stated that the transaction matters beyond the deal as it “establishes an important precedent for capital raising by Free Zone Enterprises”, while contributing to the continued development of the Nigerian capital market.

It added that the proceeds are intended to support DPRP’s long-term growth strategy, including the expansion of its refining and petrochemicals capacity.

The law firm stressed that the offer broadens public participation in one of Africa’s most significant industrial assets.

What you should know

The launch of the refinery’s offer marks a pivotal moment in the continuing development of Nigeria’s capital market.

Investors poured a whopping N1.5 trillion into the refinery IPO within the first hour after the offer opened on Monday, September 14, 2026, on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX).

Dangote outlined ambitious long-term targets during Monday’s ceremony, including growing refining capacity to 2.1 million barrels per day by 2030 and reaching a market capitalisation of no less than $350 billion within four years.

He also confirmed plans to launch a new facility in Kenya by September 30, which is expected to become operational within two years.

World.title: Aig-Imoukhuede Hosts Aliko Dangote Foundation WEF Young Global Leaders Learning Journey
World.content:
Leading African business, finance and investment leaders joined current and former members of the World Economic Forum’s Young Global Leaders community at Access Tower, Lagos, for the Finance and Investment segment of the Aliko Dangote Foundation/World Economic Forum Young Global Leaders Africa-Diaspora Leadership Programme on last Friday.

Hosted by Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede, Chairman of Access Holdings and Coronation Group, the engagement explored “Finance, Capital and the Real Economics of Building at Scale in Africa” – examining what it takes to finance, build and sustain African enterprises of global scale.

The session followed participants’ immersion at the Dangote Refinery and used the Dangote industrial experience as a practical case through which to examine the cost and tenor of capital, infrastructure and logistics constraints, development finance, backward integration, technology and talent, institutional capacity, capital markets and the discipline required to translate ambition into enduring enterprise.

Contributors included Zouera Youssoufou, MD/CEO, Aliko Dangote Foundation; Innocent C. Ike, Group CEO, Access Holdings; Obeahon Ohiwerei, Managing Director/CEO, Coronation Merchant Bank; Adebayo Adewolu, CEO, Trium; Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/CEO, NGX Group; Chuka Eseka, Group Managing Director/CEO, Vetiva Capital Management; David Bird, Managing Director, Dangote Refinery; Kola Karim, Chairman, Shoreline Natural Resources; and Adesuwa Okunbo Rhodes, Founder & Managing Partner, Aruwa Capital Management, alongside other leaders from business, investment and development finance.

A central theme of the discussions was how Africa can move from episodic examples of extraordinary scale to a more repeatable model of capital formation and institution-building, including deeper domestic capital markets, greater mobilisation of pension, insurance, sovereign and private capital, and stronger pathways from concentrated private ownership to broader institutional and public participation.

Speaking during the engagement, Aig-Imoukhuede said:

“Vision attracts capital, governance maintains capital, and execution by great talent compounds capital. All three must be present for an institution to endure.”

Reflecting on the cohort’s visit to the Dangote Refinery, Aig-Imoukhuede described the project as an example of the scale of ambition and execution possible on the continent:

“My dilemma as an African is that for the continent to realise its potential, vision, governance, and execution must happen repeatedly across several nations at the same time. It cannot remain episodic. We cannot wait 20 years between mega-projects. Furthermore, we must fix our greatest handicap, learning how to successfully transfer great visions and institutions from one generation to the next without restarting from the bottom.”

He also called for Africa’s financial architecture to extend across the full yield curve, connecting shorter-term commercial financing with the long-tenor institutional capital required to fund businesses and infrastructure across generations.

Reflecting on the purpose of the programme, Zouera Youssoufou noted that developing visionary leadership and expanding Africa’s capital ecosystems are fundamental to the continent’s long-term prosperity.

The discussions reinforced that Africa’s challenge is not a shortage of ambition or entrepreneurial capacity, but the need to strengthen the capital, institutional and operating systems that enable ambitious enterprises to reach scale and endure.

Closing his remarks with a challenge to the Young Global Leaders, Aig-Imoukhuede said:

“We know that figures like Aliko Dangote are rare, but all of you must be game changers. With the intellect, network and courage you possess, there are no excuses. You share the mantle of responsibility to carry these principles forward and build the enduring institutions Africa requires.”

The Finance and Investment engagement formed part of the wider ADF/WEF YGL Africa-Diaspora Leadership Programme, bringing together current and former Young Global Leaders and senior African decision-makers to examine practical models for building and sustaining African enterprises at scale.

World.title: Good news: Orlando Pirates handed huge CAF Champions League advantage
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have been handed a major boost in their bid to reach the CAF Champions League group stages.

The Buccaneers will face African Stars in the next round of the competition, with the Namibian side set to use the Lucas Moripe Stadium as their home venue.

That means Pirates will not have to travel outside South Africa for the away leg, giving them a significant advantage ahead of the two-legged tie.



With the matches scheduled for October, Pirates should also have the majority of their squad available by then.

The Buccaneers currently have several players on the injury list, including Thalente Mbatha and Gamphani Lungu. However, with another month to recover, Abdeslam Ouaddou could have a much stronger and more experienced squad at his disposal when the CAF Champions League preliminary round arrives.

Why Pirates have the advantage in CAF Champions League

African Stars playing their home leg in Pretoria could work heavily in Pirates’ favour.

The Buccaneers will only have to make a roughly 45-minute trip to the Lucas Moripe Stadium for what is technically their away fixture. They are also familiar with the venue, having played there during the previous season.

The conditions should therefore be less of a challenge for Pirates compared to travelling to Namibia and adapting to a different environment.

There will also be an interesting storyline involving Deon Hotto, who will come up against his former club African Stars.



The Namibian side have already shown that they are capable of competing at the venue, securing an impressive 2-0 victory over Gabonese side AS Mangasport at the Lucas Moripe Stadium.

Pirates will therefore need to remain focused despite their obvious CAF CL advantages.

If the Buccaneers can get past African Stars, they will secure their place in the CAF Champions League group stages for the second time in three years.

Can Pirates win another star?

World.title: Why did hail fall in Durban today?
World.content:
Hail fell in parts of Durban as severe thunderstorms affected KwaZulu-Natal on Tuesday. Image: Unsplash

Residents in parts of Durban were caught off guard by large hail on Tuesday as severe thunderstorms moved across KwaZulu-Natal.

Hail was reported in areas including Montclair, The Bluff and Yellowwood Park, while heavy rain and strong winds caused flooding and disrupted roads in parts of the city.

The N3 near Durban was also affected by localised flooding.



Can strong thunderstorms produce large hail?

Hail forms high inside thunderstorms where temperatures are cold enough for water droplets to freeze.

The storm’s strong upward-moving air, known as an updraught, can keep ice particles suspended inside the cloud. As they move through the storm, the ice can collect more water and grow.

When the hailstones become too heavy for the updraught to support them, they fall towards the ground.



A particularly strong thunderstorm can therefore produce much larger hail than an ordinary shower.

Why did Durban see hail today?

Today’s weather provided the ingredients for severe thunderstorms across parts of KwaZulu-Natal.

SAWS had warned of severe thunderstorms over parts of the province, with the potential for localised damage and flooding.



The storms also brought heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Durban on Tuesday.

A cut-off low has also been linked to the unsettled weather affecting KwaZulu-Natal, with heavy rain, hail and strong winds reported in the province.

However, thunderstorms can remain highly localised. This means one suburb can experience large hail while another nearby area receives mainly rain.



Damage could be reported

Large hail can damage vehicles, roofs, windows and other property, depending on its size and the strength of the storm.

The risk becomes greater when hail falls alongside strong winds and heavy rain.

World.title: Springboks: Answers found at scrumhalf, Williams ready to return
World.content:
Earlier this season, Rassie Erasmus acknowledged that Cobus Reinach and Grant Williams were understandably in the top two when it came to the Springboks’ pecking order at scrumhalf.

However, during the course of the series against the All Blacks, Morne van den Berg continued to go from strength to strength, culminating in a Man of the Match performance in the final Test last Saturday in Baltimore.

The 28-year-old appears to be hitting his prime, and offers plenty of attributes that Erasmus and the coaches will love. He is a warrior, fearless on defence and a nuisance around the fringes.



His kicking game is solid – and he even offers an option when it comes to place-kicking – while his speed of distribution is excellent.

With Reinach now 36 years of age, and having looked unconvincing at times this season, Van den Berg has really seized his opportunity to suddenly be regarded as the first-choice option at No 9.

He has also risen to the occasion in the absence of injured Grant Williams, but the good news for the Springboks is that the Sharks star has now recovered from injury, and will add further depth at scrumhalf for the remainder of the season.



Springboks blessed with depth at scrumhalf

Although Van den Berg has ensured there has been a shake up to the Springboks’ pecking order at scrumhalf, the fact of the matter is that the coaching staff could still call on the likes of Faf de Klerk, Jaden Hendrikse or even Haashim Pead.

Speaking after his performance in Baltimore, Van den Berg admitted it was a dream come true.

“It’s been such a massive honour to play for this team, for this jersey, for our country, and for my family back home. I am so proud of the boys that we could pull it through. It was special (scoring a try). It’s always good to score tries, but a bit more special to score in this game.



“It’s a dream come true (playing against the All Blacks). You honestly dream of this when you’re a young boy playing in the garden. Scoring tries in the corner of the garden. And then to be on this field in America, in Baltimore, in front of this amazing crowd. I am speechless.”

World.title: Drivers take note: These Cape Town licence centres are going cashless
World.content:
A new payment system is coming to three Cape Town driving licence centres. Image: file / canva

Motorists in Cape Town will need to take note of a payment change coming to three Driving Licence Testing Centres (DLTCs) from next month.

The City of Cape Town is testing a cashless payment system at selected centres, with the pilot set to begin on 1 October 2026.

Three driving licence testing centres will go cashless

The pilot will initially run at:



Brackenfell DLTC

Fish Hoek DLTC

Strand DLTC

The three centres are among the City’s 18 DLTCs across Cape Town, which handle thousands of transactions every month.

These transactions include traffic fine payments, learner’s and driving licence applications, licence card renewals and replacements, and applications for Professional Driving Permits (PrDPs).

The centres currently accept both cash and card payments, but customers using the three pilot centres will no longer be able to pay with cash once the cashless system takes effect.

Why is the City making the change?

The City says moving away from cash could reduce the risks associated with handling physical money, while also cutting down on reconciliation work and the costs associated with cash collection.

It also forms part of the City’s broader move towards digital services and improving service delivery.

“The City is moving towards more digital resources, to try and improve our customer experience and service delivery in general,” said Mayoral Committee Member for Safety and Security Alderman JP Smith.



He said the pilot would help determine whether cashless transactions could eventually be introduced at all of the City’s DLTCs.

More changes could be coming to Cape Town DLTCs

The cashless pilot is not the only potential change on the horizon.

Smith pointed to an online appointment system already piloted by the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC) in Gauteng and the Eastern Cape, saying a similar system in Cape Town would be a “game changer”.

The City is also hoping that the recently announced move to 10-year driving licence cards, instead of the current five-year validity period, will eventually reduce pressure on its testing centres once implemented.

World.title: Orlando Pirates’ starting XI vs Durban City
World.content:
Orlando Pirates make a long-awaited return to domestic action this week. How many changes will coach Ouaddou make to the side which played in Mauritius?

Will Pirates make wholesale changes on their return to the league?

Pirates’ predicted XI vs Durban City: Chaine; Sebelebele, Seema, Zulu, Ndaba; Mthiyane, Dansin; Kgositsile, Selepe, Appollis; Mbuthuma.

Reminder of the Starting XI vs La Cure Waves: Chaine; Sebelebele, Seema, Zulu, Rapoo; Mthiyane, Mokobodi; Kgositsile, Masilela, Appollis; Mbuthuma.



Pirates vs Durban City key details

The defending champions had time off from domestic affairs with a CAF Champions League qualifying clash with La Cure Waves FC. The Sea Robbers came from a goal down to win 3-1 thanks to strikes from Kabelo Kgositsile, Kamohelo Sebelebele and Yanela Mbuthuma. Pirates face Durban City in the league on Thursday, 17 September. Kickoff is at 19:30. 24-year-old Mbuthuma has scored three goals in his last three outings.

The situation atop the Betway Premiership

Sundowns remain top with 20 points after eight matches. Pirates are second with 13 points, but have three games in hand on the Brazilians. AmaZulu’s impressive start sees them third on 13 points after six games, while Chiefs sit fourth with 12 points after six outings.

Also read: Rele Mofokeng to leave Belgium for a superior European league

Ouaddou won’t accept showboating

Head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou says results come first and would walk away from the club if flair became more important than scoring goals and finishing matches off. Pirates claimed a 3-1 win over La Cure Waves FC to progress to the next stage of CAF Champions League qualifiers. However, the Sea Robbers took their foot off the gas after taking a two-goal lead. The Sea Robbers came from a goal down to win 3-1 thanks to strikes from Kabelo Kgositsile, Kamohelo Sebelebele and Yanela Mbuthuma.

World.title: Zim woman missing in Kempton Park amid fears over recent deaths
World.content:
A Zimbabwean woman has reportedly been missing for about two weeks in South Africa’s Kempton Park, prompting an urgent appeal for information from her family and friends.

Aisha Gracious Nkomo is reportedly based in Pretoria and worked at a lodge in Kempton Park, according to an appeal circulating among Zimbabwean community groups.

Her friends are said to have told the family that Aisha left her phone charging before leaving with three men.



She has reportedly not been seen since.

Zimbabwean woman still missing

According to the information shared by people close to Aisha, attempts to establish her whereabouts have so far been unsuccessful.

An appeal for information has been circulated on social media as relatives and friends continue to search for her.

“She’s still missing,” the latest update said, appealing to people in Kempton Park and surrounding areas to help locate her.

The family is urging anyone who may have information about Aisha’s whereabouts to come forward.

Kempton Park women’s deaths raise concern

Aisha’s disappearance comes as concern continues to grow following the deaths of several women in and around Kempton Park.



Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the deaths, with the cases attracting significant attention amid fears among women and communities in the area.

However, there is currently no confirmation that Aisha’s disappearance is connected to any of the deaths being investigated.

Her family and friends are continuing to appeal for information that could help establish where she is and whether she is safe.

Appeal for information

Aisha’s disappearance has also sparked concern among Zimbabweans living in South Africa, with appeals being shared across community groups in an effort to reach anyone who may have seen her.

Anyone with credible information about her whereabouts should contact her family or report the information to the South African Police Service.

The family is hoping that the continued circulation of Aisha’s photograph and details will help bring her home safely.

World.title: WATCH: Hail storm hits KwaZulu-Natal as Durbanites take cover
World.content:
KwaZulu-Natal residents are dealing with the fallout of severe thunderstorms that have swept across the province, bringing hail, heavy downpours and strong winds.

KWA-ZULU NATAL HIT BY HAILSTORMS

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) had issued a level two warning for severe thunderstorms for Tuesday, 15 September.

This covers large parts of southern and eastern KZN, including eThekwini, Msunduzi, Richmond, uMngeni, uMkhambathini, Impendle, Maphumulo, Mandeni, KwaDukuza, Nongoma, Ulundi, uMhlathuze and Ray Nkonyeni.



Pietermaritzburg was among the areas hit, with residents reporting a hailstorm moving through the city and surrounding Midlands area on Tuesday.

WATCH: THE THUNDERSTORMS AND HAIL

Hail in Durban. Image: supplied

SAWS had cautioned that residents could expect heavy downpours, lightning, strong winds and large amounts of small hail. The weather service also flagged the risk of localised flooding on roads and bridges.

KwaZulu-Natal had already been placed under a separate warning for strong winds along the coast earlier in the week, adding to concerns for maritime and coastal activities.

WHAT RESIDENTS ARE ADVISED TO DO

Authorities have urged residents in affected municipalities to avoid travelling on bridges and roads in low-lying areas where flooding or sinkholes may develop.

Steer clear of outdoor activities during thunderstorms given the lightning and hail risk

Secure loose outdoor items ahead of further wind gusts

Motorists have also been advised to take extra caution on exposed routes, particularly in high-sided vehicles.

This developing news story is being updated and more details will be published shortly. Please refresh the page for the fullest version.

Severe thunderstorms were also predicted in Gauteng and Mpumalanga.

World.title: Bafana Bafana’s best starting XI which can help Pitso at AFCON
World.content:
Bafana Bafana will face Guinea and Eritrea later this month in the AFCON qualifiers.

These matches will mark Pitso Mosimane’s first games in charge since taking over as Bafana Bafana head coach from Hugo Broos.

‘Jingles’ has already named his preliminary squad for the two fixtures, with a few new faces included. His final squad is expected to be announced in the coming days.



How Bafana Bafana could line up

With everyone fit and available, here is how the strongest Bafana Bafana starting XI could look.

In goal, Ronwen Williams is expected to retain his place ahead of Sipho Chaine and Ricardo Goss.

Khuliso Mudau remains the first-choice right-back, with Kamohelo Sebelebele providing competition and cover.

At centre-back, Ime Okon could keep his place in the starting XI ahead of Olwethu Makhanya and Lebone Seema.

However, if Mosimane opts for what could be considered his strongest centre-back pairing, Seema should partner Mbekezeli Mbokazi.

The two defenders enjoyed a successful partnership at Orlando Pirates and could potentially reunite for Bafana when Mbokazi returns to the national team setup.



At left-back, Aubrey Modiba remains a reliable option, although he could face increased competition from some of the exciting young left-backs coming through.

In midfield, Sphephelo Sithole is likely to retain his place, with Teboho Mokoena playing alongside him. Thalente Mbatha could provide cover or come into the starting XI when Bafana face stronger opposition and require additional energy in midfield.

Further forward, Relebohile Mofokeng could be one of the key players in Mosimane’s attack. The youngster can operate as a number 10 or from either wing, giving the coach plenty of tactical flexibility.

The biggest question could be the number nine position. Lyle Foster and Yanela Mbuthuma have struggled to find the back of the net consistently, leaving Mosimane with a decision to make in attack.

Bafana Bafana’s best starting XI

Ronwen Williams; Khuliso Mudau, Lebone Seema, Mbekezeli Mbokazi, Aubrey Modiba; Sphephelo Sithole, Teboho Mokoena; Relebohile Mofokeng, Oswin Appollis, Thapelo Maseko; Lyle Foster.

World.title: Body of seventh woman found in Ekurhuleni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG — The body of a seventh woman has been found in Ekurhuleni, adding to a string of deaths that has sparked concern among residents and heightened fears about women’s safety.



The body was discovered floating in a river in Clayville, near the Mall of Thembisa, on 7 September.



Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Major-General Fred Kekana says the latest discovery will form part of the ongoing investigations into the deaths.



This brings to seven the number of women whose bodies have been found in the area since July, with four discovered in just the past few days.



President Cyril Ramaphosa has directed police to urgently investigate and solve the murders of multiple women in Ekurhuleni.



The string of deaths has raised fresh safety concerns among women, amid growing fears that a serial killer could be operating in the area.

World.title: Pemmy Majodina apologises for 'jou ma se p***' outburst
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina has apologised for her recent outburst during a heated community engagement in Kouga.

The exchange happened on 9 September during the launch of the Loerie Sewer Pump Station in the Kouga Local Municipality.

Video of the incident shows a community member being escorted from the venue while shouting “jou ma se p***” at Majodina.

The minister then responded: “Phuma! Jou ma se p*** ook.”

In a statement on Tuesday, Majodina said she “deeply regretted” her response.

“In the heat of the moment, I reacted after being subjected to profane language. I take full responsibility for my conduct and deeply regret responding by using the same words directed at me,” she said.

“I sincerely apologise to the people of Kouga and to all South Africans.”

Majodina also urged members of the public to exercise restraint when engagements become difficult or emotions run high.

“I accept that responsibility and will continue to learn from this experience,” she said.

World.title: 'Someone saw something': Police appeal for clues in Ekurhuleni killings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - “Someone saw something.”

That’s the message from Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Fred Kekana as investigators appeal to communities for information that could help solve a series of women’s deaths in Ekurhuleni.

Kekana says it is concerning that the number of women whose bodies have been found in public spaces has now risen to six.

The latest victim was found outside a clinic in KwaThema, Springs, on Tuesday morning.

The woman, believed to be about 35 years old, was found naked and her body was in an advanced state of decomposition.

Kekana says police received a call early on Tuesday about the discovery.

World.title: No bail: Mkhwanazi, co-accused remain behind bars in Mbense murder case
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Suspended deputy EMPD chief Julius Mkhwanazi and his five co-accused have been denied bail in the Emmanuel Mbense murder case.

The six appeared in the Brakpan magistrate’s court on Tuesday. Their case has been postponed to 24 November for further investigations.

The group is facing murder, robbery and defeating the ends of justice charges in connection with the killing of the businessman.

Mbense was killed allegedly at his Brakpan home, before his body was dumped at a dam near Nigel, in April 2022.

During the bail proceedings, Mkhwanazi’s defence argued that he was not present when Mbense was allegedly assaulted and killed.

Mbense had been accused by police of stealing copper before his death.

The court is now considering the circumstances surrounding the case as the six accused fight to be released on bail.

World.title: Ekurhuleni killings: Police urge patience as probe widens
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police are urging the public to be patient as investigators work to establish whether a single suspect or multiple perpetrators are behind a series of women’s deaths in Ekurhuleni.

SAPS spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe says investigators are still analysing the evidence and victim profiles before drawing conclusions about possible links between the cases.

She says the multidisciplinary task team investigating the deaths will also be bolstered with additional personnel, including members of specialised units.

A sixth woman’s body, believed to be that of a woman in her 30s, was found on the side of the road in KwaThema, Springs, on Tuesday morning.

The body was in an advanced state of decomposition, and police believe it may have been dumped in the area earlier that morning.

Mathe says investigators have not yet determined whether the deaths are connected.

“As police, we are still not yet there. The experts are still analysing the dockets, victim profiles and the behaviour of the suspect or suspects. We are still investigating whether we are dealing with one suspect or a group of men,” she said.

Mathe says the investigation is complex and should not be rushed at the risk of compromising the case.

“We are not going to rush the investigators because we need to ensure that they do a thorough job,” she said.

She also warned that acting on incomplete information could lead to the wrong people being arrested.

“If we put them under pressure to speed up investigations, we might arrest the wrong people. We are pleading with the people of South Africa to exercise a bit of patience,” Mathe said.

She added that now was not the time for a “blame game” as investigators worked to establish the facts.

The latest discovery has intensified concern across Ekurhuleni, with residents and women’s rights groups calling for greater police visibility and urgent action.

Acting Police Minister Feroz Cachalia is expected to lead a high-level meeting on Tuesday afternoon to discuss the killings and the police response.

World.title: Sri Lanka's famed beach shack battles demolition
World.content:
COLOMBO - Sri Lanka's famed seafood shack Beach Wadiya has hosted royalty, including Britain's Princess Anne and sporting legends such as cricketer Sachin Tendulkar, but now faces demolition under a government-ordered coastal clean-up.

The simple Colombo beach restaurant has welcomed a string of celebrities, featured in Madhur Jaffrey's culinary travels and received rave reviews in international publications, including London's Financial Times.

"Beach Wadiya comes with a lot of history," said Suhara Chandrasekera, the founder's granddaughter, now a director of the restaurant.

But more than half a century after it opened, the glamour is giving way to grief at Wadiya -- which means "shack" in the island's Sinhala language.

The government's Coast Conservation and Coastal Resource Management Department gave Wadiya 10 days to pack up and leave -- or face demolition.

That deadline expired on September 10, but the restaurant is resisting the order to leave.

Seven other beach properties were given extensions of about four days to salvage furniture and fittings.

World.title: In Kashmir, lake weeds mix with traditional art
World.content:
SRINAGAR - A Kashmiri artisan is turning weeds pulled from Srinagar's famous Dal Lake into a new ingredient for the centuries-old craft of papier-mache, one of Kashmir's best-known traditional art forms.

Dal Lake is famed for its floating gardens and houseboats against a Himalayan backdrop.

Among its past visitors was Beatles guitarist George Harrison, who stayed on a houseboat in 1966 and met sitar maestro Ravi Shankar.

But the lake has long struggled with heavy growth of aquatic weeds, which Indian authorities regularly remove to keep its waterways clear.

Simran Irshad, 35, began experimenting with weeds after the rising cost of paper made traditional papier-mache increasingly expensive.

With roots in Persian craftsmanship, Kashmir's papier-mache is known for brightly painted boxes, trays and ornaments decorated with intricate floral, bird and paisley motifs -- as well as Christmas ornaments exported worldwide.

- 'Like a treasure' -

World.title: At G20 summit, US unravels power plant climate rules
World.content:
HOUSTON - President Donald Trump's administration on Monday scrapped limits on carbon emissions from coal and gas-fired power plants, the latest in a string of actions dismantling regulations aimed at curbing climate change.

The changes, announced during a G20 energy ministers' meeting in Houston, roll back measures introduced under former president Joe Biden -- and go further, proposing to stop future greenhouse gas regulations over the power sector, which accounts for roughly a quarter of the nation's planet-warming emissions.

"Today, we are cutting the red tape to deliver the largest power sector deregulatory action ever," Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin said at a press conference.

"We are not going to bend the law to climate alarmism and climate radicalism at all at the Trump EPA," he added. He also accused journalists of trying to "scare" the public, using an expletive for emphasis.

- 'Deserted its mission' -

Environmental groups vowed to sue, describing it as a dark day for policies that protect people from the ravages of climate change, and a gift to the fossil fuel industry.

The news comes amid growing signs of Earth's climate system destabilising and loading the dice for more frequent and destructive extreme weather events.

August was the hottest month ever recorded around the world, and the United States just experienced its hottest recorded summer. The main driver of global heating comes from burning fossil fuels, and this year the human-caused warming is stacking on top of a historically intense El Nino weather pattern.

"They're propping up fossil fuel industry profits and completely sidelining people's health and well-being," Rachel Cleetus of the nonprofit Union of Concerned Scientists, told AFP.

"The EPA has deserted its mission entirely, and they're doing it in a way that's cruel. They're gleefully taking credit for it."

The administration has repealed 2024 Biden-era standards that were set under the Clean Air Act to control greenhouse gas pollution from existing coal plants and new gas plants.

These required a reduction of up to 90 percent of carbon dioxide pollution over time, and would have required smokestack carbon capture technology in order to be achieved.

But in its now-finalised rule, the EPA held these standards were impossible to meet and the deadlines too tight.

The second part of the package is a proposed rule that makes a broader statutory argument that the EPA does not have the authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions from the power sector -- and that even if it did have the authority, doing so would be futile, because it would not meaningfully address global climate change.

It builds on the US government's decision in February to overturn the 2009 Endangerment Finding, the scientific determination that greenhouse gases threaten public health and welfare.

The agency said that the repeal would save $310 billion, while the proposed rule would save a further $370 million -- figures that critics expressed skepticism towards and vowed to examine.

Meredith Hankins, a legal expert at the Natural Resources Defense Council, told AFP that the actions had contradictory legal justifications.

They noted that the technical repeal, at least in the draft phase, stated that the EPA had the authority to regulate greenhouse emissions but found the Biden administration went about it the wrong way.

"We'll have to look at the final text of the rule," Hankins said. "But I think on its face you can see the contradictions. So I'm certainly looking forward to seeing them in court."

Trump often calls human-induced climate change "a hoax," and his policy rollbacks have included withdrawing the United States once more from the Paris climate accord and eliminating greenhouse gas standards for vehicle tailpipe emissions.

"Our government is ignoring the reality all around us that people are feeling every day of the impacts of climate change, and just putting their heads in the sand and saying, 'We don't care, it's not our problem, next generation, figure it out yourselves,'" said Hankins.

World.title: Null and void: Court declares sale of Safaricom illegal, unconstitutional
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The High Court has declared the sale of Safaricom unconstitutional and illegal, terming it null and void.

While ordering the shares to be restored to State ownership, a three-judge bench comprising Justices Francis Gikonyo, Roselyne Aburili and Tabitha Ouya found that the transaction of the government’s 15 per cent divestiture of its Safaricom PLC shares was undertaken in violation of the Constitution and various laws governing public finance, procurement, capital markets and competition.

In another blow to President William Ruto’s Kenya Kwanza regime, the court found that the government had already concluded agreements for the sale of its Safaricom shares before completing the policy and parliamentary approval processes.

The judges found that the government had entered into a share purchase agreement at Sh34 per share and a dividend rights purchase agreement with the proposed buyer, Vodafone Group Plc, on December 3, 2025.

The court faulted the plan for the Sh204.3 billion proceeds from the Safaricom share sale, finding that the funds were not tied to specific projects.

According to the judges, the policy documents were too broad and did not specify the projects, costs and locations to which the funds would be allocated, while depositing the money in the National Infrastructure Fund did not amount to ring-fencing it for particular projects.

Court found that the Government’s Sh204.3 billion partial divestiture of its Safaricom shares did not comply with Section 87A of the Public Finance Management Act despite approval by the National Assembly.

The bench ruled that parliamentary approval could not cure breaches in the process, including failure to conduct public participation and misrepresentation and concealment of material information.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.

World.title: Police to restrict access to CBD during Linda Mwananchi Nairobi rally
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi officials during a rally. [Courtesy]

Organisers of the Linda Mwananchi rally and their supporters will not be allowed to access Nairobi’s Central Business District (CBD), Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud has warned.

According to Mohamud, police had received notification of the planned rally, which is scheduled to take place at Jacaranda Grounds on Sunday, through Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

However, he warned that the CBD would remain off-limits, saying police would not allow Nairobi to become a battleground for political supremacy.

“The National Police Service respects the constitutional right of every Kenyan to assemble, demonstrate, express political views, and participate in public affairs, but that right must be exercised peacefully, lawfully, and with respect to the rights and safety of other Kenyans,” Mohamud stated.

According to Mohamud, they had received a tip that some individuals were planning to mobilise goons to disrupt the rally, prompting the directive to keep the CBD out of bounds.

“We have received some information, some credible information, that some individuals may seek to mobilise groups of unruly youths and goons to outnumber and intimidate and confront rival groups.”

“Therefore, I make a direct appeal to all political leaders, organisers or influencers to restrain their supporters and control their crowds. No political objective is worth the blood of a Kenyan,” he added.

Mohamud assured the organisers and those planning to attend the rally that police would provide security throughout the event and facilitate all lawful activities.

The Linda Mwananchi movement is set to hold its Nairobi rally on Sunday, September 13. The procession will start at All Saints Cathedral before proceeding to Jacaranda Grounds.

World.title: ODM vows not to interfere with Linda Mwananchi rally in Nairobi
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize
