World.title: Polls show Argentine distrust of Milei's shift on the Falklands
World.content:
Polls show Argentine distrust of Milei's shift on the Falklands

14th Monday, September 2026 - 22:06 UTC Full article

Photo: Nicolás Aguilera/AFP

Two private Argentine pollsters released findings this week pointing to an adverse reception of President Javier Milei's shift on the Falklands, even though the sovereignty claim commands broad consensus in Argentine society.

The consultancy Analogías, which surveyed views of the national government between September 5 and 8, reported that 61% of respondents expressed distrust of the president's new position: 49.8% said they did not believe him at all and 11.2% believed him little. The firm did not publish technical details such as sample size or margin of error.

Monitor Digital, which analyzed 89,900 mentions of the government on social media, ranked the Islands as the second axis of the official digital conversation, clustered around terms such as sovereignty, measures, the United Kingdom and the United States. Its director, Diego Corbalán, told Perfil the volume did not translate into support: “In some way the government managed to place the issue, but it is not clear that all of it works to its benefit.”

The same study played down the reach of the matter beyond political circles. Across nearly a thousand Google trends recorded in the week after the September 3 televised address, the cluster associated with the Islands appeared only at 27th place, with some 50,000 searches, and the foreign policy category accounted for 0.8% of the total, far below sports and entertainment.

The sequence began with that address, in which Milei asserted sovereignty over the archipelago and announced measures against oil development. The following day the government confirmed sanctions against individuals and companies linked to that activity, and this week it is preparing to send Congress a National Sovereignty Defense bill.

The announcements followed the World Cup episode in July, when National Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva endorsed a ban on flags and shirts referring to the Islands during the semifinal between Argentina and England. The players themselves defied the measure by displaying a banner at the end of the match, and the episode led to the suspension of debate on the land ownership bill in the Senate.

On Sunday the government distributed to the press an institutional video by Santiago Oria, director of audiovisual production at the Presidency, combining statements by Milei, remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump on a possible review of Washington's neutral position, and footage of the match against England, set to terrace music. Milei and La Libertad Avanza figures shared the piece.

Corbalán criticized the strategy in political terms: in adopting it, he said, the libertarians “embrace the whole Kirchnerist populist mode,” which he described as chauvinism.

Islanders confirmed their status as a British Overseas Territory in the 2013 referendum, with 99.8% of the vote.

World.title: Falklands donate £40,000 to Red Cross appeal for Nepal flood victims
World.content:
Falklands donate £40,000 to Red Cross appeal for Nepal flood victims

14th Monday, September 2026 - 21:52 UTC Full article

The flash flood tore through the north of the country on August 26, destroying homes, roads and bridges and cutting off entire communities

The Falklands Legislative Assembly has approved a donation of £40,000 to the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) in support of its emergency response to the floods that devastated northern Nepal.

The flash flood tore through the north of the country on August 26, destroying homes, roads and bridges and cutting off entire communities. The worst-hit districts were Rasuwa and Nuwakot. The IFRC estimates that around 93,000 people have been affected. The Legislative Assembly put the death toll at more than 1,300; Nepali police confirmed 469 in the days following the disaster, and humanitarian agencies maintain that thousands remain missing, among them more than 500 foreign nationals.

The cause is still under investigation, though early indications point to the collapse of a glacier near the Langtang Lirung peak upstream, which is believed to have sent a sudden surge of water into the Bhote Koshi river.

The donation will support the work of the IFRC and the Nepal Red Cross Society, whose teams are on the ground providing clean water, shelter, first aid and emergency supplies. The IFRC released nearly one million Swiss francs from its disaster response fund on the day of the disaster and launched a 25 million Swiss franc emergency appeal the following day.

The Falklands hold a long-standing connection with Nepal. Gurkha soldiers took part in the liberation of the Islands in 1982 and two died as a result of the conflict: Lance Corporal Budhaprasad Limbu, of the 1st Battalion, 7th Duke of Edinburgh's Own Gurkha Rifles, was killed on June 24 at Goose Green when his spade struck a grenade during battlefield clearance work, and Corporal Krishnakumar Rai, of the Queen's Gurkha Engineers, died months later in an ordnance explosion while engaged in similar work. Memorials to both were unveiled in the Islands in 2019. Gurkha units have continued to serve in the archipelago since.

MLA Jack Ford, Chair of the Legislative Assembly, said: “Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this terrible disaster. The Falkland Islands know what it means to depend on the courage and kindness of others in our own hour of need, and the people of Nepal hold a special place in our history. This donation is a heartfelt expression of the solidarity and gratitude our community feels towards them.”

World.title: Milei reaches 166 judicial appointments in a year and announces a federal courts overhaul
World.content:
Milei reaches 166 judicial appointments in a year and announces a federal courts overhaul

14th Monday, September 2026 - 10:25 UTC Full article

Appointing judges in Argentina follows a multi-stage process

Argentine President Javier Milei signed a new round of judicial appointments last week bringing his government to 166 appointments of judges, prosecutors and public defenders in a year, according to a tally released by Justice Minister Juan Bautista Mahiques, who presented it as a record figure.

Decrees published on September 8 in the official gazette formalized 63 appointments: 42 judges, nine prosecutors and twelve public defenders, added to 103 earlier ones. The minister did not publish the full list or the historical series he is comparing against, nor did he specify whether the period covers the calendar year or twelve consecutive months, so the total and its status as a record are figures announced by the government, pending documentary verification.

Appointing judges in Argentina follows a multi-stage process. The Council of the Magistracy runs competitive examinations and draws up a binding shortlist of three; the executive selects from those three and sends the nomination to the Senate, which reviews it in a public hearing and votes; the president then formalizes the appointment by decree. The Senate approved 177 nominations in total, 67 of them on August 27, in the third round since Mahiques took office in March. Most passed unanimously, with opposition votes, prompting internal criticism within Peronism.

Mahiques said the accelerated filling of vacancies eases the burden on courts and speeds up procedural timelines, and mentioned the president and the general secretary of the presidency, Karina Milei, in his post.

Two civil society organizations specializing in the field questioned the procedure. Celeste Fernández, co-director of the Civil Association for Equality and Justice, said there was “a accumulation of irregularities” at every stage of selection, noting that in oral interviews some candidates with low written scores climbed many places. The group also objected to the executive combining members of different shortlists or selecting more than one from the same list, and filed a legal challenge covering fourteen appointments. Paula Litvachky, director of the Center for Legal and Social Studies, said this is the largest appointment process in recent times and warned of conflicts of interest and a lack of independence.

In recent days, several court rulings favored the government and allied figures. The Federal Court of Appeals in Buenos Aires removed the private complainants in the case over an alleged cryptocurrency fraud involving the president, upheld the closure of a file against Economy Minister Luis Caputo over dealings incompatible with public office, and confirmed the dismissal of another case against Macri, Caputo and Deregulation Minister Federico Sturzenegger over a 2018 International Monetary Fund loan. A judge also shelved the file on the entry of ten suitcases without customs checks aboard a private aircraft. None of those allegations was proven. It has not been established that the judges involved are among the recent appointees.

Mahiques announced he will push a federal judicial overhaul aimed at reducing the number of courts in Buenos Aires, where corruption cases involving national officials are concentrated. The government will also seek to fill the two remaining Supreme Court vacancies.

World.title: Falklands RAF’s Voyager tanker back in MPA after support of US efforts in Iran
World.content:
Falklands RAF’s Voyager tanker back in MPA after support of US efforts in Iran

14th Monday, September 2026 - 05:10 UTC Full article

The need to reinforce allies across Middle East after US and Israeli attack on Iran forced the RAF to pull back its resident Voyager tanker from Falklands in April.

RAF air defenses protecting the Falklands Islands have been bolstered by the re-deployment of an Airbus A330 Voyager tanker aircraft back to Mount Pleasant airbase after a five-month long gap.

The need to reinforce allies across the Middle East after the US and Israeli attack on Iran in the spring forced the RAF to pull back its resident Voyager tanker from the Falklands in April.

Open-source aircraft tracking websites showed that a RAF Voyager flew to Ascension Island at the end of August and arrived at Mount Pleasant on 3 September. Since then, it has been flying patrols with the RAF Eurofighter Typhoon fighter jet detachment in the Falklands.

In related news Falklands are upgrading their defense capabilities, and have launched a recruitment drive for a restricted circle of participants with drone operators among those being vetted. Falklands as reported in UK, are primarily hiring Britons with drone-flying experience.

While the locally-maintained volunteer force, FIDF, works close to Britain military personnel at MPC to safeguard the remote South Atlantic islands, it has further stated an interest in regionally integrated candidates, navigation skills and drones operating experience.

The latest controversy with Argentina and territorial claims over the Falklands had Foreign Office Minister Kirsty McNeill tell the Commons that there was no doubt over British sovereignty and reaffirmed the administration’s pledge to safeguard the democratic freedoms of the Falkland Islanders.

The Islands’ defenses have come under renewed political examination after president Milei’s escalation of tensions with Parliament seeking clear assurances over Britain’s extended strategic responsibilities.

Milei further capitalized on comments from Trump suggesting Washington was reviewing its position on the dispute showing them as evidence that international attitudes towards Argentina's claims are shifting.

World.title: Falklands ex Chief Executive, Keeling holding temporary CEO job in Cornwal
World.content:
Falklands ex Chief Executive, Keeling holding temporary CEO job in Cornwal

14th Monday, September 2026 - 05:04 UTC Full article

Keeling served in the chief executive role at the Falkland Islands government from 2021 to 2025

A former chief executive of the Falkland Islands government is taking on a temporary leadership role at a council in the UK. Andy Keeling has been appointed by Cornwall Council as interim deputy chief executive and will start the job this week.

It comes after chief executive Kate Kennally went on a leave of absence. A council spokesperson said there could not be two chief executives at the same time but an officer could deputise if the chief executive was absent.

Interim arrangements were discussed at the chief officers' employment committee, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.

Keeling served in the chief executive role at the Falkland Islands government from 2021 to 2025. He was also previously chief operating officer at Leicester City Council.

Leigh Frost, Cornwall Council's leader, said Keeling had a wealth of experience and “will provide valuable leadership at an important time”.

“We are grateful to him for stepping into the role at such short notice,” Frost added.

World.title: The National Palace’s new resident has four legs and one role: to support emotional well-being
World.content:
The Mexican government has just introduced a new resident of the National Palace. And no, it’s not a politician or public official. It’s a puppy, and his name is Rollo.

In a video posted on the government’s official social media accounts, Rollo is seen running playfully through the corridors and gardens of the National Palace. In another scene, he’s behind a desk, wearing a tie.

Él es Rollo, trabaja en Palacio Nacional. Es un cachorro mestizo adoptado que hoy se divierte en jardines y oficinas bajo el resguardo de la Dirección General de Comunicación Digital de la Presidencia. Tiene un papel muy importante: el apoyo y bienestar emocional de todas y… pic.twitter.com/aoRmKbXHlT — Gobierno de México (@GobiernoMX) September 10, 2026

“This is Rollo. He works at the National Palace,” the post says, adding that the adopted pet, a mixed-breed, has a “very important role: the support and emotional well-being of everyone.”

The video also indicates that Rollo has a brother named Theo, who is still looking for an adoptive family. However, details of where and how to adopt him have not been shared.

Rollo joins other animals living at the National Palace, including the cats that inhabit its gardens and other areas of the palace. President Claudia Sheinbaum herself has shown off these pets during tours of the presidential headquarters.

In May 2026, during the visit of the K-pop group BTS to the National Palace, Sheinbaum said that 16 cats lived there. However, the number of these animals has varied over the years.

In 2024, it was reported that 19 cats inhabiting the National Palace were designated as “living fixed assets” — a legal measure to guarantee resources for their food, medical attention and care for the rest of their lives.

The gatos that have been publicly identified include Coco, Zeus, Roja, Ollie and Balam — two of whom have made a debut on the internet. During the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Coco appeared in posts on official government accounts wearing Mexico’s jersey. Meanwhile, Zeus once wandered into a morning press conference during Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s term (2018-2024).

Unlike Rollo, these cats were not adopted. According to information from the presidential office, they have been there for years, and there is no precise record of how each one arrived.

With reports from Infobae and El Financiero

World.title: Mexico moves toward promoting sports tourism as a major draw for international visitors
World.content:
Fresh off hosting the fourth World Sports Tourism Congress that attracted 500 participants from 30 countries, Mexico is developing a campaign to turn sports tourism into a major draw for visitors.

Spearheaded by the Confederation of National Chambers of Commerce, Services and Tourism (Concanaco Servytur), the project will get support from the public sector, including the Association of Tourism Secretaries of Mexico (Asetur), the federal Tourism Ministry and state sports institutes, all aiming to develop broader tourist experiences around national and international sports competitions.

For starters, Concanaco is developing Mexico’s 2027 sports tourism calendar to enhance the country’s potential for attracting tourists via sporting events.

Mexico is the first Latin American country to host the World Sports Tourism Congress, which ran from Sept. 7 to 9, and is already rich in major sporting events. Concanaco will identify existing championships or tournaments and promote additional tourism activities in the destinations where they are held.

“These aren’t new tournaments; they already exist and are held in the country,” Concanaco President Octavio de la Torre said in an interview with the newspaper EFE, referring to the events on the calendar. “But we’re going to make them visible as sports tourism, not just as a sporting activity. In this ecosystem, we’re going to connect experiences with lodging and, of course, commerce.”

The northeastern border state of Tamaulipas in particular is looking to establish itself as a leading destination for sports tourism. According to state Tourism Minister Benjamín Hernández Rodríguez, the state has allocated over 236 million pesos (US $13.8 million) to the improvement and construction of recreational and high-performance facilities.

Tamaulipas already hosts several major sports events, such as the upcoming Gran Fondo Tampico, a cycling event set for Sept. 27, which offers visitors not only a race to watch but also opportunities to enjoy cultural, gastronomic and recreational activities in the Gulf coast city of Tampico.

International tourism is up — at the border

Mexico received 4.41 million international tourists in July, 3.8% more than in the same month of 2025, the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) reported on Monday. The United States remained the leading source market, with 1.69 million arrivals.

However, July registered a 3.2% decline in international tourists staying at least one night while simultaneously logging a 13.2% increase in border tourism, referring to visitors who enter Mexico at its northern or southern border but do not travel farther inland. Similarly, air arrivals of international tourists in July were down 5.7%.

With reports from López-Dóriga Digital and Diario de México

World.title: Industrial activity grew 2.4% in July, its best result in nearly 3 years
World.content:
Industrial activity in Mexico grew 2.4% in annual seasonally adjusted terms in July, the best result in almost three years.

Month-over-month growth was 0.5%, according to the national statistics agency INEGI, which published the data last Friday.

The construction sector was the driving force behind the annual growth, the strongest since October 2023, although the mining, manufacturing and energy sectors also made gains.

Construction activity increased 6.7% annually in July, mining activity grew 1.6% and manufacturing activity rose 1.3%. Activity related to electricity, gas and water supply increased 0.7% compared to July 2025.

On a month-over-month basis, construction activity grew 0.9% in July and manufacturing activity increased 0.7%. The electricity, gas and water sector recorded 0.0% month-over-month growth, while mining activity declined 1.8%.

The year-over-year industrial activity growth in July was triple the 0.8% reading in June. The month-over-month growth was more than double the 0.2% increase recorded in June.

Industrial activity has now increased on an annual basis across four consecutive months. July marked the second consecutive month with sequential growth in industrial activity.

Industrial activity is up slightly this year

In the first seven months of 2026, industrial activity grew 0.4% compared to the same period of last year, according to INEGI.

Mining activity increased 3.5% annually in the January-July period, while construction activity grew 2.8%.

Manufacturing activity — the largest contributor to the industrial data — declined 0.7% on a year-over-year basis while the electricity, gas and water sectors collectively recorded 0.0% annual growth.

The modest year-over-year growth between January and July came after industrial activity contracted 1.3% in 2025.

Economists from Grupo Financiero Monex said in a report that they anticipated that industrial activity would continue to grow at a “moderate” pace in the coming months.

They said that USMCA-related uncertainty and U.S. tariffs on certain strategic Mexican goods (vehicles, steel and aluminum) could continue to constrain investment decisions and the performance of export-oriented manufacturing sectors.

With reports from El Economista

World.title: Riviera Maya regains its color as sargassum subsides
World.content:
Slowly but surely, the Riviera Maya has begun to regain the clear turquoise waters that underpin much of its tourist appeal, following several months of massive sargassum arrivals along the Quintana Roo coast.

In an interview with the news outlet Reportur, head of the Federal Maritime-Terrestrial Zone in Tulum David Buchanan García said that local beaches are returning to their natural colors following the removal of 5,600 tonnes of seaweed in recent months. Though influxes are down, Buchanan García insisted that his brigades will continue cleanup efforts in anticipation of potential new deposits of the macroalgae.

🌊 ¿Plan de sábado? El Caribe mexicano luce con playas limpias y poca presencia de sargazo en Playa del Carmen. ☀️ Con clima ideal para disfrutar el mar, solo recuerda estar atento a las condiciones.#NEXO #PlayaDelCarmen #QuintanaRoo #CaribeMexicano pic.twitter.com/Yv0uVU9FYd — Nexo Quintana Roo (@nexoquintanaroo) September 12, 2026

Arturo Quintero Díaz, head of the Municipal Public Services Department for the municipality of Benito Juárez in Cancún, told the news outlet Novedades Quintana Roo that this slowdown is typical of the sargassum cycle, which sees fluctuations and a gradual decline between the months of August and October.

2026 has been the worst sargassum year ever recorded in the Riviera Maya. Between April and August, Quintana Roo removed 124,852 tonnes of sargassum from its coasts — 29,069 tonnes more than during the same period in 2025 — according to figures from the state’s Environment Ministry.

Meanwhile, in Cancún alone, 29,482 tonnes of sargassum have been collected so far this year — a figure far exceeding the 16,000 tonnes recorded throughout 2025. Playa Delfines was among the locations requiring the most attention.

Playa del Carmen also reported large volumes of macroalgae removed, followed by Cancún, Puerto Morelos, Tulum and Mahahual.

Quintana Roo’s pristine beaches may be resurfacing once again, however, challenges lie ahead in 2027.

Esteban Amaro Mauricio, head of the Quintana Roo Sargassum Monitoring Network, told the newspaper La Jornada that although seaweed wash-ups are expected to be minimal during November and December, they could increase shortly after.

According to Amaro, influxes may begin as early as January rather than April or May, when the season typically ramps up. This pattern was observed at the beginning of 2026, which marked the earliest arrival of the seaweed since the seasonal phenomenon began affecting the Mexican Caribbean some 12 years ago.

With reports from Reportur

World.title: Pemex contains another oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico
World.content:
An oil spill was detected at Pemex facilities north of Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche, last Thursday, prompting the Navy to activate a contingency plan to help the state-owned company control the leak quickly enough to assure the public that no oil would reach the coastline.

Unlike the major Gulf Coast incident that occurred earlier this year, Pemex quickly confirmed that crude was leaking from one of its pipelines.

En la Sonda de Campeche, Pemex inició instalación de la envolvente metálica, a 50 metros de profundidad, para la reparación de la sección afectada del ducto submarino en campo Ek-Balam, ocurrida el jueves 10 y que puso en alerta ante derrame de crudo en aguas del Golfo de México. pic.twitter.com/dNDHANG8kA — Quadratín Tabasco (@QuadratinTa) September 14, 2026

“Immediate action was taken to depressurize the pipeline and isolate it by closing safety valves at its ends,” Pemex said in a statement released on Saturday. “Since then, it has remained without flow and without any leakage.”

Complementing Pemex’s security measures, the Navy deployed its ARM “Guanajuato” Ocean Patrol Vessel, four additional boats and two aircraft, along with 255 naval personnel.

Additionally, continuous observation is being carried out to monitor the evolution of the slick — which measured 4 square kilometers on Thursday — and forecast its movement so as to apprise state authorities and the public.

Agency for Safety, Energy and the Environment (ASEA) scientists were analyzing three drift forecast models, all projecting a net westward shift over the next five days. ASEA has also been conducting overflights to document the containment, the clean-up and repair efforts.

The Permanent Observatory of the Gulf of Mexico — which discovered and reported the leak — is an integrated, real-time environmental monitoring system created by the federal government in April.

It was launched amid fallout over a massive leak in February that Pemex officials originally hid from upper management and then was made worse when the oil company denied responsibility.

This time, authorities have been more transparent. Pemex acknowledged that the incident occurred at its Ek Balam platform system, part of the Cantarell oil field, one of the most productive in Mexican history

By Sunday, the dredging of the seabed had been completed and Pemex said pipeline repairs would be completed in the coming days.

With reports from LopezDoriga.com, El Economista, Vanguardia and El País

World.title: Spanish exchange student killed in Morelos
World.content:
A 21-year-old Spanish university student was murdered in the state of Morelos, Mexico, on Saturday in a crime that is being investigated as a femicide.

Claudia Tacoronte Aguilera, a University of Granada (UGR) student who was studying at the Autonomous University of the State of Morelos (UAEM) on an exchange program, was stabbed at the Casa de la Cultura cultural center in Cuautla, a city around 40 kilometers southeast of Cuernavaca.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by adn Noticias (@adnnoticiasmx)

The cultural center was hosting an event focused on medicinal plants when the murder was perpetrated. Casa de la Cultura de Cuautla said in a statement that Tacoronte was the victim of an “alleged robbery with a bladed weapon.”

Morelos Attorney General Fernando Blumenkron told reporters on Sunday that the crime was being investigated as a femicide as authorities seek to determine whether the victim’s gender was a motivating factor. As of Monday morning, no one had been arrested in connection with the murder. Blumenkron said on Sunday that the aggressor hadn’t been identified.

He said that Mexican authorities immediately notified the Spanish Consulate in Mexico of the death of Tacoronte, who was studying early childhood education. She began her exchange program at the UAEM campus in Cuautla last month.

UAEM and UGR condemn the murder

In a statement, the UAEM expressed its “profound anger” over the “femicide” of Tacoronte, a native of the Spanish island of Gran Canaria.

“The Autonomous University of the State of Morelos expresses its most sincere condolences to her family, her friends, her classmates, the University of Granada, … the Spanish government and Spanish society,” the UAEM said.

“We stand in deep solidarity with all of them in the face of this irreparable loss and we share the grief that overwhelms them today,” the university said.

The UAEM called on the Morelos Attorney General’s Office to carry out an “immediate” and “exhaustive” investigation “with a strict gender perspective” in order to “guarantee justice and avoid impunity.”

In its own statement, the UGR expressed its “absolute” condemnation of the murder of Tacoronte.

“The university community wishes to convey its deepest condolences, solidarity and affection to Claudia’s family, friends and classmates at these times of such profound pain,” the university said.

The Conference of Rectors of Spanish Universities also condemned the murder of Tacoronte, saying she was a “victim of an intolerable act of violence that has shocked all Spanish universities.” At a press conference in Andorra on Monday, the Spanish Minister of Foreign Affairs, the European Union and Cooperation José Manuel Albares said that the Spanish government will seek to shed light on what happened so that “those responsible are brought to justice.”

The rector’s office of the University of Granada later announced the cancellation of the exchange program with UAEM, impacting three students who were set to study in Morelos next semester.

Tacoronte is the 4th UAEM student to be murdered this year

Tacoronte is the fourth UAEM student to be murdered this year. All of the other victims were women.

An average of around 10 women are murdered daily in Mexico. Around one-quarter of those murders are prosecuted as femicides, according to the EFE news agency, which cited statistics from Mexican authorities and non-governmental organizations.

In the first seven months of 2026, a total of 380 femicides were committed in Mexico, according to official statistics.

More than 40% of the cases occurred in just five federal entities: Sinaloa, Morelos, Chiapas, Mexico City and Tamaulipas.

With reports from EFE, El País, Cadena Ser, El Economista, El Financiero and DW

World.title: Mexico, US aiming to resolve trade issues before US midterms
World.content:
Listen to this article

The fourth round of trade talks between Mexico and the United States will take place next week, with officials from both sides expressing eagerness to hammer out a deal before the U.S. midterm elections in November, according to sources interviewed by Reuters.

A framework for a deal would benefit both parties.

U.S. President Donald Trump is looking for a win on the economic front (a bilateral deal may bring down consumer prices in the U.S.) as he faces the possibility of losing control of Congress when ballots are cast on Nov. 3. Meanwhile, the Mexican government is struggling with investor unease and a cooling economy.

Mexico’s push to reach a deal comes after U.S.-Canada trade talks — the other half of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) review process — collapsed last month.

The U.S.-Mexico talks are seen as an effort to reach an interim bilateral deal while issues with the USMCA on the whole are ironed out.

President Sheinbaum chatted with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last Wednesday to assess the progress of the negotiations, after which Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard flew to Washington, D.C., to finalize details ahead of the fourth round. Next week’s bilateral meetings will be the first formal return to the negotiating table since the third round of talks was held in Mexico City from July 21-23.

Upon his return to Mexico City on Friday, Ebrard met with José Medina Mora — president of Mexico’s Business Coordinating Council (CCE), the principal organization representing Mexico’s private sector before federal and local governments. It groups 14 major business umbrella organizations that represent more than 2,000 trade associations comprising roughly 80% of Mexico’s GDP.

Medina Mora told the newspaper El Universal that the elimination of Section 232 tariffs, which place duties on aluminum, steel and automobiles, is expected to be a primary focus next week.

He expressed confidence that the two sides will avoid the problems that arose during the U.S.-Canada dialogue, saying they would not affect negotiations with Mexico.

“The bilateral relationship between the United States and Canada is different from our relationship [with the U.S.],” he said, adding that Sheinbaum “has clearly defined the limits of what is unacceptable, while maintaining a cordial … relationship” with Trump.

“[Sheinbaum’s strategy] has yielded results and our negotiations are moving forward,” he said.

On Saturday, when asked whether the United States would leave the USMCA, Trump told the Irish press that “we’re going to have a great relationship with Mexico” and that a deal with Canada would come soon.

With reports from El Universal, Bloomberg and Reuters

World.title: Sheinbaum attributes rise in national pride to 4T governments: Monday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🛣️ Accountability tour hits 18 states: Speaking after her latest “honesty and results” assemblies, Sheinbaum said her nationwide accountability tour has drawn more than 300,000 attendees across 18 states so far, calling the experience “very moving” and framing it as a way to speak to citizens directly about her government’s achievements.

📰 Media outlets are “propaganda of the right”: Sheinbaum accused much of the Mexican press of acting as “propaganda outlets” for the political right, claiming important stories go unreported and that commentators coordinate their criticism of her government in a group chat.

🇲🇽 National pride climbs to 90%, Sheinbaum says: Citing an El Financiero poll, the president said pride in being Mexican rose from 58% in 1990 to 90% today, crediting the shift to “fourth transformation” governments.

Why today’s mañanera matters

President Claudia Sheinbaum held her Monday morning press conference after completing the second leg of her “accountability tour,” a nationwide effort to report directly to citizens on her government’s achievements during its second year in office. To date, Sheinbaum has held so-called “honesty and results” assemblies in 18 of Mexico’s 31 states and will make public speeches in the 13 remaining ones before concluding her tour in Mexico City’s central square, the Zócalo, on Sept. 27.

As was the case last year, the president is undertaking her accountability tour after delivering her annual government report to the nation. The assemblies Sheinbaum holds while “on tour” are similar to her weekday mañaneras insofar as she can bypass intermediaries — such as media outlets — and speak directly to Mexicans, including some of her biggest supporters, about government actions and achievements.

At today’s mañanera, the president sought to underscore the importance of such communication as, in her view, many Mexican media outlets are biased against her administration.

Also of note at today’s press conference were Sheinbaum’s remarks about Mexican patriotism ahead of Mexican Independence Day this Wednesday. On Tuesday night, the president will lead the traditional Grito de Independencia (Shout or Cry of Independence) from the National Palace balcony.

Sheinbaum: Accountability tour has been ‘very moving’

Sheinbaum told reporters that her accountability tour has been “very moving” because large numbers of people have come out to see her everywhere she has gone.

“What I talk about when I speak is the history of Mexico and the patriotic month [mes patrio], and people are very aware of what’s happening, and of the importance of defending independence and sovereignty,” she said.

Sheinbaum said that more than 300,000 people have attended the 18 events she has held so far on her accountability tour.

Sheinbaum: Many Mexican media outlets serve the political right

Sheinbaum asserted that the “objective” of many Mexican media outlets is “to be propaganda of the right.”

“They’re not news outlets, they’re propaganda outlets. That’s what they are,” she said.

” … If something very important happens in the country, it doesn’t appear [in the media],” Sheinbaum claimed.

She subsequently accused media outlets of “distorting reality in a way that agrees with their propaganda.”

“… They seek to distort everything, adapt everything to what they want, create political propaganda for the right,” Sheinbaum said.

The president also accused media commentators of coordinating their attacks on the government.

“They have a [group] chat where they talk about what everyone is going to say during the week,” she said.

“This week, the INE. The INE is not an institution that guarantees clean elections,” Sheinbaum said, referring to the National Electoral Institute and seeking to provide an example of the kind of coordination she believes occurs.

In the context of alleged media bias and distortion, the president portrayed her accountability tour as a presentation of the truth, although her administration also faces allegations of bias.

“What do we do? Disseminate [information], talk. Why do I go to all the states to report [to the people]? So that they hear what we’re doing in all the federal entities,” Sheinbaum said, asserting that if citizens relied solely on the media, it would be difficult for them to find out what her government is actually achieving.

Sheinbaum: There is ‘deep pride’ in being Mexican

Citing poll results, Sheinbaum highlighted that pride in being Mexican is much more prevalent today than it was in 1990.

“The other day we brought out an El Financiero newspaper poll where it said that in 1990, 58% of Mexicans felt proud of being Mexican. Today it’s 90%,” she said.

🗣️ “El 90% está orgulloso de ser mexicanas y mexicanos” 🇲🇽 Claudia Sheinbaum resaltó que el trabajo de la Cuarta Transformación ayudó a que la población sea más orgullosa del país; “algo que no lo dio el neoliberalismo”, agregó pic.twitter.com/kfTuPxe3hH — El Universal (@El_Universal_Mx) September 14, 2026

“I like the poll [result] precisely because it’s what I see every day, especially when I go out on tour,” Sheinbaum said before asserting that there is “deep pride” in being Mexican.

“This didn’t happen during neoliberalism in Mexico,” she said, referring to the period between 1982 and 2018.

Rather, “deep pride” in being Mexican became more prevalent with “fourth transformation” (4T) governments in office, said Sheinbaum, who now leads the 4T movement founded by former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador.

“And it’s very powerful — very powerful because when a people knows their strength and their history, there is nothing that can stop them,” she said.

World.title: Argentina Takes Its Nuclear Export Plan to Vienna
World.content:
ARGENTINA · NUCLEAR

Key Facts — What happened Argentina presented a nuclear export strategy at the International Atomic Energy Agency in Vienna on 14 September.

— Who presented it Federico Ramos Napoli, at the IAEA’s 70th General Conference.

— What it is A plan to sell Argentine nuclear technology and services abroad.

— What it is not A programme to build new reactors in Argentina. That is a separate question.

— Why Argentina can It is one of a small number of countries that designs and builds its own research reactors, and it has exported them since the 1980s.

— Who buys Australia, Egypt, Algeria, Peru and the Netherlands have all bought Argentine research reactors.

Argentina has quietly sold nuclear reactors for forty years. In Vienna this week it said it wants to sell more.

Argentina presented an export strategy at the IAEA General Conference in Vienna on 14 September.

Argentina presented a nuclear export and commercialisation strategy in Vienna on 14 September. The venue was the 70th General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency. Federico Ramos Napoli made the presentation.

What Was Presented

The IAEA General Conference brings member states to Vienna each September. The 70th session opened this week.

Argentina used it to present a strategy for exporting and commercialising its nuclear technology.

Federico Ramos Napoli delivered the presentation.

The subject is selling Argentine capability abroad, not building new capacity at home.

INVAP, based in Bariloche, designs and exports Argentine research reactors.

Why Argentina Has Anything to Sell

Argentina began its nuclear programme in the 1950s and operates three power reactors: Atucha I, Atucha II and Embalse.

It also designs and builds research reactors, a specialised market in which very few countries compete.

INVAP, a state-owned company in Bariloche, is the designer and exporter. It built the OPAL reactor in Australia, which remains its best-known contract.

Argentina has also supplied reactors or components to Egypt, Algeria, Peru and the Netherlands.

What a Research Reactor Is For

Research reactors do not generate electricity. They produce neutrons for scientific work and, commercially, medical isotopes.

Molybdenum-99, used in millions of diagnostic scans a year, comes from a small number of reactors worldwide.

Supply has repeatedly been disrupted when one of them shuts for maintenance.

A country that can build and supply these reactors occupies a narrow but durable position in a global market.

CAREM has been under development for more than a decade.

The Domestic Programme Is a Separate Matter

Argentina has been developing CAREM, a small modular reactor of domestic design, for more than a decade.

Its construction has been repeatedly delayed and its budget repeatedly cut.

The current government has also raised the possibility of private participation in the nuclear sector.

None of that was the subject of the Vienna presentation, and the two should not be merged.

Why Now

Argentina needs foreign currency and has few high-value technology exports.

Nuclear engineering is one of the areas where its capability is recognised internationally rather than argued for.

Global interest in nuclear power has risen with electricity demand from data centres and with decarbonisation targets.

Research reactor procurement runs on a slower cycle and is driven by medical isotope supply rather than by energy policy.

The Constraints

Nuclear exports require safeguards agreements and international approvals, which takes years.

Argentina is a party to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and to the Brazilian-Argentine agency ABACC, which inspects both countries’ facilities.

That arrangement, unique in the world, is part of why Argentine exports are accepted.

Financing is the harder obstacle. Buyers expect export credit, and Argentina’s ability to extend it is limited.

What to Watch

Any contract announcement following the Vienna presentation.

INVAP’s order book, which is the practical measure of whether a strategy becomes sales.

CAREM funding in the 2027 budget, which went to Congress the same week.

And the medical isotope market, where supply shortages drive procurement decisions.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Argentina present in Vienna?

A nuclear export and commercialisation strategy, at the IAEA’s 70th General Conference on 14 September 2026.

Who presented it?

Federico Ramos Napoli.

Is this a new reactor programme for Argentina?

No. It concerns exporting Argentine nuclear technology and services abroad.

What has Argentina exported before?

Research reactors and components to Australia, Egypt, Algeria, Peru and the Netherlands, through the state company INVAP.

What is a research reactor for?

Scientific work and the production of medical isotopes such as molybdenum-99, not electricity generation.

What is CAREM?

A small modular reactor of Argentine design, under development for over a decade and repeatedly delayed. It was not the subject of the presentation.

Sources: International Atomic Energy Agency, Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica, INVAP, ABACC, Télam, Infobae.

World.title: Argentina Protests to Uruguay Over Expo Prado Show
World.content:
URUGUAY · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts — What is Expo Prado Uruguay’s largest agricultural show, held every September in Montevideo. It is the country’s main livestock and farming event.

— What happened Argentina’s embassy in Montevideo sent a formal diplomatic protest about the event.

— What is a nota verbal An unsigned diplomatic note between governments. It carries the sending state’s position without naming an individual author.

— The date 31 August. It surfaced in the press on 14 September.

— Why the date matters It predates President Javier Milei’s 3 September announcement, so it is not a response to it.

— Who signed it Nobody. Notas verbales are unsigned by convention, and no official has been named.

Argentina lodged a formal complaint with Uruguay over an agricultural fair. The note was written before the event everyone assumed prompted it.

Argentina’s embassy in Montevideo sent a nota verbal dated 31 August about the agricultural show.

The Argentine embassy in Montevideo sent a nota verbal dated 31 August protesting about Expo Prado, Uruguay’s annual agricultural show. It became public on 14 September.

The Note

The document is a nota verbal, the standard instrument for a government to register a position with another government.

It is written in the third person and carries no signature. That is convention, not evasion.

It was dated 31 August and lodged with the Uruguayan foreign ministry.

Its existence became public on 14 September, two weeks later.

Why the Date Settles an Argument

President Javier Milei made an announcement on 3 September that has been widely linked to this protest.

The note is dated three days earlier.

A document written on 31 August cannot be a response to something announced on 3 September.

The two are being reported together because they surfaced in the same news cycle, not because one caused the other.

What Expo Prado Is

Expo Prado is run by the Asociación Rural del Uruguay and held each September at the Prado grounds in Montevideo.

It combines livestock judging, agricultural machinery, food and a public fair, and it draws hundreds of thousands of visitors.

Uruguayan presidents traditionally attend and the opening speech is a fixture of the political calendar.

For a country where agriculture drives exports, it is closer to a national occasion than a trade show.

Uruguay and Argentina have managed disputes through formal diplomatic channels for decades.

Uruguay and Argentina

The two countries share a border, a river, a language and a long history of managing disputes through formal channels.

They have argued over pulp mills on the Río Uruguay, over dredging of the shipping channel, and over trade rules inside Mercosur.

Uruguay has pushed for freedom to negotiate trade agreements outside the bloc. Argentina has resisted.

Diplomatic notes between them are routine. What is unusual is one becoming public.

What Has Not Been Established

The text of the note has not been published in full.

No Argentine official has been named as its author, which is normal for the instrument.

The Uruguayan foreign ministry has not published a reply.

What is documented is the date, the sender and the subject.

A separate Argentine sovereignty announcement surfaced in the same news cycle.

Why It Surfaced Now

Expo Prado opens in September, so the timing of a protest about it is not in itself surprising.

The publication two weeks later, in the same week as a separate Argentine sovereignty announcement, is what generated the coverage.

Argentina holds legislative elections in October and Uruguay is governed by an administration that took office in 2025.

Both governments have reasons to be seen defending a position.

What to Watch

Whether Uruguay responds formally, which would normally be a note in return.

Whether the text of the Argentine note is published.

The Mercosur summit calendar, where trade disagreements between the two are usually aired.

And Expo Prado itself, which runs through September regardless.

More: Latin America news, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Argentina send Uruguay?

A nota verbal from its embassy in Montevideo, dated 31 August 2026, protesting about Expo Prado.

What is a nota verbal?

An unsigned diplomatic note written in the third person, the standard way one government registers a position with another.

Was it a response to Milei’s 3 September announcement?

No. The note predates it by three days.

Who signed it?

Nobody. Notas verbales are unsigned by convention and no official has been named.

What is Expo Prado?

Uruguay’s largest agricultural show, run by the Asociación Rural del Uruguay and held each September in Montevideo.

Has Uruguay replied?

No public reply has been published by the Uruguayan foreign ministry.

Sources: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Uruguay, Embajada Argentina en Montevideo, Asociación Rural del Uruguay, El País (Montevideo), Búsqueda.

World.title: SpaceX Shares Reach Mexican Investors Through the BMV
World.content:
MEXICO · MARKETS

Key Facts — What happened SpaceX shares became available to Mexican investors through the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores on 14 September.

— How A cross-listing into the Sistema Internacional de Cotizaciones, the mechanism that lists foreign shares in Mexico.

— Is SpaceX private No, not since June. It listed on Nasdaq on 12 June 2026 under the ticker SPCX.

— The listing 555,555,555 Class A shares at US$135 each.

— What the SIC is not A new issue. No new shares are sold and SpaceX raises nothing from a cross-listing.

— Who benefits Mexican investors, including pension funds, who can now buy in pesos through a local broker.

Mexican investors can now buy SpaceX without leaving the Mexican exchange. The company gets nothing from it.

SpaceX shares entered Mexico’s international quotation system on 14 September.

SpaceX shares were cross-listed into the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores’ Sistema Internacional de Cotizaciones on 14 September. The company went public on Nasdaq on 12 June 2026 under the ticker SPCX.

What the SIC Does

The Sistema Internacional de Cotizaciones is a section of the Mexican exchange that carries shares listed elsewhere.

It lets a Mexican investor buy a foreign share through a Mexican broker, settled in Mexico, without opening an international account.

More than 1,500 foreign securities trade there, and the SIC accounts for a substantial share of total BMV volume.

The foreign company is not involved in the transaction beyond meeting disclosure requirements. It raises no capital.

SpaceX Is Already Public

SpaceX listed on Nasdaq on 12 June 2026 under the ticker SPCX.

The offering was 555,555,555 Class A shares at US$135 each.

Descriptions of SpaceX as a private company are three months out of date.

The Mexican cross-listing is an addition to that listing, not a substitute for it.

More than 1,500 foreign securities trade on the Mexican international quotation system.

Why Mexican Funds Wanted It

Mexican pension funds, the afores, operate under investment rules that restrict direct foreign holdings but permit SIC-listed securities.

That makes the SIC the practical route for Mexican institutional money into large foreign companies.

Retail investors gain simpler access, peso settlement and Mexican tax treatment.

The trade-off is liquidity. SIC volumes for any single security are a fraction of those on the home exchange.

The Date Question

Two dates have circulated for the SIC listing, 14 August and 14 September.

The September date is the better-supported of the two in available filings and reporting.

Listings of this kind are announced by the exchange rather than by the company, which is part of why dates get muddled.

The BMV publishes its SIC additions in its own daily bulletins.

For an investor the date matters only for tax and record-keeping. For anyone checking a claim, it is the field to verify.

Starlink is the revenue engine and is a consumer subscription business.

What Mexican Investors Are Buying

SpaceX operates Falcon and Starship launch vehicles and the Starlink satellite internet constellation.

Starlink is the revenue engine and is a consumer subscription business, which makes it more predictable than launch contracts.

It also has substantial exposure to United States government contracts, in launch and in defence-related programmes.

A Latin American investor gets dollar-denominated revenue exposure. In peso terms that is a large part of the appeal.

Starlink also sells in Mexico, Brazil, Chile and much of the region. The product is familiar to the investors now able to buy the shares.

The Week It Arrived In

Technology stocks fell on Monday. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.2% intraday to a six-month low.

The fall followed an argument about the pace of artificial-intelligence development rather than any earnings news.

Mexico’s IPC index rose 0.26% on Tuesday and was not caught in it.

A cross-listing is announced weeks in advance and does not time the market.

What to Watch

SIC trading volume in SPCX over the first weeks, which shows whether Mexican demand is real or notional.

Afore allocations, published quarterly by the Mexican pension regulator.

SpaceX quarterly results, the first full ones since listing.

And further SIC additions, which the BMV bulletins list.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is SpaceX listed in Mexico?

Its shares are available through the Sistema Internacional de Cotizaciones of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores, from 14 September 2026.

Is SpaceX still a private company?

No. It listed on Nasdaq on 12 June 2026 under the ticker SPCX.

What was the IPO?

555,555,555 Class A shares at US$135 each.

Does SpaceX raise money from the cross-listing?

No. A SIC listing creates no new shares and raises no capital for the company.

Why does it matter to Mexican funds?

Mexican pension funds face limits on direct foreign holdings but may hold SIC-listed securities.

What does SpaceX do?

It operates the Falcon and Starship launch vehicles and the Starlink satellite internet service.

World.title: China to Inspect 17 Brazilian Meat Plants in September
World.content:
BRAZIL · MEAT EXPORTS

Key Facts — What is happening A Chinese inspection mission will visit Brazilian meat plants from 20 to 28 September.

— How many plants Seventeen units.

— Whose plants JBS, Minerva and MBRF, the company created by the merger of Marfrig and BRF.

— Why it matters China is the largest buyer of Brazilian beef and poultry. Plant-by-plant approval is how access is granted.

— A name to get right MBRF, not BRF. The merged entity is the one named in the mission.

— What is not known Which Chinese authority is conducting the mission has not been named in available reporting.

Chinese inspectors will spend nine days inside seventeen Brazilian meat plants. What they decide sets export volumes for years.

A Chinese inspection mission visits seventeen Brazilian plants from 20 to 28 September.

A Chinese inspection mission will visit seventeen Brazilian meat processing units between 20 and 28 September. The plants belong to JBS, Minerva and MBRF, the merged Marfrig and BRF entity.

What an Inspection Mission Does

China does not grant market access to a country. It grants it to individual plants.

An inspection team visits each facility and assesses hygiene, traceability, veterinary supervision and record-keeping against Chinese requirements.

A plant that passes is added to the approved list and may export. A plant that fails is not, regardless of what its neighbours do.

The list is maintained by Chinese customs and is published, which is how exporters know where they stand.

The Companies

JBS is the largest meat company in the world by revenue and operates plants across Brazil.

Minerva is the largest beef exporter in South America and has expanded through acquisitions in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

MBRF is the entity formed by the merger of Marfrig and BRF, bringing beef and poultry under one company.

Reports naming BRF rather than MBRF are using the pre-merger name.

China buys more Brazilian beef than any other country.

Why China Decides Brazilian Prices

China buys more Brazilian beef than any other country, by a wide margin.

When Chinese demand moves, Brazilian cattle prices move with it, which reaches Brazilian consumers at the butcher counter.

Approved plants command a premium over unapproved ones because they can access the largest market.

A mission that approves seventeen units expands capacity for the export channel that sets the domestic price.

China suspended Brazilian beef imports in 2021 and again in 2023.

The History of Suspensions

China suspended Brazilian beef imports entirely in 2021 after two atypical BSE cases, and again in 2023 for the same reason.

Each suspension lasted weeks and cost Brazilian exporters hundreds of millions of dollars.

The protocol between the two countries now provides for suspension of the affected plant rather than the whole country in some circumstances.

That change is why plant-level approval has become the centre of the relationship.

What Is Not Confirmed

The Chinese authority conducting the mission has not been named in reporting available so far.

The customs administration, GACC, normally leads inspections of this kind, but that has not been stated for this mission.

The specific plants have not been listed publicly either.

What is established is the window, the count and the three companies.

What It Means for Brazil

Agribusiness is Brazil’s largest export sector and meat is its most politically sensitive component.

Beef exports have grown for most of the past decade and the constraint has been market access rather than production capacity.

Approvals also matter for the currency. Meat is a dollar-earning export in an economy that needs them.

For Brazilian consumers the effect runs the other way. More export capacity tends to mean higher domestic beef prices.

What to Watch

The publication of approvals after the mission ends on 28 September. It typically takes weeks.

Whether all seventeen units clear, which is not the usual outcome.

Chinese import volumes in the fourth quarter, published monthly by GACC.

And cattle prices at the Brazilian arroba, which respond to approvals before shipments do.

More: Brazil news, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Chinese inspection mission?

From 20 to 28 September 2026.

How many plants will be inspected?

Seventeen units.

Which companies?

JBS, Minerva and MBRF, the entity created by the merger of Marfrig and BRF.

Is it BRF or MBRF?

MBRF. The merged Marfrig and BRF entity is the one named in the mission.

Which Chinese authority is conducting it?

Not named in available reporting. Inspections of this kind are normally led by Chinese customs.

Why does plant approval matter?

China grants export access plant by plant, not country by country. Only approved units may ship.

Sources: Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária, ABIEC, JBS, Minerva Foods, MBRF, Reuters, Valor Econômico.

World.title: Peru Travel Advisory Stays at Level 2 and Excludes Cusco
World.content:
PERU · TRAVEL

Key Facts — What is a travel advisory A rating the US State Department assigns to each country, from Level 1 to Level 4, telling Americans how much caution to use.

— Where Peru stands Level 2, exercise increased caution. Unchanged.

— When it was last issued 4 September 2026. It did not raise the country level.

— What about Cusco The advisory says explicitly that Cusco and the tourist sites near it are not in the affected area.

— Which areas are Level 4 The Loreto border region, the VRAEM valley, and the Abancay, Ayacucho, Huancavelica and Huancayo areas.

— A source to avoid OSAC hosts an archived Level 3 notice. It is out of date and should not be cited.

Reports this week said Washington raised its warning on Peru. It did not, and it named Cusco as an exception.

The US advisory states that Cusco and nearby tourist sites are not in the affected area.

The United States travel advisory for Peru remains at Level 2, exercise increased caution. It was reissued on 4 September 2026 and the level did not change. The advisory explicitly excludes Cusco from the areas it warns about.

What the Advisory Says

Peru is rated Level 2 on the State Department’s four-point scale. That is the second-lowest rating and applies to much of Europe.

The advisory was reissued on 4 September 2026. A reissue is a routine republication and does not by itself indicate a change.

The country level did not move. Reports describing a raised warning for Peru describe something that did not happen.

Within the country, specific regions carry higher ratings, which is standard practice for large countries.

Cusco Is Named as an Exception

The advisory text states that the City of Cusco and popular tourist sites nearby are not located in the affected area.

That is unusual. The State Department rarely names a destination to exclude it.

The wording covers the Sacred Valley and the approaches to Machu Picchu, which sit within the same corridor.

For anyone planning the standard Peru itinerary, the advisory says the opposite of what has been reported.

Machu Picchu sits within the Cusco corridor the advisory excludes.

Where the Level 4 Areas Are

The Colombian border area of Loreto region carries Level 4, do not travel.

So does the VRAEM, the valley of the Apurímac, Ene and Mantaro rivers. Coca production and remnants of the Shining Path persist there.

Level 4 also applies to the Abancay, Ayacucho, Huancavelica and Huancayo areas.

None of these is on a standard tourist route. Reaching them requires deliberate travel away from the main corridors.

The Stale Source Problem

OSAC, the State Department’s Overseas Security Advisory Council, hosts an archived Level 3 notice for Peru.

Archived documents remain online and are indexed by search engines. They carry no date warning on the page itself.

That archive appears to be the origin of this week’s reports.

The authoritative source is travel.state.gov, which carries the current advisory and the date it was issued.

How to Read a Travel Advisory

Level 1 is exercise normal precautions. Level 2 is exercise increased caution. Level 3 is reconsider travel. Level 4 is do not travel.

Most of Latin America sits at Level 2 or Level 3. Regional variation within a country matters more than the headline number.

Travel insurance policies sometimes reference advisory levels, which is the practical reason the rating matters to a traveller.

The United Kingdom, Canada and Australia publish their own advisories, and they do not always agree with Washington.

Rail access to Cusco has been disrupted by political protest in the past, most recently in 2023.

What Peru Looks Like on the Ground

Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu operate normally and receive the great majority of Peru’s visitors.

Lima has the petty crime profile of a large Latin American capital, concentrated away from Miraflores and Barranco.

Peru has had periods of political protest that disrupted rail and road access to Cusco, most recently in 2023.

Nothing comparable is under way now.

What to Watch

The advisory page at travel.state.gov, which carries the issue date at the top.

Peruvian rail operators, which announce service changes for the Machu Picchu route directly.

Any change to the VRAEM designation, which has been stable for years.

And the date on any advisory you are shown. That is the field that settles the question.

More: Travel coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did the US raise its travel warning for Peru?

No. Peru remains at Level 2, exercise increased caution, reissued on 4 September 2026.

Is Cusco covered by the warning?

No. The advisory states that the City of Cusco and popular tourist sites nearby are not in the affected area.

Which parts of Peru are Level 4?

The Loreto border area, the VRAEM, and the Abancay, Ayacucho, Huancavelica and Huancayo areas.

Why do some sources say Level 3?

OSAC hosts an archived Level 3 notice that is no longer current. It should not be cited.

Where is the authoritative source?

travel.state.gov, which shows the current advisory and its issue date.

Is Machu Picchu affected?

No. It sits within the Cusco corridor that the advisory explicitly excludes.

Sources: US Department of State (travel.state.gov), Bureau of Consular Affairs, OSAC archive, Ministerio de Comercio Exterior y Turismo del Perú.

World.title: Quito Fire Forces 23 Families From Homes in La Bota
World.content:
ECUADOR · QUITO

Key Facts — What happened A fire broke out at about 3pm on Monday 14 September in La Bota, a neighbourhood in the north of Quito.

— When it ended It was brought under control around midnight.

— The response Fifty-eight personnel, 21 vehicles, the helicopter Argus and twelve water drops.

— Who moved Twenty-three families were evacuated as a precaution.

— The smoke The city says 63 neighbourhoods could be affected by smoke. A further 698 are under surveillance, which is not the same thing.

— The season Quito has recorded 154 fires and 1,118 hectares burned citywide between 1 July and early September.

A hillside above northern Quito burned for nine hours on Monday. Twenty-three families left their homes.

The La Bota fire began at about 3pm on Monday and was controlled around midnight.

A fire in the La Bota neighbourhood of northern Quito began at about 3pm on Monday 14 September. It was brought under control around midnight. Twenty-three families were evacuated as a precaution.

The Fire

La Bota sits on the northern edge of Quito, on slopes that rise away from the valley floor.

The fire started at around 3pm and burned for roughly nine hours.

Fifty-eight personnel and 21 vehicles were deployed, supported by the municipal helicopter Argus.

Argus made twelve water drops. The fire was declared controlled around midnight.

Who Left

Twenty-three families were evacuated. The evacuation was precautionary rather than a response to homes being alight.

Quito’s protocol moves households out when a fire front comes within a set distance of housing. It applies whether or not the fire is advancing on them.

The Ministry of Public Health deployed mobile brigades on 14 September to handle smoke inhalation and related complaints.

No deaths or serious injuries have been reported.

Two Numbers That Are Not the Same

The city said 63 neighbourhoods could be affected by smoke from the fire.

It also said 698 neighbourhoods are under surveillance. That is a monitoring list covering the whole city during fire season.

Those two figures have been merged in some coverage into a claim that 698 neighbourhoods were affected. They were not.

Surveillance means the municipal risk agency is watching. Affected means smoke reached the area.

A Second Fire the Day Before

On Sunday 13 September a separate fire burned in the La Vicentina and Itchimbía areas, closer to the historic centre.

Itchimbía is a park on a hill overlooking colonial Quito and is one of the city’s most visited viewpoints.

The two fires were not connected and were fought by separate deployments.

Both fall within the pattern of the current dry season.

Quito sits at 2,850 metres in a valley flanked by steep, grass-covered slopes.

Why Quito Burns in September

Quito sits at 2,850 metres in a valley flanked by steep, grass-covered slopes.

The dry season runs from roughly June to September, and the vegetation on those slopes cures into fuel.

Much of it is eucalyptus and introduced pasture grass, both of which burn faster and hotter than the native vegetation they replaced.

Most fires in the city are started by people, whether through burning refuse, agricultural clearing or discarded cigarettes.

The Season So Far

Between 1 July and early September, Quito recorded 154 fires across the metropolitan district.

Those burned 1,118 hectares in total.

That figure is a citywide seasonal total and does not describe the La Bota fire, which was a fraction of it.

Ecuador’s national fire statistics are published by the Servicio Nacional de Gestión de Riesgos.

The municipal helicopter Argus made twelve water drops on the La Bota fire.

What It Means for Residents and Visitors

Smoke from hillside fires settles in the valley overnight and clears through the morning.

Anyone with respiratory sensitivity is advised to stay indoors on affected evenings. The health ministry’s mobile brigades are the first point of contact.

Quito’s airport is at Tababela, outside the valley, and was not affected.

Hiking on the slopes around the city is restricted during high-risk periods, and the restrictions are enforced.

What to Watch

The end of the dry season, usually in October, which is what actually ends the fire risk.

Whether the La Bota site reignites, which is common on slopes where roots continue to smoulder.

Municipal restrictions on access to hillside parks.

And the seasonal total, which the city updates through the end of the period.

More: Latin America news, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where was the Quito fire?

In La Bota, a neighbourhood on the northern edge of Quito. It began at about 3pm on Monday 14 September.

When was it controlled?

Around midnight, after roughly nine hours.

How many people were evacuated?

Twenty-three families, as a precaution.

What was the response?

Fifty-eight personnel, 21 vehicles and the helicopter Argus, which made twelve water drops.

How many neighbourhoods were affected?

The city said 63 could be affected by smoke. A separate figure of 698 refers to neighbourhoods under citywide surveillance.

How bad has the season been?

Quito recorded 154 fires and 1,118 hectares burned between 1 July and early September, across the whole metropolitan district.

Sources: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Quito, Municipio del Distrito Metropolitano de Quito, Ministerio de Salud Pública del Ecuador, El Comercio, Primicias.

World.title: MercadoLibre Raises US$1 Billion in Ten-Year Notes
World.content:
ARGENTINA · MERCADOLIBRE

Key Facts — Who is MercadoLibre Latin America’s largest e-commerce and payments company, founded in Argentina and now incorporated in Delaware.

— What it did Sold US$1 billion of ten-year bonds. They priced on 11 September and settled on 14 September.

— The terms 5.850% coupon, due 2036, yield 6.139%, priced 130 basis points over US Treasuries.

— Who owes the money MercadoLibre, Inc., the Delaware parent, not an Argentine subsidiary.

— The other announcement A company study called Efecto MELI, presented on 14 September, claiming its Argentine operations add US$5.4 billion of value, about 1% of GDP.

— Whose numbers The company’s own. The study was commissioned and presented by MercadoLibre.

MercadoLibre borrowed a billion dollars at 6.1% in a week when US ten-year yields touched 5%.

MercadoLibre priced US$1 billion of 2036 notes on 11 September at 130 basis points over Treasuries.

MercadoLibre priced US$1 billion of 5.850% notes due 2036 on 11 September, settling on 14 September. The yield was 6.139%, a spread of 130 basis points over US Treasuries.

The Bond

The issue is US$1 billion of senior notes with a 5.850% coupon, maturing in 2036.

Pricing was on 11 September and settlement on 14 September, a standard three-day cycle.

The yield to investors is 6.139%, which is 130 basis points above the comparable Treasury.

The issuer is MercadoLibre, Inc., the Delaware-incorporated parent company.

Why 130 Basis Points Is the Number

A spread of 130 basis points over Treasuries is what an investment-grade American corporate borrower pays.

It is not what a Latin American issuer usually pays. Argentine sovereign debt trades at 485 basis points over.

MercadoLibre borrows as a United States company with revenue across the region. That, not its Argentine origin, sets the spread.

The timing was difficult. US ten-year yields touched 5.011% the following day, the highest since July 2007.

What MercadoLibre does. MercadoLibre, Inc. operates online commerce platforms in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, and internationally. The company operates Mercado Libre Marketplace, an online commerce platform that can be accessed through mobile app or website; and Mercado Pago, a financial technology solution platform, which offers comprehensive set of financial technology services to users and other users…

What the Money Is For

Ten-year money at a fixed coupon funds long-lived assets: warehouses, logistics networks and the lending book of Mercado Pago.

MercadoLibre has been building fulfilment capacity across Brazil, Mexico and Argentina at a pace that consumes cash faster than operations generate it.

Its credit business also requires funding, and funding it with ten-year debt rather than short-term borrowing reduces refinancing risk.

The company has not specified an allocation beyond general corporate purposes.

The Efecto MELI study claims 126,500 jobs in Argentina, direct and indirect.

The Argentina Study

On 14 September MercadoLibre presented a study it calls Efecto MELI, on its economic footprint in Argentina.

The headline claim is US$5.4 billion of added value, which the study puts at roughly 1% of Argentine GDP.

It also claims 126,500 jobs: 16,700 direct and 109,800 indirect.

These are the company’s own figures from its own commissioned study. They have not been independently verified, and indirect-employment multipliers are a contested methodology everywhere they are used.

Why the Company Publishes Numbers Like These

MercadoLibre was founded in Buenos Aires in 1999 and remains the largest private-sector technology employer in Argentina.

It is also a Delaware company listed on Nasdaq. Its relationship with the Argentine state is therefore negotiated, not owed.

Argentina is in the middle of a deregulation programme, and companies with a case to make are making it.

A study quantifying national contribution is an argument addressed to a government, published in the week its budget went to Congress.

Brazil is MercadoLibre’s largest market by revenue, followed by Mexico.

Where the Business Actually Is

Brazil is MercadoLibre’s largest market by revenue, followed by Mexico. Argentina is third.

The company reports in US dollars and has managed Argentine peso devaluation through pricing and local reinvestment.

Mercado Pago, its payments arm, has grown faster than the marketplace in recent years and now carries a substantial credit portfolio.

A comparison circulating this week between founder Marcos Galperín and Carlos Slim does not appear in the coverage of either announcement.

What to Watch

Where the notes trade after settlement, which shows whether the 130 basis point spread was correctly priced.

Third-quarter results, which will show whether the credit book is growing faster than provisions.

Argentine regulatory decisions on payments and credit, the area where the Efecto MELI argument is aimed.

And US Treasury yields, which set the cost of the company’s next issue.

What did MercadoLibre issue?

US$1 billion of 5.850% senior notes due 2036, priced on 11 September and settled on 14 September.

What was the yield?

6.139%, a spread of 130 basis points over comparable US Treasuries.

Who is the issuer?

MercadoLibre, Inc., the Delaware-incorporated parent, not an Argentine subsidiary.

What is Efecto MELI?

A study the company presented on 14 September claiming its Argentine operations add US$5.4 billion of value, about 1% of GDP.

Are those figures independent?

No. They come from MercadoLibre’s own commissioned study and have not been independently verified.

How many jobs does the study claim?

126,500 in total: 16,700 direct and 109,800 indirect.

World.title: Prosecutor Sues Vale and Regulators Over Mine Overflow
World.content:
BRAZIL · MINING

Key Facts — Who is Vale The world’s largest iron ore producer and one of Brazil’s biggest companies.

— What was filed A public civil action, the Brazilian instrument for suing on behalf of a collective interest, lodged on Wednesday 9 September.

— Who filed it Procurador Eduardo Henrique de Almeida Aguiar of the federal public prosecution service.

— Who is being sued Vale, the national mining agency ANM, and the Minas Gerais state government. All three are defendants.

— What it is about An overflow in January 2026 from two sumps at the Mina de Viga in Congonhas, Minas Gerais.

— What it asks for An independent audit of the site, paid for by Vale.

A prosecutor is suing Vale over a January overflow. He is also suing the two agencies that were meant to be watching.

A public civil action over a January overflow names Vale, the ANM and the Minas Gerais government.

A federal prosecutor filed a public civil action on 9 September. It concerns an overflow from two sumps at Vale’s Mina de Viga in Congonhas, Minas Gerais. Vale, the mining regulator ANM and the state government are all defendants.

What Happened at Mina de Viga

In January 2026, two sumps at the Mina de Viga overflowed. The Portuguese term is extravasamento.

A sump is a collection basin for water and sediment within a mine. It is not a tailings dam.

No dam ruptured at Viga. A containment overflow is not the kind of structural failure Brazil has seen twice in a decade.

Congonhas sits in the iron quadrangle of Minas Gerais, about 80 kilometres south of Belo Horizonte.

What the Action Asks

The filing seeks an independent audit of the site, commissioned from a third party and paid for by Vale.

It was lodged on Wednesday 9 September and reported on 14 September.

The procurador who filed it is Eduardo Henrique de Almeida Aguiar.

A public civil action in Brazil is brought on behalf of diffuse interests. That means environmental or collective harm, not one plaintiff’s loss.
