World.title: Iraq postpones start of 2026–2027 academic year to October 11
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Education announced on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, the postponement of the official start of the 2026–2027 academic year to Sunday, October 11, pushing back the previously scheduled launch date of September 20.

According to an official statement issued by the Media Office of the Minister of Education and carried by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Minister Abdul Karim Abtan Al-Jubouri issued the directive to grant administrative and teaching cadres the operational bandwidth needed to conclude second-round examination cycles for non-terminating grades and finalize campus preparations nationwide.

The ministerial directive also incorporated seasonal climate considerations, citing prevailing high temperatures across the country as a primary factor behind the delay to ensure student health and classroom safety.

Ministry officials underscored that the additional three-week window will be utilized to wrap up logistical, technical, and administrative arrangements, enabling local directorates across all governorates to complete physical facility upgrades and coordinate school readiness before millions of pupils and students officially resume classes across Iraq.

World.title: China CAMC Engineering to construct new airport in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Governor of Diwaniyah, Abbas al-Zamili, has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Chinese state-owned firm China CAMC Engineering to develop Diwaniyah International Airport.

The agreement includes the local company al-Balaghi as a joint partner in the project that will be constructed in the capital city of the south-central province of al-Qadisiyyah, located about 181 kilometers (112 miles) south of Baghdad.

The plan includes the construction of a complete civilian and commercial airport, as well as a specialized free trade zone in the province, to stimulate the local economy.

The airport is designed as an aviation hub to boost trade, logistics, and investment in south-central Iraq. It takes advantage of a recent increase in regional aviation traffic and the revenues generated from the growing number of flights.

This agreement expands Baghdad and Beijing’s existing “oil-for-projects” framework and larger infrastructure agreements. It builds on previous aviation initiatives in Iraq, such as the China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC) project at Nasiriyah International Airport.

The exact cost, capacity, and timeframe for development are expected to be determined in subsequent phases.

World.title: Integrity Chief, French agencies hold talks to recover stolen Iraqi assets
World.content:
Paris (IraqiNews.com) – The head of Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity, Mohammad Ali Al-Lami, held high-level discussions in Paris with senior French judicial and anti-corruption authorities on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, focusing on expanding direct bilateral mechanisms to extradite wanted fugitives and repatriate illicit Iraqi sovereign assets stashed abroad.

The meetings took place alongside the ongoing official government delegation visit to France led by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, aligning anti-corruption cooperation with broader diplomatic efforts to deepen Iraqi-French institutional partnerships.

During talks with the leadership of the French Anti-Corruption Agency (AFA), the Asset Recovery and Management Agency (AGRASC), and representatives from the French Ministry of Justice, Al-Lami emphasized that domestic legislative and regulatory oversight alone cannot counter the cross-border architecture of modern financial crime without proactive international cooperation.

He noted that tracking illicit wealth, executing freeze orders, and recovering state assets require streamlined mutual legal assistance requests, calling for direct channels to remove operational bottlenecks and accelerate judicial proceedings against convicted figures evading justice overseas.

Al-Lami stressed that repatriating stolen sovereign capital represents an economic imperative alongside a legal one, asserting that recovered funds will be channeled directly into vital national infrastructure, public service delivery, and sustainable development projects.

He added that restoring illicit assets and enforcing rigorous accountability are indispensable steps to establishing a secure, transparent business ecosystem capable of reassuring and attracting foreign investors. Pointing to Baghdad’s adherence to the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC), Al-Lami urged international partners to actively assist Iraq in tracing and returning funds held across foreign financial jurisdictions to the federal treasury.

The session concluded with both sides agreeing to formalize a comprehensive institutional agreement between Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity and the French Anti-Corruption Agency.

The prospective framework will focus on sharing French operational expertise in forensic financial investigations, corporate compliance, and risk assessments across both the public and private sectors, while establishing technical training pipelines to build the capacity of Iraqi investigative cadres and deploy advanced asset-tracing technologies.

World.title: Iraq, France sign agreements to enhance economic, defense capacities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and French President Emmanuel Macron sponsored on Monday a ceremony to sign six different memoranda of understanding at the Élysée Palace in Paris.

These agreements aim to boost Iraq’s economic, defense, and infrastructural capacities through strategic partnerships with France.

The accords overseen by the two leaders include air defense, military supply, energy supplies, civil aviation, development finance, and youth and innovation support.

Both countries reached two significant security agreements. The first is a letter of intent signed by the Iraqi Ministry of Defense and Harmattan AI for strategic air defense collaboration.

The second is a declaration of intent with the French Ministry of the Armed Forces to procure military equipment to assist Iraq in rebuilding its defensive capabilities.

The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and French energy giant TotalEnergies inked an important cooperation document involving a gas supply and sale deal. The agreement expands existing regional initiatives to recover associated gas for power plants.

The transportation ministries of both countries signed a declaration of intent to work directly on improving civil aviation operations.

The French and Iraqi foreign ministries signed a declaration of intent to deepen Iraq’s collaboration with the French Development Agency (AFD).

The final agreement establishes an official collaboration structure between the French and Iraqi foreign ministries to promote research, innovation, and professional prospects for young people.

World.title: Iraq reviews work with foreign banks, credit rating with Rothschild & Co.
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Edouard de Rothschild of Rothschild & Co. discussed on Monday cooperation with international banks and strategies to improve Iraq’s credit rating.

During their meeting in the French capital, Paris, the two sides discussed approaches to expand Iraq’s cooperation with foreign banks, as well as the Iraqi government’s efforts to develop the banking sector, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The discussions also focused on the Iraqi government’s objectives in building a strong and diversified economy.

Rothschild highlighted Iraq’s investment potential and the approaches in which foreign financial institutions might contribute to the country’s development objectives.

The prime minister’s meeting with Rothschild is part of his diplomatic agenda in Paris. Al-Zaidi also met with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace to discuss regional security and energy supply channels.

Al-Zaidi held a separate meeting with TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne to discuss a multibillion-dollar expansion of Iraq’s oil and gas production capability.

Following his trip to France, the Iraqi prime minister is planned to fly to the German capital, Berlin, to continue his European tour.

World.title: Three talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix
World.content:
Madrid – Eight wins, the most by an Italian driver in a single season, and blessed with good fortune as well as extreme talent, it is no longer a question of if Kimi Antonelli will win the drivers’ world championship, but when?

In a season of uncertain length, with the final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remaining in doubt, there are various permutations in terms of the points likely to be required for an unassailable advantage.

As Antonelli closes in on becoming Italy’s first champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, AFP Sport looks at three talking points from Sunday’s processional Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit:

More records ready to be broken by Antonelli

The 20-year-old prodigy from Bologna already has a lead of 81 points ahead of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who has abandoned talking of his own title bid.

If the season includes a two-race finale in the Middle East, where the US-Israeli war with Iran makes this doubtful, he will need 153 points, from the 233 available, to become champion.

A total of 152 might be enough, thanks to his tie-breaking supremacy in number of race wins -– offering up the prospect of Antonelli taking his maiden title in Singapore next month.

But if the season is reduced from 23 races to 22 with a final race taking place at Imola, close to Antonelli’s home town, on December 6, a reduced maximum of 208 points will be on offer and the target falls to 127 –- which may be achievable in Mexico on November 1.

If he succeeded in Mexico, he would take the title aged 20 years, two months and eight days — thus reducing the record for youngest world champion held by four-time champion Sebastian Vettel by three years.

Norris’s bad luck with safety rules

World champion Lando Norris described himself as “insanely unlucky” not to win Sunday’s race as a result of the timing of a Virtual Safety Car (VSC) that was called seconds after he passed the pit lane entry.

It cost him a “cheap” pit stop and handed the initiative to his rivals, Charles Leclerc of Ferrari and Antonelli, who waited for the Monegasque driver to make his essential pit-stop before seizing victory with aplomb.

Antonelli and others pitted during the VSC, saving time and gaining an approximate 20-seconds advantage on Norris who had to fight back from fifth to finish third behind four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull.

It was clearly unfair on Norris to be penalised for being the fastest driver on track and leading at the time when Lance Stroll lost control of his Aston Martin and went into the barriers.

“It is a rule that should not define a whole race,” said Norris. “I was the only one on the whole grid that didn’t get the chance to do the pit stop.”

His McLaren team boss Andrea Stella said: “Perhaps there’s a wider reflection that the F1 community should apply, as to whether you keep things like they are — or you introduce ways of maintaining more fairness.”

Honda make changes

Fernando Alonso was more than two seconds off the pace when he was eliminated from qualifying at his home race on Saturday, a clear sign his Honda-powered Aston Martin was lacking power.

As the two-time world champion publicly ponders his future, Honda announced a change of leadership for their engine programme. It may, however, be too late to persuade Alonso to stay for another year.

World.title: Germany seeks guarantees from Italy’s UniCredit over Commerzbank takeover
World.content:
Frankfurt – Germany’s finance minister was due on Monday to meet the UniCredit CEO to seek guarantees over the future of Commerzbank, as the Italian lender gears up to complete a takeover of its German rival.

Lars Klingbeil would urge UniCredit boss Andrea Orcel to protect jobs in Germany and ensure Commerzbank remains a key lender to the country’s small- and medium-sized businesses, Berlin said.

Despite fierce resistance from Berlin and the German lender, UniCredit has built up a stake of nearly 50 percent in Commerzbank and is close to sealing one of Europe’s biggest banking mergers in recent years.

A German finance ministry spokesman conceded the banks had moved into a “a different phase now” and were negotiating a transaction.

But he stressed Klingbeil wanted to ensure Commerzbank’s interests and the country’s were protected during the talks in Berlin.

“Commerzbank has over 40,000 employees and we naturally want to safeguard their interests,” he told a press conference.

Commerzbank’s “core business model” in financing Germany’s small businesses, which form the backbone of Europe’s biggest economy, should be preserved too, he said.

It was also key that Commerzbank’s main operations remained in Frankfurt to ensure the city continued as “one of the most important financial centres in Europe,” the spokesman said.

– Banking behemoth –

Berlin still believes it has some influence over the deal through its representation on Commerzbank’s supervisory board and its roughly 12-percent stake in the bank, both legacies of a state bailout during the financial crisis.

But its leverage is now likely to be diminished given the size of UniCredit’s stake.

UniCredit started building up its holding in Commerzbank in 2024 in a bid to launch a takeover.

Commerzbank slashed thousands of jobs and hiked its financial targets in an effort to convince shareholders to back its campaign to remain independent.

But these efforts failed and, with UniCredit closing in on a controlling stake, Commerzbank’s CEO Bettina Orlopp called in late July for “constructive” talks with the Italian lender.

UniCredit wants to create a European banking behemoth better able to take on bigger US rivals and argues that a merger would strengthen the region’s fragmented banking sector.

Despite resistance in Germany, some policymakers in Brussels and at the European Central Bank have been more supportive of a possible takeover.

World.title: Saudi football body vows action against Jota chants, Ronaldo urges life ban
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabian football authorities promised to take action and Cristiano Ronaldo called for life bans after rival fans taunted Al-Hilal’s Ruben Neves about the death of Diogo Jota, his friend and former Portugal team-mate.

Chants about Jota, the Liverpool and Portugal forward who died in a car crash last year, rang out during Al-Hilal’s 6-0 away win over Al-Taawoun on Saturday.

“The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” Saudi-based Portugal captain Ronaldo wrote on Instagram on Sunday.

“People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again,” he added.

Midfielder Neves, 29, reacted to the chants coming from the stands by sarcastically giving a thumbs-up and applauding, before pointing towards the sky.

“I just hope they don’t go to pray later after what they did,” he said after the match.

Neves was one of Jota’s closest friends and was a pallbearer at his funeral. Jota, 28, and his brother Andre, 25, died in a crash in Spain in July 2025.

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation and Saudi Pro League condemned “unacceptable conduct by some supporters” in a joint statement late on Sunday.

“Exploiting personal tragedies for the purpose of abuse or provocation is unacceptable behaviour that has no place in Saudi football,” the statement said.

“Relevant committees have identified the conduct in question and will take the necessary action in accordance with the applicable regulations and procedures,” it added.

Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup, one of the flagship events underpinning its drive to diversify an economy still heavily dependent on oil.

The powerful Gulf monarchy has invested nearly two billion dollars in football over three years, attracting stars such as Ronaldo, Neymar and Karim Benzema.

World.title: The engineers India trains, the infrastructure it still can't build
World.content:
Every June, before the monsoon fully sets in, a familiar sequence plays out across Indian cities. Mumbai's suburban trains stall in ankle-deep water. Bengaluru's tech corridors flood after a single evening's rain.

Delhi's underpasses fill up fast enough to trap cars. None of this is new, and none of it, by now, is unpredictable. What is harder to explain is why a country that trains more engineers than almost anywhere else on earth keeps failing at the most basic engineering problem a city faces: keeping water out and heat down.

Waterlogging in Delhi

India's technical education system is producing at record scale. AICTE data shows 12.53 lakh BTech seats were filled in the 2024-25 academic session, an eight-year high and a 67 percent increase over 2017-18.

But that surge is concentrated in one discipline. Computer science and engineering leads enrolment at 3,90,245 students, followed by mechanical engineering, civil engineering at 1,72,936, electronics and communication, and electrical engineering.

Civil engineering, the discipline that actually builds and maintains drains, embankments and disaster-resilient housing, trails computer science by more than two to one at the point of enrolment itself, before a single graduate has even entered the job market.





Where the engineers actually go

The surplus is real, but it isn't evenly distributed across the problems India needs solved. Computer science and IT graduates are pulled toward software, finance and consulting at a pace and pay scale that civic engineering roles, largely government postings with slower promotion cycles and lower starting salaries, cannot match. The result is a lopsided allocation: a country producing engineering talent at record volume, with that volume skewed away from the disciplines that keep cities functioning, and further skewed again once graduates choose where to build a career.

India's engineer surplus ends before it reaches the drains

This isn't a story about a shortage of trained people. It's a story about where trained people end up, and about how thin institutional capacity is on the other side of that choice, inside the departments actually responsible for stormwater drains, building safety audits and urban planning.

The departments meant to absorb them are understaffed by design

The gap shows up starkly inside Urban Local Bodies, the municipal corporations and councils responsible for drainage, building approvals and disaster preparedness.

A compendium of CAG performance audits covering 393 urban local bodies across 18 states, released in 2025, found a 42 percent gap between the revenue resources and actual expenditure of ULBs, with just 32 percent of ULB revenue self-generated and the rest arriving as grants from state and central governments.

In Karnataka, government data reviewed this year showed close to 60 percent of sanctioned ULB posts vacant across ten city corporations, prompting the state to permit hiring retired engineers just to keep basic project planning functioning.

Building codes compound the problem. The National Building Code, published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, is only a recommendatory document, not a binding law, so states can adopt, adapt or largely ignore its provisions. Maharashtra's own regulations don't even apply uniformly within the state: the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations explicitly exclude the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai and other planning authorities within its limits, leaving the city to run on a separate rulebook altogether.

Drainage systems in most major cities were designed decades ago and were never built for the rainfall intensities cities now regularly see. On June 28, 2024, Delhi's Safdarjung Observatory recorded 228.1 mm of rainfall in 24 hours â more than three times the June average and the highest for the month in 88 years, since 1936, according to the India Meteorological Department. The waterlogging and traffic disruption that followed looked no different from floods a decade earlier.

What a new industrial corridor risks repeating

This matters beyond the annual monsoon cycle because India is now committing serious capital to exactly the kind of large-scale infrastructure build-out that depends on this workforce functioning well. The East Coast Industrial Corridor, pegged to the Union Budget 2026-27's announcement of a Durgapur-anchored industrial belt spanning ports, manufacturing zones and logistics networks across Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, is one of several major infrastructure pushes riding on the assumption that India's technical capacity can execute at scale.

But the same staffing vacancies, advisory-only codes and enforcement gaps that produce annual urban flooding sit underneath these new projects too. A corridor is, in the end, drainage, ports, road networks and disaster-resilient construction multiplied across four states; the same civic engineering functions currently understaffed in every city that already exists.

India's next industrial boom to happen on the East Coast

The heat side of the problem makes the stakes clearer still.

India's peak power demand climbed from 214.9 GW on April 1 to a record 270.8 GW on May 21, 2026, according to the Union Ministry of Power, a 26 percent jump in fifty days, driven by sustained heat. That's a building-design and urban-planning failure as much as a climate one: cool roofs, passive ventilation and heat-resilient construction are still treated as add-ons rather than baseline requirements in most bye-laws.

A multi-city study analysing roughly 3.6 million deaths across ten Indian cities between 2008 and 2019 found that heatwave days were associated with a 14.7 percent increase in daily mortality, and estimated around 1,116 deaths a year attributable to heatwaves. The 2025 Report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change estimated that India lost about 247 billion labour hours to heat exposure in 2024, translating to roughly $194 billion in economic losses, concentrated in agriculture and construction.

None of this points to a talent problem. India has the engineers, more of them, and more concentrated in one discipline, than ever before. What it doesn't have, consistently, is a civic system built to employ the rest where the predictable failures actually happen, inside municipal drainage departments, building-approval desks and disaster-management cells that are short-staffed and underfunded by a documented, audited margin.

Every large infrastructure announcement adds new physical assets to maintain. Unless the capacity gap inside the institutions responsible for maintaining them closes at the same pace, each new corridor, each new industrial belt, inherits the same vulnerability the rest of urban India already lives with every monsoon and every summer.

World.title: Gurgaon hit-and-run case: Accused Kalyan Bainsla made to kneel before car, bandaged hand visible - watch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A video showing Kalyan Bainsla, the car driver accused of hitting a woman biker, kneeling before his vehicle with a bandage on his hand surfaced on Tuesday.

This comes as police arrested Bainsla from Rajgarh in Rajasthan, two days after his speeding Ciaz allegedly rammed into the womanâs Aprilia RS 457, causing her to skid across the road, police said.

Gurgaon DCP Sandeep Kumar said on Tuesday that the accused car driver allegedly intended to kill the woman biker he rammed into on Golf Course Road. Police arrested the driver and his cousin in connection with the case.

Police arrested Bainsla and his cousin, Lavish, after tracing them to Rajasthan.

The DCP said attempt-to-murder charges were added based on the victimâs statement and CCTV footage, which allegedly showed Bainsla deliberately ramming his car into the womanâs bike, indicating an alleged attempt to kill her.

Police also invoked Sections 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), he said. According to the DCP, Bainsla had borrowed the car from a friend and allegedly used it in the incident. Police said he runs gyms in Palwal.

After giving a statement to the media, Bainsla fled to Rajasthan, where he and his cousin, Lavish, were later arrested, police said.

World.title: ‘Not everyone in NDA agrees’: Omar Abdullah questions Centre’s UCC plan amid JD(U)'s opposition
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jammu & Kashmir chief minister

on Tuesday questioned the Centreâs plan to implement the

(UCC) in all 21 BJP-led NDA-ruled states before 2029, citing the Janata Dal (United)âs opposition to implementing the law in Bihar and questioning whether the government can secure the numbers to pass it in Parliament.

Abdullahâs remarks came a day after JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak said the party was opposed to implementing the UCC in Bihar, despite supporting the UCC Bill in Parliament. The JD(U), which has 12 Lok Sabha MPs, is a key

ally and shares power with the

BJP

in Bihar.

Speaking to reporters in Srinagar, Abdullah also questioned the state-wise rollout of the UCC, arguing that civil legislation should be dealt with by Parliament.

"In this regard, the National Conference has issued its statement.

Our Rajya Sabha MP Shammi Oberoi has said that it is Parliament's job to do this. Why are you doing it from different states? Not everyone in their NDA agrees with this. JDU has straight-up raised its hands and said it won't be implemented in Bihar. If their own people aren't ready for UCC, how can these people say that it should be implemented across the entire country? I don't think these people will be able to pass it in Parliament," Abdullah said.





Rajak said on Monday that the partyâs position on implementing the UCC in Bihar remained unchanged, despite its support for the legislation in Parliament.

"Our stand on the issue was made clear by our leader way back. He had said that although our party was supporting the UCC Bill in the Parliament, it was not in favour of implementing the same in Bihar," Rajak said.

Rejecting suggestions that the partyâs position could change after BJP leader Samrat Choudhary became Bihar chief minister, Rajak said the state government depended on its allies.

"The chief minister may be of the BJP but the government is being run with the help of allies... our stand is clear, the question of implementing UCC in Bihar does not arise," he said.

JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha said the party would soon meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the implementation of the UCC in states.

âWe will soon meet Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the issue,â Jha told PTI.

JD(U) legislature party leader and minister Shrawon Kumar, meanwhile, said the party's spokespersons would comment on the issue.

The JD(U) position came a day after Shah said NDA governments in 21 states would introduce the UCC before 2029.

Addressing a press conference in Mumbai on Sunday, Shah said the government had already introduced the UCC in several states and expressed confidence that it would be extended to all 21 BJP-NDA ruled states before 2029.

"We introduced the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in several states. I am confident that we will implement the UCC in all 21 states governed by the BJP-led NDA before 2029.

Operations such as the surgical strikes, air strikes, and Operation Sindoor have established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, while security has been prioritised across various sectors," Shah said.

Abdullah also welcomed the mention and condemnation of the Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics New Delhi Declaration, calling it a success for India's foreign policy.

"That is something for the government of India, and particularly for the foreign ministry, to talk about.

The fact that Pahalgam itself was condemned is a big thing. Please see how many allies of Pakistan were in that room. Therefore, for even Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy," Abdullah remarked.

"Anything that reduces tension along the Line of Control or the Line of Actual Control is a good step, particularly for those people who live close to it. World.title: 'See how many allies of Pakistan were in that room': Omar Abdullah praises Centre over Pahalgam condemnation at Brics
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief minister

on Tuesday heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre and recently held

in Delhi. Omar Abdullah said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed

Pahalgam terror attack

was a major diplomatic win.

J&K CM remarks came after India hosted the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, bringing together several world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The National Conference leader particularly highlighted the inclusion of the Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics New Delhi Declaration, pointing out that the statement came in the presence of countries that share close ties with Pakistan.

"That is something for the Government of India, and particularly for the foreign ministry, to talk about. The fact that Pahalgam itself was condemned is a big thing. Please see how many allies of Pakistan were in that room. Therefore, for even Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy," Omar Abdullah said.

J&K CM Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along Indiaâs fronts with Pakistan and China.





Reacting to the ministry of defenceâs report on the operational situation along the Northern Front, he said any move to reduce troop deployments along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) or Line of Control (LoC) would be a positive development, particularly for people living in border areas.

"Anything that reduces tension along the Line of Control or the Line of Actual Control is a good step, particularly for those people who live close to it.

We know that living near the LoC or LAC is extremely difficult for people. If there is any step that reduces deployments along the Line of Actual Control, that is a good step. Similarly, we hope that, over time, things will also get better along the Line of Control," he added.

The comments came days after the Brics Summit concluded in the national capital. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the New Delhi Declaration had been unanimously adopted and called the gathering as a huge summit.

Days ago, senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor backed the Brics Summit as an important diplomatic opportunity for India, appearing to differ with party colleague P Chidambaram, who questioned whether recent Brics meetings have produced tangible benefits.

World.title: ‘Public will back BJP again’: CM Adhikari predicts 50,000 margin win in Bengal's Nandigram
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday claimed that the BJP would win the upcoming Nandigram assembly bypoll by more than 50,000 votes, saying voters had already expressed their faith in the party and him.

"We will win the by-election by over 50,000 votes. The public had voted for the BJP and me, but as per the Constitution, I cannot hold two seats, so I had to leave one," Adhikari said.

The Nandigram bypoll was necessitated after Adhikari vacated the seat and chose to retain Bhabanipur, where he defeated TMC chief Mamata Banerjee in the assembly elections held earlier this year.

'I have responsibility for Nandigram'

Adhikari said he continued to have a responsibility towards Nandigram and cited development work carried out by the BJP government as a reason for expecting voters to back the party again.

"I have responsibility for the Nandigram seat. The way development work has been done by the BJP government, we will again see the public express its faith in the BJP," he said.

TMC names candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar

The Trinamool Congress faction led by Mamata Banerjee on Sunday announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) as its candidate for Nandigram and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury for Rejinagar. The bypolls are scheduled for October 6, with counting of votes on October 9.

Pradhan is a new face, while Chowdhury is a former MLA, PTI reported.

The announcement came after an earlier rebel TMC faction said it would support Mamata Banerjee, potentially strengthening the party's position ahead of the bypolls.

World.title: CJP protest assault case: 'Influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj gets 3-week interim bail
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Tuesday granted Swatantra Bhardwaj interim bail for three weeks in connection with the alleged assault of the father of a Dalit student-activist during a protest at Jantar Mantar.

Bhardwaj is facing charges in connection with the alleged assault during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar in June. He was arrested in Uttar Pradesh on September 5 and has been in judicial custody.

The court's interim bail order comes a day after Bhardwaj's counsel argued that his arrest was politically motivated and claimed that the complainant had attacked Bhardwaj during the incident.

During Monday's hearing, advocate Umesh Sharma told the court that a video purportedly showed the complainant attacking Bhardwaj.

"Police ko wo video nazar nahi aa raha... Is video m clearly dikhai de raha hai ki complainant is mujhpe attack kiya hai aur main gir gaya hu (The police are not able to see that video. It is clearly visible in this video that the complainant attacked me and I fell down)," Sharma told the court.





Sharma also alleged that Bhardwaj was arrested under the SC/ST Act for political reasons. He said Bhardwaj had initially received a police notice to appear for questioning on June 27 and appeared before investigators on June 29, after which he was allowed to leave.

"The police issued me a notice on June 27 to appear for questioning, and I appeared for questioning on June 29. After that, I was allowed to go. Then, after some political developments, I was arrested on September 4.

After my arrest, a new FIR [under POCSO] was registered," Sharma said.

Advocate Swati Khanna, appearing for the complainant, opposed the bail plea and alleged that Bhardwaj had used casteist slurs against the complainant. She also claimed that Bhardwaj had admitted in a video that he was the one who attacked the complainant.

Delhi Police told the court that the original complaint did not mention any casteist slur.

However, a casteist slur was included in a subsequent statement, following which provisions of the SC/ST Act were added.

Khanna also informed the court that Bhardwaj had approached the Delhi high court with a habeas corpus plea challenging his arrest, but the plea was rejected.

World.title: Technical education must keep pace with emerging technologies: expert
World.content:
Technical education should keep pace with rapid technological advancements, while students should focus on innovation and continuously upgrade their skills, said Aravapalli Srinivas, CEO of Bluebinaries Engineering.

Addressing an Engineers’ Day programme at Siddhartha Deemed University, Kanuru, on Tuesday to mark the 165th birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya, Mr. Srinivas stressed the importance of technical education, innovation and emerging technologies in the development of the nation.

Siddhartha Academy president Mallineni Rajayya and secretary Paladugu Lakshmana Rao urged students to make effective use of technological advancements and strive for excellence.

Head of the Department of Mechanical Engineering Narra Ravi Kumar said technology was advancing rapidly and called upon students to actively participate in technical activities and keep abreast of emerging technologies.

Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao and Pro-Vice-Chancellor A.V. Ratna Prasad felicitated the chief guest. University Registrar M. Ravichand advised students to cultivate innovative thinking, strengthen their technical skills and bring recognition to the institution through their achievements.

As part of the celebrations, students displayed innovative models and projects developed by them. Prizes were presented to the winners by the heads of various departments in recognition of their performance.

World.title: BJP names mother of slain Suvendu aide as Nandigram by-poll candidate
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) nominated Hasirani Rath as party candidate for Nandigram Assembly byelection. Ms. Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, former personal assistant of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari who was killed in May 6 2026.

Ms. Rath will file her nomination to contest the polls on September 15, and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari is likely to be present during the event. Chandranath Rath was shot inside his vehicle in Madhyamgram in Kolkata around 10 p.m. on May 6. The CBI had filed a chargesheet before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate’s court in Barasat on August 7, which names 12 accused.

The byelection at Nandigram is being held because Mr. Adhikari relinquished the seat after getting elected from Bhabanipur and Nandigram both during the 2026 Assembly polls. The byelection is a prestige battle for the BJP particularly the Chief Minister who had represented the seat from 2021-26, when he was Leader of the Opposition.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari joined the rally of submission of nomination papers of Hasirani Rath and walked along with party workers to the Sub- Divisional Officer (SDO)’s office for over a kilometer long strech.

Addresing a gathering after the nomination, Mr. Adhikari exuded confidence by saying that the BJP will win by “such a big margin in Nandigram that no one has ever imagined”. He said that the biggest sin of Chandranath Rath was that he was aide of the Leader of Opposition and promised that he will fulfill all the promises made to the people of Nandigram.

Mr. Adhikari had defeated former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee from Nandigram by a margin of 1956 votes in 2021 and in 2026 his margin over the Trinamool Congress candidate was 9,665 votes.

Both Nandigram and Rejinagar where by-polls are held have a significant Muslim population and the Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari in his speech said that that October 6 was a test of minority electorate.

“October 6 will be your test of whether you want to be with the government and the Chief Minister and work hand-in-hand. I leave it to you whether you want to pass or fail in the test,” Mr. Adhikari said.

The BJP has nominated Sakharav Sarkar from Rejinagar where by-polls will be held with Nandigram on October 6. The Mamata Banerjee led faction of Trinamool Congress has fielded Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) from Nandigram and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury from Rejinagar seat. The other Trinamool faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee has fielded Mohammad Eteshamul Haque from Nandigram and Safiuzzaman from Rejinagar in Murshidabad.

Both the factions of Trinamool have sought the grass and twin flowers symbol of the party and have approached Election Commission for this.

The CPI(M)-led Left Front has nominated Sayeed Asad Aliu from Rejinagar and Shanti Gopal Giri from Nandigram. The Congress has nominated Mohd Abdullahil Kafi from Rejinagar and Milan Pradhan from Nandigram.

The byelection at Rejinagar is being held following the decision of Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) leader Humayun Kabir to vacate the seat. Mr. Kabir, who had won from both Naoda and Rejinagar, decided to give up Rejinagar. His son Golam Nabi Azad is the AJUP candidate from Rejinagar.

With every faction now announcing candidates, the stage is set for an electoral contest on two seats – Nandigram, located in Purba Medinipur district and Rejinagar in Murshidabad district. The counting of votes will be held on October 9.

World.title: Mettur dam level stands at 87.82 feet
World.content:
The water level in the Stanley Reservoir in Mettur stood at 87.82 feet, against its full reservoir level (FRL) of 120 feet, at 8 a.m. on Tuesday (September 15, 2026).

According to Water Resources Department officials, the storage was 50.19 tmcft, against the reservoir’s full capacity of 93.47 tmcft. The inflow was 7,599 cusecs, while 12,000 cusecs was released into the Cauvery for delta irrigation and 400 cusecs through the canal. The reservoir received 5.6 mm of rainfall.

Meanwhile, the water level in the Bhavanisagar Dam in Erode district stood at 53.06 feet, against its FRL of 105 feet. At 8 a.m., the storage was 5.20 tmcft, against the dam’s total capacity of 32.80 tmcft, accounting for 15.88% of its storage capacity. The 24-hour average inflow was 299 cusecs, while the current inflow was 711 cusecs. The total outflow was 105 cusecs.

World.title: Lokesh to inaugurate renovated government school in Nellore on September 16
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh IT and Education Minister Nara Lokesh will inaugurate the Devireddy Sarada Government High School, which was renovated by Hyderabad-based real estate company DSR Group using its CSR funds of ₹13.40 crore, at Mulapet in Nellore on Wednesday (September 16).

The school, which had once fallen into a dilapidated state, has now been transformed into a modern institution. From classrooms and laboratories to sports grounds and a library, it has been transformed into a premier centre of learning, equipped with international-standard facilities essential for students.

Municipal Administration and Urban Planning (MA&UD) Minister Ponguru Narayana had earlier initiated the modernisation of government schools in the city by upgrading VRC Government High School at Chinna Bazar to international standards. In the same spirit, he initiated measures to revamp the girls’ high school in Mulapet with modern amenities.

Through the Minister’s initiative, DSR Group managing director Devireddy Sudhakar Reddy contributed ₹13.40 crore to rebuild the school, which has been renamed Devireddy Sarada Government High School.

Twenty-four classrooms have been constructed across two floors, covering an area of ​​approximately 24,000 square feet. To facilitate modern teaching methods, 15 LED screens and 300 benches have been installed in the school. Specialised laboratories have been set up in the school to meet contemporary educational needs, while labs dedicated to computers, robotics, astronomy, physics, chemistry, and biology will serve as platforms for hands-on learning.

Additionally, special facilities such as art, music, and language rooms, along with store, library and modern toilets have been provided. Courts for basketball, pickleball, volleyball, kabaddi, and kho-kho have been arranged for holistic development of the students.

“We are committed to upgrading government schools in the city to international standards. We are moving forward with the goal of modernising 15 government schools and providing quality education to 15,000 poor students,” Mr. Narayana said.

“Driven by the conviction that no student should miss out on opportunities due to poverty, this initiative aims at providing essential infrastructure, modern education, sports facilities, and access to technology in government schools,” the Minister added.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Saudi Arabia warns it will react 'firmly' to Houthi attacks
World.content:
Saudi Arabia warned Tuesday (September 15, 2026) it will react “firmly” to Yemen’s Houthis, after a series of attacks carried out by the pro-Iranian rebels using ballistic missiles and drones wounded 13 civilians in the country’s south.

The Houthis have been engaged in renewed fighting with Saudi-backed government forces since Yemen’s civil war reignited in July, when the group declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea. The group seized control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait last week, which has become vital as the wider U.S.-Iran war chokes the Strait of Hormuz, in a significant blow to Yemeni government forces.
